themes.title: Keep the machine up and the work safe
themes.covers: The one PC: power-offs, restarts, resuming after a stop, off-machine copies, memory, Docker and disk, and keeping secrets out of agents’ reach.
intro: Everything we build runs on one PC. Between 7 October and 10 November it powered off unexpectedly 24 times [M]. Of the 25 power-offs since 1 October, 15 [M] came with no Claude call in any project in the ten minutes before, so our own load alone does not explain them. The clinic testbed still lives only on this machine.

The ideas here keep work safe when the PC stops and bring it back without me: an off-machine copy, a resume list that brings sessions back two at a time, and an always-on sensor logger that will show why it powers off. Separate worktrees already pay: when the power went for 28 minutes on 13 November, all eight FixFlow lanes resumed from their own copies [M]. This theme is harness v2 phase 1, and I answered its first six decisions on 11 November; a full restart chain waits, because I chose to keep Docker’s start at sign-in off for now (D03).

ideas.name: Checkpoint and resume by dependency hash
ideas.how: A stdlib Python tool hashes the task file, a context packet and chosen source files; resume re-hashes and lists changed or deleted dependencies.
ideas.problem: After a stop, an agent cannot tell which files it relied on have changed, so it trusts a stale handoff or re-reads everything.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: stale dependency rejected, fresh and unrelated changes accepted; 29 behaviour tests pass [M]. Eight red-team defects still open [M]; whole-file granularity.
ideas.next: Fix the open red-team defects, including 'verify passes when every test is skipped'; list only changed docs on resume.

ideas.name: Resume-safe long runs and sleep prevention
ideas.how: Save run state around each step with a continue entry; keep the PC awake during runs; check long log gaps against sleep records.
ideas.problem: A Windows sleep or a usage-limit stop in mid-run produced false timeouts and lost progress.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed drivers: wall time 16,888.984 s [M] vs 2,661.859 s awake [M]; sleep gap 14,227.125 s [M]. Two arms hit the account limit mid-compaction and resumed in-session [M].
ideas.next: Check sleep and wake records before blaming the agent or network for a stall.

ideas.name: Files-first outputs and resume-from-disk rules
ideas.how: Agents write outputs to files; a state file makes resume from disk idempotent; model-written summaries are re-verified.
ideas.problem: Session limits stopped lane agents, a resumed workflow re-ran agents that had already edited files, and summaries drifted from the sources.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: rules after the incidents; recovery manual. Six interruptions [M]; six of eight lanes stopped in run 1 [M]; 133 queries of aborted agents recovered from transcripts [M].
ideas.next: Write agent outputs to files and resume from disk state.

ideas.name: Parked starts released later by message
ideas.how: On my turn, pre-create dependent sessions with a parked-start brief; release each later by message when a dependency merges.
ideas.problem: New sessions can start only on a turn I begin, so work stops while I am away; messages reach a busy lane only at turn end.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: used 6 Nov for three parked sessions [M]; it did not prevent the 6 to 9 Nov halt. Releasing all at once on 9 Nov caused a 2,030 s [M] queue.
ideas.next: Keep it; release two sessions at a time, aiming at idle under three hours [T].

ideas.name: Dead locks after a boot; commit and push at every green checkpoint
ideas.how: Locks older than the last boot are dead. Lanes commit and push at each green checkpoint; the coordinator restarts Docker, then wakes each lane.
ideas.problem: The PC lost power for 28 minutes [M] on 13 November and cut off eight [M] lanes. We want stale locks never to block the lanes afterwards.
ideas.stands: In use: implemented in the slot and gate scripts after the event. After the 28-minute [M] outage, all eight [M] lanes resumed from their worktrees.
ideas.next: Add off-machine copies of unpushed work (suggested; not yet decided). That could make longer outages safe too.

ideas.name: Shared-machine etiquette and session ceiling
ideas.how: FixFlow sessions remove only fixflow-* containers, never restart Docker or WSL, never prune networks, and swap shared scripts atomically. Eight [S] sessions at most.
ideas.problem: Another project's containers share this PC, so touching Docker could break them, and too many sessions would use up the memory.
ideas.stands: In force (rated adopt). With eight lane sessions, 5.5 to 7.7 GB [M] was free of 31 GB [M], and commit was 35 to 41.5 GB [M] of 50.1 GB [M].
ideas.next: Raise the ceiling only after memory is measured free; lower it to about six [S] sessions when memory is tight.

ideas.name: Leave the antivirus alone; unpack from official archives
ideas.how: Unpack from Google's named archives, verify every file's name and size, leave the blocked DLL absent, and use host or software GPU mode.
ideas.problem: The antivirus scanner blocks one emulator file, which makes Google's package tool abandon the package. We want the lab to work without changing any antivirus setting.
ideas.stands: In use: all installed files match the official archives except the one blocked DLL [M]. FixFlow never changes an antivirus setting.
ideas.next: Keep using it. I may allow the Android folder later; it is not needed today.

ideas.name: Windows-host traps recorded as lessons
ideas.how: Each trap is a written lesson: grep -c on carriage returns lies, Python writes CRLF, heredoc EOF failures, shared temp logs, Hyper-V gotchas.
ideas.problem: Windows shell quirks gave us false passes and extra rounds, and we want each one to be known before an agent hits it.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed as notes only; no check enforces them. One rerun cost a 16-minute [M] check; each Hyper-V trap cost 10 to 40 minutes [M].
ideas.next: Write logs to the scratchpad and check line endings with git ls-files --eol; turning notes into checks could unlock more.

ideas.name: Concurrency cap and load rules after two shutdowns
ideas.how: At most three or four children and one full check at a time, enforced by a lock; slots replaced the lock on 6 Nov.
ideas.problem: The PC shut down uncleanly on 5 and 6 November under concurrent full test runs, two of the 24 [M] power-offs we later counted; the cause is still open.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed as a mitigation, not a diagnosis; cause never found. Free memory 0.0-0.8 GiB at lows with two checks beside six sessions, 2-6 GiB with one [M].
ideas.next: For FixFlow on the same PC, add a memory-aware slot gate and sample CPU and free memory every second.

ideas.name: Memory headroom guard on the second check slot
ideas.how: The second slot opens only while 8.0 GiB of physical memory is free, re-read at every poll; unreadable means closed.
ideas.problem: Two simultaneous checks drove free memory to 0.0-0.8 GB [M], the suspected cause of unclean shutdowns.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed but collapses to one slot: in about 980 samples [M], 8 GiB [S] was never free (2.1-6.2 GiB [M]). Waits 647, 3, 256, 614 s [M].
ideas.next: Measure the per-check memory footprint first; a guard on idle-session or container count may matter more than free RAM.

ideas.name: Drop Docker's page cache after each backend run
ideas.how: The gate script runs a privileged container that drops the page cache at the start and end of every backend run; no data touched.
ideas.problem: The Docker virtual machine hoards disk cache it is not using, starving Windows of RAM while lanes run.
ideas.stands: In use in the gate script. The first drop gave back 2.2 GB [M]; the VM held 8.3 GB [M], 4.4 GB [M] of it unused cache.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Write scripts with the file tool; give Workflows paths
ideas.how: Write every script with the file-writing tool, and give Workflow scripts file paths so agents read the content themselves.
ideas.problem: The shell tool collapses doubled backslashes in heredocs, which altered two regular expressions, and Workflow scripts cannot read files.
ideas.stands: In use, adopted from the review addendum. Before the fix, the first attempt of one review run cost 1.38M tokens [M] and 15 minutes [M].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Shutdown diagnosis and always-on sensor logger
ideas.how: Join shutdown times to commit and Claude logs; run an always-on temperature, power and memory logger; decode the 7 October dump; note mains cuts.
ideas.problem: The PC switched itself off unexpectedly about two dozen times [M] since early October and we do not know why; agent work stops without warning.
ideas.stands: Join done (harness v2 phase 1): 25 shutdowns since 1 October [M], 24 of them between 7 October and 10 November; 15 had no Claude call in the ten minutes before [M]. Logger and debugger allowed, not yet installed; cause not found.
ideas.next: Install the logger and debugger; I supply the days the house lost power. The next shutdown then has a trace.

ideas.name: One Linux image for every engine arm
ideas.how: A 1.26 GB [M] Docker image holds both graph engines, their algorithm libraries and the runner, and is rebuilt from a Dockerfile recipe.
ideas.problem: A Windows build would have handicapped one graph engine, whose algorithm extension would not load. We want every arm on identical footing.
ideas.stands: Built and used in the graph test. PageRank, Louvain, connected components and k-core (see Connected components / k-core) ran natively and PageRank matched DuckDB [M]. Docker had to be restarted twice; the image stayed intact.
ideas.next: Keep the recipe with the evidence so the test can be rebuilt.
ideas.origin: Graph test (I chose Linux over a handicap)

ideas.name: Never let the PC sleep on mains power
ideas.how: Set Windows sleep when plugged in to Never, so a sleeping or idle-hung PC cannot cut agent sessions off.
ideas.problem: We think 11 of 25 shutdowns [M] point to the sleep path or an idle hang, and the PC sleeps after 900 s [S] on mains.
ideas.stands: Adopted: I said yes (D04) but have not yet applied the Windows setting. Current setting read: sleep after 900 s [S], hybrid sleep on, hibernate never. Target: zero sleep-related events in 14 days [T].
ideas.next: I switch the Windows setting to Never, then watch 14 days [T] for sleep-related shutdowns.

ideas.name: Off-machine copy of the work
ideas.how: A verified git bundle of every branch copied off the PC, plus a nightly copy of uncommitted work, transcripts and evidence, logged.
ideas.problem: The work exists only on this PC: the clinic repository has no remote and six folders [M] are in no commit, so a single failure of this PC would take the only copy.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 1; not yet run. Clinic repository: 432 commits, 19 worktrees, no remote [M]; git integrity check (fsck) clean, 55 MB packed [M]. Target: copy under 24 h old [T].
ideas.next: I plug in the encrypted drive and switch on encryption; then run the first bundle and a clone check.

ideas.name: Resume list at sign-in, two sessions released at a time
ideas.how: At sign-in, list mid-work sessions and where each branch stands; after one message from me the root releases two sessions at a time.
ideas.problem: Work pauses when I am away or the PC reboots; idle time from 'could resume' to the next commit was about three days [M].
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 1; not yet built, and the script needs a session in the clinic repository. Idle time now about three days [M]; target under three hours [T].
ideas.next: Build it on my word (D06); idle time could fall from about three days [M] to under three hours [T].

ideas.name: Stop on resume when record and branch disagree
ideas.how: On resume, if the record is missing or the branch holds uncovered commits, list them and ask; a match resumes with no wait.
ideas.problem: After many power-offs a session's record and branch can drift apart, and a released session may start fresh, duplicating or discarding committed work.
ideas.stands: Adopted in PR #186 for FixFlow and designed into harness v2; not yet tested. Plan: replay the 9 November mass resume; zero mismatched sessions means unproven and the guard stays dormant.
ideas.next: Count mismatched sessions in the 9 November resume; add one fault-injected dispatch to the cold-resume trial.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Resume a run from its journal; retry last
ideas.how: Stable agent labels and fixed call order; finished agents replay from the journal, dead ones replay null; retries go at the tail.
ideas.problem: A session limit can kill a run midway; re-running everything wastes tokens, and a cached failure could be served as a result.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design (section 4.3) with a skeleton script; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Run the skeleton and test a forced halt and resume.

ideas.name: Docker engine up first; agents never start it
ideas.how: I start Docker Desktop before the first wave. Every Docker agent runs docker info first; on failure it returns DOCKER_ENGINE_DOWN and stops.
ideas.problem: Our backend checks run only in Docker, and an agent that tried to start or reconfigure Docker could damage the machine and the other project's containers.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design; not yet tested. The Docker engine was down when the design was written.
ideas.next: I start Docker Desktop; then the first Docker agent proves the docker info stop works.

ideas.name: Secret-safe scans: fingerprint, never value
ideas.how: The dependency and secret scan returns file, pattern, line number, first commit and a hash fingerprint, never the value or a quoted line.
ideas.problem: Every agent output is saved in the run journal, so a pasted secret would be stored there. We want scans that can never leak one.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design; not yet tested. The output schema enforces the rule. Added after the second external review.
ideas.next: Run the secret-scan test and inspect the journal for leaks; a clean journal would make scans safe to run.

ideas.name: Deny railway up and run in permissions
ideas.how: A deny block in the project settings covers the shell forms of railway up and railway run, and optionally a forced git push.
ideas.problem: Running railway up from the repo root rebuilt the API as the web app and caused a production outage; the trap lives only as prose.
ideas.stands: Adopt, not yet tested. It does nothing for the self-reported compliance problem, but it matters during the Railway drain window.
ideas.next: In bypass mode, have an agent try four railway commands; all four must be denied. I accept the deny block.

ideas.name: Keep-work-safe bundle applied to CureFound training
ideas.how: Keep a copy off the machine, a resume list, and a restart chain; for Colab or Kaggle training, one checkpoint per disease area.
ideas.problem: Unexpected power-offs interrupt agent work, and CureFound training on Colab or Kaggle (free hosted notebooks with GPU time limits) faces similar interruptions. We want work to survive a stop.
ideas.stands: Designed; no result yet. 25 [M] unexpected power-offs since 1 October; build load explains at most 6 [M]; 15 [M] came with no Claude call in the prior ten minutes; cause not found.
ideas.next: Set up the resume list and an off-machine copy; this protects CureFound runs too.

ideas.name: Separate Postgres 17 restore stack for evidence
ideas.how: A production dump is restored into its own Postgres 17 container, never the test database; exact table counts and fixed read-only queries verify it.
ideas.problem: Restoring a production dump into the test database, or into an older Postgres, could mix evidence with test state or simply fail.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Added after the second external review. Used only if the first wave produces a dump.
ideas.next: Hold until a dump exists, then run it; exact counts would make dump evidence trustworthy.

ideas.name: Memory table of who holds RAM when short
ideas.how: Run one build day with a per-process-group memory sampler, read who holds memory, then choose: shared test database, WSL2 memory cap, or closing apps.
ideas.problem: Memory runs short during builds and we do not know who holds it, which limits check slots and rules out a graph server.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 2; waits on the always-on logger. No-build reading: browser 6.1 GB, WSL2 VM 5.2 GB, Claude 3.2 GB [M]. Target: a table when under 2 GB is free [T].
ideas.next: Run the always-on logger through one build day, then choose among the three options (D11).

ideas.name: Archive policy and reaper for worktrees and containers
ideas.how: A written archive rule and a list-only reaper for merged, clean worktrees and containers, skipping anything written in the last 24 hours.
ideas.problem: Worktrees, sessions and containers pile up (19 worktrees, 34 containers [M]) and eat memory.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 2; list-only. 34 containers, 25 of 26 clinic databases stopped, 19 worktrees [M]. Target: counts back to active slices plus one after each merge [T].
ideas.next: Write the archive policy (D10) in phase 2, then run the reaper in dry-run mode.

ideas.name: Circuit breaker on session limit
ideas.how: Readers run in slices of five; two fresh nulls in one slice stop issuing and list every unstarted id as not started.
ideas.problem: When the account session limit hits, issuing more agents only produces nulls and hides what did not run.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design, hardened in version 3 with a not-started list; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Simulate two nulls in one slice to confirm it halts.

ideas.name: Never run expo prebuild in place
ideas.how: Agents may not run expo prebuild or expo run:android in the app directory; native questions are answered from cached package sources instead.
ideas.problem: Generating the native Android folder in the app directory would make the build service treat the project as bare and skip its config plugins.
ideas.stands: Stated as a hard constraint in the orchestration design; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep it in the shared context block rules.

ideas.name: Secrets and private data kept out of agents' reach
ideas.how: Pass secrets by variable name only, never read .env, and use a restricted research agent (no shell) with deny rules for credential folders.
ideas.problem: Sessions holding production credentials could leak secrets or obey injected text; subagents in bypass mode can reach Railway and GitHub credentials in the user profile.
ideas.stands: Trial for FixFlow only; not yet tested here. The testbed holds no production credentials and records no leak. The first check is a ten-minute canary (a small trial run) in a bypass-mode workflow.
ideas.next: Add to briefs of production-touching phases and run the canary. I decide on a project deny rule for .env files.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, after Simon Willison's lethal trifecta

ideas.name: Codex session folders and skill sourcing review
ideas.how: 16 [M] Codex session folders exist; one FixFlow skill sourcing review was run by three subagents.
ideas.problem: We want to know where my Codex sessions leave their work, so none of it is lost.
ideas.stands: An observation, not yet a built mechanism: the session folders are mostly empty and nothing is measured yet.
ideas.next: Read it in full on the FixFlow skills track.

ideas.name: Proposed: one shared database container
ideas.how: One shared database container with a separate database per checkout, instead of one container per worktree.
ideas.problem: One database container per worktree eats memory on a PC where RAM is short.
ideas.stands: Idea only: not built or tested. It is also one of the three options in the memory-table choice.
ideas.next: Prototype it, after the memory table shows how much the containers cost.

ideas.name: Proposed: expiry list and progress file
ideas.how: An automatic expiry list of finished worktrees and containers, plus a short progress file that each session writes every N minutes.
ideas.problem: Idle worktrees and containers pile up, and I cannot see progress while sessions run. We want both cleaned up and visible.
ideas.stands: Idea only; not built and not yet tested. It came from a transfer note on a clinic testbed card.
ideas.next: Add the expiry list and progress file; it could clear clutter and give me a live progress view.

ideas.name: Restart chain for Docker and databases after reboot
ideas.how: Docker starts at sign-in; used databases restart themselves (two at most); the check starts its own database if missing.
ideas.problem: After a reboot nothing restarts by itself: Docker Desktop and the database containers are started by hand, so work idles until I return.
ideas.stands: Parked (D03, 11 Nov): Docker's start at sign-in stays off. 31 of 34 containers have restart policy no [M]; target is databases healthy within 3 minutes of reboot [T].
ideas.next: Meanwhile the resume list starts with 'start Docker'; add a restart policy and logon task if I reopen D03.

ideas.name: Doctor script for tool checks
ideas.how: A script would check which tools are installed on the machine.
ideas.problem: We wanted to confirm the machine has the tools the harness needs.
ideas.stands: Parked for FixFlow: item 10 of my P0a setup list covers tools instead. One fact was corrected: a Python 3 interpreter exists at the Codex runtime path.
ideas.next: Would return if tool gaps start costing real time. For now, nothing.

ideas.name: Scripted worktree setup checklist
ideas.how: One repo-defined setup script would copy env and settings, install dependencies and launch the implement command, cleaning up if setup fails.
ideas.problem: A new git worktree is only useful if its setup is repeatable and leaves shared state untouched.
ideas.stands: Parked after refutation: FixFlow has no untracked env to copy, and a shared-state guard and per-phase worktree checklist already exist. The source evidence was one anecdote.
ideas.next: Would return if FixFlow gains untracked environment files that worktrees need.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, Matt Pocock livestream

themes.title: Fast, fair, trustworthy checks
themes.covers: The test run that decides whether work is right: speed, the Linux container gate, check slots, fair queues, heartbeats, clean-up, and checks that can really fail.
intro: The check is where our biggest measured wins already are. Running tests in parallel took the clinic check from 855.2 s to 283.8 s [M], tracing start-up took a 16-test run from 43 s to 11.5 s [M], and the Linux container run takes 230.1 s against 367.2 s natively [M].

What remains is making it the one gate everyone trusts: sized from measured memory, fair in its queue, visible while it runs, and never green when it tested nothing. FixFlow’s gate harness already carries several of these ideas into daily use; harness v2 phase 2 does the rest.

ideas.name: Parallel check with one database per worker
ideas.how: Six pytest-xdist workers, one PostgreSQL test database each, plus a serial pass for race tests. A script proves every test ran exactly once.
ideas.problem: The full run took about 14 minutes [M], so every gate and review round waited on it, and one session's wait held up everyone behind it.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 855.2 s [M] became a mean of 283.8 s [M] over 12 runs (range 268.3 to 298.3 s [M]), about 3.0x faster. Eight workers gain only 3% [M].
ideas.next: Keep as the speed baseline; re-measure the worker count for FixFlow's backend, which needs per-worker databases.

ideas.name: Machine-wide check lock with two slots
ideas.how: An OS file lock shared by all worktrees, two slot files, one check per checkout. The second slot opens only with 8 GiB [S] free.
ideas.problem: Several sessions running full checks at once coincided with unexpected power-offs and slowed each other, then queued behind one another.
ideas.stands: In use: two overlapping checks took 435 s [M] each against 389 to 418 s [M] alone, 1.8 to 1.9x [M] throughput. The 8 GiB gate never opened in about 980 samples [M].
ideas.next: Measure one check's peak memory, set the slot count from it, and add a fair queue with a printed position.

ideas.name: Stall watchdog, heartbeat and queue position
ideas.how: A plugin writes a heartbeat on each test event; 600 s [S] of silence kills the process tree. Planned: waiting/running/stalled states, stack dumps.
ideas.problem: A check that hangs silently costs minutes and holds up the queue, and I cannot see progress while a check waits or a loop runs long.
ideas.stands: Watchdog in use in the testbed; one real hang was killed after 961 s [M], cause never found. Heartbeat states, stack dump and queue position are designed; hooks stay off (D17).
ideas.next: Record the last started test, dump worker stacks on a stall, then lower the limit toward 120 s [T].
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Exactly-once proof and planted-fault demos
ideas.how: Judge the split by test ids: parallel ids equal the serial pass's left-out ids, no overlap. Skips fail. Planted faults must fail the check.
ideas.problem: A faster gate must not be weaker: never drop a test or print PASS wrongly, and a passing test does not prove its guard works.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 1,844 parallel plus 128 serial test ids [M] in the run that proved the split, none in both. Six planted faults gave CHECK FAILED [M]. Not yet in FixFlow CI.
ideas.next: Add the same id accounting and a scripted guard removal to FixFlow CI and the fix-round contract.

ideas.name: Race tests decide blocked from the database
ideas.how: A helper polls pg_stat_activity (the Postgres list of open sessions) up to 15 s [S] for a session waiting on a lock, with the first call among the blockers.
ideas.problem: Under load a slow second call looked blocked after 0.6 s, so a race test could pass with a broken lock; timing-based race tests are flaky.
ideas.stands: In use: 59 blocked assertions in 13 files migrated [M]; 159 race tests pass in 189 s [M]. It does not show which lock, and serial pass cost is unchanged.
ideas.next: Replace remaining sleep-and-check assertions with database-observed waits.

ideas.name: Random-tag flaky tests fixed after parallel runs
ideas.how: A letters-only random_tag() and without_identifiers() replaced 33 uses [M] in 21 files [M], plus a layout test that fails if the old hex-tag forms return.
ideas.problem: Parallel runs exposed chance failures from random digit-bearing test data, which made the gate unreliable.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: about 3 failures in about 40 full runs [M] before; seven consecutive green runs [M] after. Small sample; random values elsewhere may recur.
ideas.next: Audit FixFlow's uuid fixtures for random hex before parallelising its tests.

ideas.name: Retry for Windows loopback error 10055
ideas.how: A helper retries only that error, 0.02 s [S] apart, up to five times [S]; a serial-pass retry fails the step, parallel retries are reported.
ideas.problem: The Windows socket error 10055 (no buffer space available) made checks fail spuriously: 2 of the first 22 full runs [M].
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: no further failure in 17 full runs [M] after the retry. Port exhaustion was ruled out (TIME_WAIT peak 352 [M]); the cause is not found.
ideas.next: Use the same narrow bounded retry if FixFlow sees this refusal.

ideas.name: Start-up cost found by tracing
ideas.how: Tracebacks from Python’s faulthandler (which prints where a stuck process is) showed pytest's base-temp step (setting up its temporary-folder root) taking about 32 s [M] via symlink on Windows; --basetemp fixed it.
ideas.problem: Even a 16-test run paid a large fixed start-up cost that no test caused.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 43 s to 11.5 s [M] on a 16-test run. Windows-specific; why the symlink was slow is not explained.
ideas.next: Pass --basetemp or avoid tmp_path in FixFlow runs on this PC; it would likely hit the same cost.

ideas.name: Native Windows stays the gate, Linux optional
ideas.how: Only native exercises Windows branches (job object, file lock, socket retry), so it stays the gate, run when devtools change or as canary.
ideas.problem: Native and container modes cover different code, so we need to decide which run counts as the gate.
ideas.stands: Decision in force in the testbed. No measurement of its own; it forgoes about 230 s [M] against about 367 s [M]. Harness v2 proposes the container as gate instead (D09).
ideas.next: Decide explicitly which mode is the gate (D09).

ideas.name: Pre-commit hook running the workflow verify command
ideas.how: A hook runs one verify command at commit: links, JSON, provenance hashes, instruction contracts, workflow tests. Local and bypassable.
ideas.problem: We want broken links, bad JSON and failing workflow tests caught at commit time, not found later, because nothing was checking at that moment.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 227 [M] tracked files matched their commits, 29 [M] workflow tests pass, bad commits rejected. Skipped for FixFlow: it read the working tree and let an all-skipped suite pass.
ideas.next: Copy the lesson, not the code: a gate must fail on skipped or empty suites, with negative controls.

ideas.name: Fair first-come queue with heavy-job patience
ideas.how: Tickets give arrival order. A light job may pass a heavy one that waited under 900 s [S]; after that the heavy job blocks.
ideas.problem: Waiters retried at random: one lane waited 20 minutes [M] while later arrivals were served; two Android builds stalled eight short runs for about an hour [M].
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow's slot script, rewritten after those failures. Waits since the change are not yet measured.
ideas.next: Measure waits after the change; it could confirm that short runs no longer starve.

ideas.name: Per-lane gate harness with Docker recipe
ideas.how: ff-gates.sh runs each gate in a lane-named container with its own database, a read-only source copy, per-gate logs, exit-code lines and a summary.
ideas.problem: A gate script reporting only the last exit code hides which gate failed, and allowing one backend gate at a time blocked parallel lanes.
ideas.stands: In use by every FixFlow lane, and measured: backend 757 tests [M] in 7 min 23 s [M] cold; web 106 tests in 33 s [M]; mobile 334 tests in 29 s [M].
ideas.next: Lanes pass pytest arguments in the inner loop and keep full runs for merge-readiness.

ideas.name: Skip-aware integration gate
ideas.how: pytest's junit report (an XML file of test results) lists skip reasons; a script fails the gate on any skipped integration test. Mobile CI no longer passes with no tests.
ideas.problem: A test run can look green while integration tests were silently skipped because the database variable was unset, proving nothing about the real database.
ideas.stands: In use in every FixFlow backend gate run. Baseline: 0 integration tests skipped of 757 [M].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Checks must be able to fail (red-team lessons)
ideas.how: Plan rules, no machinery: no accepted row beside a failed check, if/raise not assert, clean-environment boot tests, unknown never recorded as zero.
ideas.problem: Gates go green without testing anything: accepted rows beside failed checks, bare asserts, boot tests in a dirty environment, unknown recorded as zero.
ideas.stands: Carried as plan rules in the harness; the BAML sweep confirmed they were already held. Not otherwise tested.
ideas.next: Apply when writing the drain audit script and the first-wave results tables.
ideas.origin: Harness review; clinic red-team lessons; BAML sweep

ideas.name: Merge-readiness labels on gate summaries
ideas.how: The summary prints tree=dirty for uncommitted files and RUN partial for extra pytest arguments. Merge-readiness needs a clean tree and no extra arguments.
ideas.problem: Gates test the working tree but label the result with HEAD, and extra arguments can deselect tests, so a green summary could mislead a merge decision.
ideas.stands: In use: printed in every FixFlow gate summary. Not yet tested against a real misleading case.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Named exit-coded gates per runtime
ideas.how: Each runtime has a named exit-coded gate: backend in Appendix A, web and mobile as CLAUDE.md chains. A cross-runtime aggregate was weighed.
ideas.problem: We want agents to hand off only after the typecheck, format and tests ran together, not after a partial or noisy run.
ideas.stands: In use per runtime (backend gate, web and mobile chains). A cross-runtime aggregate does not fit a backend gated in Docker on Windows; no verdict on it.
ideas.next: Keep using it; revisit an aggregate only with a defined measurement.

ideas.name: Pass counts are not the success signal
ideas.how: CI runs every suite per PR; phases close only on green gates; reviewers name a test that fails on base and passes on head.
ideas.problem: We want a plain pass count never to stand in for proof, because it can hide regressions.
ideas.stands: In use: already how FixFlow works. It would be reopened only if a regression escaped the full CI suite after merge.
ideas.next: Count post-merge regressions after P1.

ideas.name: Weighted machine-wide slot lock for heavy jobs
ideas.how: ff-slot gives out 3 [S] slots (2 [S] while a Gradle lane runs). Backend stacks, Jest, Vitest and emulators take 1; a Gradle build is exclusive.
ideas.problem: We want eight lanes starting at once never to exhaust this PC's 31 GB [M] of RAM with stacks, test runs, builds and emulators.
ideas.stands: In use: every gate run takes a slot. A backend stack used about 0.4-0.5 GB [M], not its 3 GB [S] cap; free RAM with eight sessions was 5.5-7.7 GB [M].
ideas.next: Raise the slot count only after more free RAM is measured.

ideas.name: Gates share the database container's network
ideas.how: Gates join the database container's network, so the database is at localhost as in CI. A real network takes an explicit subnet in 10.77.0.0/16 [S].
ideas.problem: We want gates to run when another project's 29 [M] networks have used up Docker's address pools, which stopped the first gate design.
ideas.stands: In use, fixed in commit be2e27a. The address-pool error was measured on 2026-11-13 [M] and no longer blocks gates. Design Appendix C still cannot run as written.
ideas.next: Use the working dump script for dumps. Keep; FixFlow never prunes networks it did not create.
ideas.origin: Ship plan §7, found by running the first gate draft

ideas.name: Architecture rules file plus CI boundary checks
ideas.how: CLAUDE.md invariants state the rules, and import-linter and ESLint boundary checks in CI enforce them.
ideas.problem: We want agents not to drift from the architecture, so we keep durable rules and enforce the slice boundaries mechanically.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow: the rules file plus import-linter and ESLint checks already run in CI. An outside team's report confirmed the same shape.
ideas.next: Keep using it; the mobile app's boundary checks are a separate idea.
ideas.origin: FixFlow repo practice; BAML sweep confirmed

ideas.name: Before and after file manifests
ideas.how: Each task writes a hash manifest of all tracked files before editing, then compares after, so every changed file is accounted for.
ideas.problem: We want edits not to touch files that were not meant to change, and a way to audit what a session touched.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 247 [M] baseline files all accounted for, six [M] declared documents changed, 23 [M] protected source paths unchanged. It catches unintended change, not wrong change; no timing cost recorded.
ideas.next: In FixFlow a pre-task git diff --stat or tree hash gives the same guard.

ideas.name: Two container checks at once
ideas.how: Run two container checks at the same time on the PC, since each needs less than the whole machine.
ideas.problem: Checks queued behind each other for up to 34 minutes even though one check does not use the whole machine.
ideas.stands: Measured, not used: 266 s and 267 s [M] together against about 440 s [M] in a row; least free memory 5.3 GB [M].
ideas.next: Measure one check's peak memory and size the slots from it; this could nearly halve queue waits.

ideas.name: Non-durable test-database settings
ideas.how: The dev and test Postgres container runs with fsync, synchronous commit and full-page writes switched off, in the compose file only; deploy files untouched.
ideas.problem: We wanted to know whether the test database's disk writes were slowing the check.
ideas.stands: Tested in the testbed: 316 s to 297 s [M] on single runs, inside the noise. The check is CPU-bound, not flush-bound, so the gain is unproven.
ideas.next: Cheap to copy for a local Postgres test container, kept out of production; a clean same-tree comparison would settle it.

ideas.name: Queue-wait measurement for the test lock
ideas.how: Collect waits from printed lock-holder messages and check logs across single, paired and gated runs; log each merge's check size and duration.
ideas.problem: We want to know how much of a gate's cost is queueing rather than testing.
ideas.stands: Measured in the testbed: 15 [M] recorded waits, 3 s to 726 s [M]. A check of about 5 minutes [E] cost 10-18 minutes [E] with two to four sessions.
ideas.next: Run the gate once per merge, not per slice session; this decides whether it is sharded.

ideas.name: Per-lane run lock and fixed container names
ideas.how: A lane-and-kind lock refuses a second run (exit 4). Fixed container names fail a second start. Never re-issue a mutating command after a timeout.
ideas.problem: Two gate runs against one database deadlock or drop each other's database, and re-issuing a command after a timeout can duplicate its effects.
ideas.stands: Tested: a second run was refused with exit 4 [M]. The lock is reclaimed if older than the last boot or its process is gone. The container-name rule is designed only.
ideas.next: Verify the container-name rule with a forced second start.

ideas.name: Linux container check, proposed as the gate
ideas.how: A pinned Debian 12 container beside the database, 12 workers [S], a hash-verified copy of the tree, and no fallback to native.
ideas.problem: Tests ran only on Windows while production is Linux, and the Windows-to-Docker database path made the check slow and hid Linux-only failures.
ideas.stands: Built in the testbed, optional: mean 230.1 s [M] against 367.2 s [M] native, about 1.6x faster. The Linux run found 2 failures [M] in 2,472 tests that Windows missed.
ideas.next: My decision D09 to make it the gate, then build in harness v2 phase 2; expect one fix-up round.

ideas.name: Mirror CI environment in the gate
ideas.how: The gate reads the environment setting from the worktree's own CI file and passes it on; an older worktree gets none, as CI did.
ideas.problem: A gate with a different environment than CI could pass or fail differently, especially once the backend refuses to boot outside dev or test.
ideas.stands: Built into the FixFlow gate script. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep; confirm once a phase that changes the boot rule runs through it.

ideas.name: Check slots sized from one measured memory number
ideas.how: Measure one check's peak memory, size the slots from it, run a fair queue printing each place, and run one full gate per round.
ideas.problem: Checks wait 6 to 34 minutes behind each other: one slot open, longest wait 2,030 s [M].
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 2, not yet run; peak-memory table still to take. Target: second slot open on at least half of polls, median wait under a minute [T].
ideas.next: Take the peak-memory table, then decide D11; it could open the second slot safely.

ideas.name: Re-run Node failures under Node 22
ideas.how: A Jest or React Native failure on Node 24 is re-run once in a node:22 container before it is called a defect.
ideas.problem: This PC has Node 24 while CI pins Node 22, so a failure could be a machine artifact rather than a repo defect.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design and ship plan; not seen in the gate script. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Prepare the node:22 re-run command; it could remove false mobile defects.

ideas.name: CI checks for known prose traps
ideas.how: A Ruff rule bans hmac.compare_digest outside the security module; one check rejects an empty eas.json env value; another rejects the Sentry plugin in app.json.
ideas.problem: We want FixFlow's costly written warnings to fail a build, not rely on an agent reading CLAUDE.md.
ideas.stands: Adopt for the three history-backed checks, with a railway deny rule and a skill-frontmatter lint also adopt, narrowed. Proposal only, nothing installed. FixFlow-only: no testbed number would move.
ideas.next: Plant a violation of each; it must fail CI on the base commit and pass after the fix.

ideas.name: Stop after three identical CI failures
ideas.how: Rule line: if the same CI job fails on 3 [S] pushes running after green local gates, stop, journal it, hand it to me.
ideas.problem: We want an agent never to keep re-pushing and re-running until CI turns green, which could hide a real failure.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a rule line, flaky-rerun allowance dropped; PR Auto-fix stays off. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Over 5 [T] code phases, no job should fail on 3 [T] consecutive heads unless journaled.

ideas.name: Stub run of gate scripts with no model
ideas.how: Run a gate script under node with stand-in agents that return nothing, crash or refute; every id must appear once; none may reach merge.
ideas.problem: We want to know a new gate script never reads a reviewer that returned nothing as a clean one, without spending model tokens.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 (mechanism 5). Feasibility proven in one stub run (the script ran with stand-in agents, reported two live results [M] and named the missing one). Not yet tested against the three recorded defects.
ideas.next: Re-introduce each of the 3 [M] recorded defects and confirm it fails all; build before any real agent enters the gate.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after Pydantic AI; Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Caller-pin test in repository CI
ideas.how: A backend pytest using Python's ast module pins the only allowed callers of verify_pin and create_access_token to the login function.
ideas.problem: We want a new file minting a login token without the lock check to fail the merge, since no store lookup can see that second door.
ideas.stands: Designed (decision KS-D17: yes, one PR per probe). Needs no store, so it can land any time before ship phase P7b-1. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: I choose the timing; P7b-1 must extend the allow-list under review.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, my critique and refuter pass

ideas.name: CI check that CLAUDE.md facts match the code
ideas.how: CI fails if CLAUDE.md's migration head differs from the end of the down_revision chain; a second check warns on paths that no longer resolve.
ideas.problem: We want the instruction file never to drift from the code, such as a wrong migration head, so agents never trust a wrong fact.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a phase P1 deliverable. The path check is a warning only until P13c, so it does not fail on first run. Not yet built or tested.
ideas.next: Build in P1, warning-only for paths with an allow-list.
ideas.origin: Harness review; clinic harness drift checks

ideas.name: Import rules for the mobile app
ideas.how: dependency-cruiser mirrors the backend import rules in the mobile app: screens cannot import write functions; raw fetch stays in two files; runs in CI.
ideas.problem: We want the rule that no mobile write bypasses the outbox enforced by a check, because today it is only prose.
ideas.stands: Adopted in the harness review as the better alternative to a code-graph tool; scheduled as phase P5b-2. Not built or tested yet.
ideas.next: Build in P5b-2; it turns a prose invariant into a CI-enforced rule.

ideas.name: Verifying command and negative run per tick
ideas.how: Each tick records the exact verifying command and expected result; for a gate box, a negative run showing the gate fails when it should.
ideas.problem: Checklist boxes for CI gates, docs and deploy steps can be ticked without proof that the check works.
ideas.stands: Trial in P1 and the next two code phases; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Apply the per-tick line in P1 and the next two code phases.

ideas.name: One-off tsc unused-code check on mobile
ideas.how: Run tsc with the noUnusedLocals flag once on the mobile app; set it in tsconfig only if it finds real unused code.
ideas.problem: We want to know whether agents leave unused code in the mobile app that no gate flags.
ideas.stands: Trial: the one new idea to survive the Horthy addendum cap review, after 15 [M] other families fell. Mobile parity only, no new tooling. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Run it once; adopt the flag only if real hits appear.

ideas.name: Close-time clean worktree and manifest check
ideas.how: At phase close, run git status and compare a file listing of the evidence folder with its manifest; each entry is committed or excluded.
ideas.problem: We want intended files, such as a review-input tool, never left uncommitted at phase close.
ideas.stands: Trial over the next 5 [T] phase closes. It costs nothing to run; the slop-scoring part of the source idea was dropped. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Add it to the closing message of the section 0 gates.

ideas.name: Red-team of the workflow gates and repair plan
ideas.how: A nine-perspective review of the testbed's gates found nine defects, each with a reproduction and closure condition; a repair plan ordered the fixes.
ideas.problem: We want to know the workflow's own gates can fail, since they could pass while checking nothing.
ideas.stands: Deferred: it found 3 P1, 5 P2 and 1 P3 defects [M], eight still open; an all-skipped suite passed with exit 0 [M]. No code repair was made, as the build moved on.
ideas.next: Use the defect shapes as a red-team checklist for FixFlow's own hooks.

ideas.name: Stop hook that re-runs the CI checks
ideas.how: When an agent tries to finish, a hook runs the same quality and typecheck commands as CI and blocks with only the errors.
ideas.problem: We want an agent never to end its turn with a red tree, without waiting for CI to tell us.
ideas.stands: Parked: first pass left it deferred with no verdict; the addendum ruled skip. It reopens the pre-commit skip, and backend gates take minutes in Docker. Not tested.
ideas.next: Would return if gates get fast enough to run at every stop, and only after D17 reopens hooks.

ideas.name: Slop and complexity detectors as a gate
ideas.how: Run slop-rule or complexity and duplication scripts as a gate on agent code.
ideas.problem: We want to stop agent code getting messier over time, with some gate that scores it.
ideas.stands: Parked: such detectors flag most code (77.75% to 94.25% [S] of lines across models) and can be gamed, so they give no clear bad-code verdict.
ideas.next: Return only if I propose a slop gate.

ideas.name: CI-driven fix agents per failure stage
ideas.how: CI and a review bot trigger fresh follow-up fix agents at each failure stage, instead of agents running the full suite themselves.
ideas.problem: We want agents not to wait a long time running the full suite in their own sandbox.
ideas.stands: Parked: FixFlow CI runs the suite in about 3 minutes [E]; dropping the local run would leave release and drain branches ungated. The source saw waits fall from 15-20 to 2-4 minutes [S].
ideas.next: None; it would return if local runs became the slow step.

ideas.name: Tiered verification and rework-rate metric
ideas.how: Run a relevant test subset per phase with cheap proxies, the full suite at close; track the share of a diff changed after review.
ideas.problem: We want less time spent on full suites each session, and a health measure for review rework.
ideas.stands: Parked: full gates at close already exist, Docker setup cost does not shrink with a subset, and squash merges break the metric. Its 5% [G] bar is an unmeasured rule of thumb.
ideas.next: None; no change planned.

themes.title: Review and fix rounds that converge
themes.covers: Reviewing work and fixing what review finds: fix rounds, claims checks, fresh reviewers, refuters, severity, reading the final commit, and merging.
intro: In the clinic testbed a slice took 2.8 review rounds on average [M], and 64 % of reviews sent the slice back [M]. Some fixes created new defects, some reports claimed more than was done, and in 5 of 6 high-risk merges nobody had read the final commit [M].

The ideas here make review converge and make its verdicts checkable: a contract for each fix round, scripts that test claims, fresh reviewers that try to refute, and a merge queue that records who read what. Harness v2 phase 3 turns the strongest of them into six scripts that spend no tokens.

ideas.name: Two-level merge gates with refute-reviewers
ideas.how: Root runs the full check; two read-only Opus reviewers try to refute claims; findings numbered P1 to P3 with owner; root reads round three.
ideas.problem: We need agent output checked before it merges, so no unresolved critical finding reaches main.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed for every slice: 9 of 11 [M] gates took three rounds; 19 [M] P1 findings in round one; at least 5 [M] more P1 created by fixes.
ideas.next: Add an independent read of the last fix diff and a per-round cost record.

ideas.name: Close findings only on tests with positive controls
ideas.how: A finding closes only on a harness-run test; each 'nothing found' check needs a case it must find; remove one lock at a time.
ideas.problem: Findings and claims closed on a model's say-so, and our own checks reported success wrongly: a drill printed PASS while testing nothing.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed; at least four [M] instances later proved less than claimed. A trial for the root's gate in FixFlow is proposed.
ideas.next: Start in the root's gate; add positive controls to FixFlow check scripts.

ideas.name: Review bots, unmeasured-as-failure, hand-back labelling
ideas.how: A per-PR Opus reviewer exists, gates treat unmeasured as failed, and Claude Code labels subagent reports as model output, not user instruction.
ideas.problem: We want review that adds no noise, no missing scan counted as clean, and no instructions smuggled in through hand-backs.
ideas.stands: Already in place or provided by the platform; nothing new to build or measure.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Dated audits by parallel automated reviewers
ideas.how: Three parallel automated reviewers plus an integration review audit a repo, separating hash-verified preservation from substantive review; a static fit audit reads tool code.
ideas.problem: We want stale guidance and missing evidence found before we build on a repo, and a clear boundary on what a recall tool puts in context.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed, done once: 61 files reviewed [M], 14 findings [M], 641 cached members re-hashed with no failures [M], 5 peer-review corrections closed [M]. Cost not recorded.
ideas.next: Copy the dated-audit format with a stale-guidance table as a CLAUDE.md drift check for FixFlow.

ideas.name: Assess, refute by default, then judge idea sweeps
ideas.how: Cards cluster into families; two Opus reviewers score each; a fresh refuter attacks every adopt or trial family by default; a judge decides.
ideas.problem: We want to judge about 1,900 sweep cards fairly, without the orchestrator scoring them and without one reader's enthusiasm promoting weak ideas.
ideas.stands: In use on two sweeps: Horthy, of 144 attacked families 65 refuted and 79 narrowed, none passed [M]; BAML, none of 24 families proposed for adopt survived and 4 of 22 proposed for trial did [M].
ideas.next: Give the next sweep's assessment brief the design text; trial whether refuting by default earns its cost.

ideas.name: Screenshot capture and rubric scoring of screens
ideas.how: A capture script screenshots every role and screen at 375 and 1280 px with a manifest; an Opus rubric review and refutation score results.
ideas.problem: We want screen quality and UI changes checked with visible before and after evidence, without a human looking at everything.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 130 pages, 260 PNGs [M]; rubric score rose from 64 to 110 of 160 [M]; of 59 findings 16 fixed, 20 partly, 22 not, 1 regressed [M].
ideas.next: Build a Playwright (browser automation) capture for FixFlow's React app; treat model scores as triage only.

ideas.name: Fresh-context skeptic per finding
ideas.how: An Opus xhigh skeptic sees only the claim, evidence and failing condition; one per P0 and per P1 in sensitive areas.
ideas.problem: Confident but wrong findings get into the plan when the same reasoning that produced them also checks them.
ideas.stands: In use since gate G2: 12 [M] skeptics over 109 [M] claims; 8 [M] verdicts lowered a severity, none refuted a claim. A second-lens brief for the geofence claims (a second skeptic reading the symptom from another angle) is designed, not run.
ideas.next: Brief the geofence P0 skeptic to explain the field symptom with app-logic causes alone.

ideas.name: Skeptic budget capped at twelve, allocated by priority
ideas.how: At most 12 Opus skeptics per run, given to highest-priority claims first; claims over the cap are listed or dispositioned, never dropped.
ideas.problem: Unbounded verification multiplies Opus tokens, but at gate G2 the first four analysts to finish used up all the skeptics, leaving other P1 claims unverified.
ideas.stands: In use: the cap is applied, and priority allocation became a rule after G2. 12 [M] skeptics covered 109 [M] relocated claims; 8 [M] verdicts lowered severity. Overflow handled by corroboration.
ideas.next: Reserve skeptic slots for P0 and P1 claims before analysts finish; log overflow ids.

ideas.name: Corroboration policy for over-cap claims
ideas.how: Mark each over-cap claim C (corroborated elsewhere, natively checked, or arithmetic) or O (open, awaiting a fact); buy no second Opus pass.
ideas.problem: Claims beyond the skeptic cap cannot be verified, yet we must neither drop them nor trust them blindly.
ideas.stands: In use at gate G2 on 17 [M] over-cap rows: 15 [M] ruled C and 2 [M] ruled O. Unattacked claims stay questions for me, not findings.
ideas.next: Replace with proper skeptic coverage when the budget allows.

ideas.name: Verified register, open-risks list and refuted list
ideas.how: From verdicts, a script derives a verified register, an open-risks list and a refuted list; each finding has a severity and status code.
ideas.problem: A single pass or fail list loses unsettled claims and hides refutations; every finding needs a uniform record of how well it is verified.
ideas.stands: In use at gate G2 as the verified findings register: 139 [M] findings; a P0 on the open list blocks work on its area. The deriving script is not yet built.
ideas.next: Keep numbering continuous; implement the derivation in the workflow script.

ideas.name: Citation check over every claim
ideas.how: A Sonnet agent per analyst re-locates each quote by content and git history and marks it located, moved, dead or already fixed.
ideas.problem: Analyst and research claims may quote text that moved, was fixed or never existed, and agent research may misquote its sources.
ideas.stands: In use at gate G2 and in the clinic research pack: 109 [M] claims re-located, none dead; 575 of 579 [M] quotes matched exactly. It checks existence only.
ideas.next: Wire up per-analyst pipelining; apply quote matching to FixFlow agent reports.

ideas.name: Honest-empty web research and re-fetch check
ideas.how: Agents log tool status and URLs tried, stop after two denials, and may return empty; Sonnet re-fetches key URLs and downgrades unconfirmed facts.
ideas.problem: A research agent that cannot reach the web may invent facts, and a cited web fact may not appear on the page.
ideas.stands: In use at gate G2: 11 of 12 [M] web statements re-checked were confirmed on the page. The honest-empty rule is part of the research schema.
ideas.next: Check the first research topics for degraded coverage; run the re-check after the top hypotheses.

ideas.name: Evidence tags and honest labels on every fact
ideas.how: Every claim cites path:line with a quote and is tagged verified-in-code, verified-by-command, web or inferred; agents return facts, not severity, unless asked.
ideas.problem: Readers cannot tell how strongly a fact is established, and reports blur observed, inferred and never-checked, or mistake automated review for human review.
ideas.stands: In use as a convention in all agent definitions and the clinic testbed; nothing enforces it. Clinic labels were wrong at least twice [M].
ideas.next: Check tag use in the first results; add a machine check that labelled logs exist.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design, Skills packages, Clinic testbed

ideas.name: Multi-lens architecture panel with judges and refuters
ideas.how: Four Opus architects propose, one lens each; two opposed Opus judges score each area; 45 claims each get two refuters; the main session rules.
ideas.problem: A plan repaired in place can hide a wrong foundation, and a design written alone carries blind spots; I wanted the architecture tested before work started.
ideas.stands: In use: run once on 1 November with 101 [M] agents, about 10.1M [M] subagent tokens, 34 [M] minutes; verdict: no wrong foundation. 7 [M] refuters were lost to a usage limit.
ideas.next: Reuse for the next architecture question, budgeting refuters so none hit a usage limit.

ideas.name: Critique rounds on a design before it runs
ideas.how: Three Opus critics and two external reviews critique the design; section 11 records each accepted or rejected point with its reason.
ideas.problem: A design written alone carries blind spots, and finding them after a run is costly.
ideas.stands: In use; two rounds done. Version 3 accepted data-preservation, verification buckets, script bookkeeping, gate recipe, dump inspection, evidence and secret rules.
ideas.next: Add an Opus critic at Stage 3 for the phase plan.

ideas.name: Two refuters per claim: repository and operations
ideas.how: Each falsifiable claim is attacked by two fresh Opus refuters, one reading the repository, one operations, defaulting to refuted and needing executed counter-evidence.
ideas.problem: We want every recommendation's premises checked before we build on it, including facts about real hosts and phones that a code-only reader misses.
ideas.stands: In use: 45 panel claims attacked; several premises were refuted or unmeasured and narrowed before the plan [M]. Knowledge store: 1 confirmed, 21 narrowed, 8 refuted [M]; second pass 6 narrowed [M].
ideas.next: Re-run the seven refuter runs on the cash and accounting-books claims, lost to a usage limit, if those claims become decisions; re-run on new mechanisms.

ideas.name: Completeness critic over a draft
ideas.how: One Opus xhigh critic reads draft and register, listing missing items, unsupported claims, contradictions, readability problems; each becomes a numbered amendment.
ideas.problem: A finished draft can still lack mechanisms, hold contradictions or be hard for me to read, so we want a last read for completeness.
ideas.stands: In use on the knowledge-store design, run twice: 19 missing, 15 unsupported, 19 contradictions, 9 readability items [M]; later 22 contradictions, 15 mismatches, 17 leftovers [M]. All text repair.
ideas.next: Run again after major edits and before my review.

ideas.name: Skeptic round with forced verbatim citation
ideas.how: A skeptic files counterexamples quoting the passage; the designer accepts with a diff or rejects citing a verbatim rule; one round, then stop.
ideas.problem: Reviews stay vague in both directions; we want attacks and rebuttals that point at exact text.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed, once: 21 attacks, 12 accepted, 3 rejected on one ground, 6 on another [M]; 15 design elements revised [M]. Both sides were the same model family.
ideas.next: Adopt the quote-forced attack and rebuttal format in FixFlow gate reviews.

ideas.name: Hand-written reading-coverage ledger
ideas.how: A file-by-file, page-by-page table records what was read in full or sampled, with access limits and a verification record.
ideas.problem: A report may claim sources were read when they were not, so we want coverage to be visible.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed: 41 coverage rows checked by script on 2026-09-30 [M]. Hand-maintained, so it drifts; effect on rework not yet measured.
ideas.next: Generate the table from agent transcripts instead of writing it by hand.

ideas.name: Design adjudicated by sweep, judges, refuters, my critique
ideas.how: Four workflows: a research sweep, four architects scored by three judges, refuters plus a completeness critic, then each point of my critique checked by two verifiers.
ideas.problem: A design from one session carries unchecked claims, and my critique is sometimes right and sometimes not, so we neither obey nor ignore it blindly.
ideas.stands: In use on the knowledge-store design: about 15M subagent tokens [M]; scores of 360: A 292, C 282, D 281, B 222 [M]; critique verdicts partly or mostly right [M]; 20 amendments.
ideas.next: Reuse the pattern for other designs and later critiques.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after the Orchestration design

ideas.name: Sonnet builds, Opus reviews
ideas.how: The cheaper model builds and the stronger model reviews. Available today with no library.
ideas.problem: We hoped Sonnet at lower effort could match Opus through cached reasoning, but on judgment-heavy work the quality came from review.
ideas.stands: In use: an Opus reviewer found a serious defect in 9 of 14 [M] Opus-built clinic slices. Our tests resolve only ±11 to 14 points [E], wider than the 2 to 8 point [M] tier gap.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Delta check of a plan revision by fresh critics
ideas.how: Fresh Opus critics read only a plan's changes; Sonnet re-locates blocker and major citations; findings are tabled and folded into the next version.
ideas.problem: Each plan revision can bring in new defects, so I want a fresh read of what changed before the revision is trusted.
ideas.stands: Tested: the v6-to-v8 delta check found 1 blocker, 20 major, 20 minor [M]; the section 7 amendment critic found 1 blocker, 7 major, 12 minor [M]; 19 accepted, 1 open ruling.
ideas.next: Repeat after any large plan change; decide, before P7a merges, whether a manager may record or void a payment on a closed job.

ideas.name: Binding PR review: fresh, refute-by-default, head-bound
ideas.how: Coordinator sends a fresh Opus reviewer, refute-by-default, bound to the PR head commit, with a brief built from the phase's register ids.
ideas.problem: A review of an older commit can pass for approval of a later one, and an author who briefs its own reviewer chooses what is attacked.
ideas.stands: Rule accepted 13 Nov; reviewer agent and repo-conventions skill built in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. No lane has reported ready yet, so it has not run on a real PR.
ideas.next: Coordinator dispatches the first binding review when the first PR is marked ready.
ideas.origin: Harness review, Ship plan §7, Skills packages

ideas.name: Transcript audit at each merge
ideas.how: Read-only script over our own tool-call transcripts tells whether a reviewer read the final head and how many root edits each merge had.
ideas.problem: The merge record is self-reported and fields have been filled falsely; we have no independent source for who read the final head.
ideas.stands: Used once in the testbed with 0 [M] model calls. The merge-time version is designed for harness v2 phase 3, not yet run; it needs transcripts to survive cleanup.
ideas.next: Run the tally over the 10 and 11 November merges; it must find the unread heads by itself.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, Clinic testbed, Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Cross-runtime contract map
ideas.how: A script extracts client URL to route, settings keys, migration chain, slice contracts, outbox kinds and handlers, and file-tied invariants as review input.
ideas.problem: Silent breaks between web, mobile, backend and configuration live in contracts, not imports, so neither a search nor an import graph sees them.
ideas.stands: Partly built as a script: 65 of 73 client URL literals matched 77 route decorators [M]; 46 settings keys, 46 migration links [M]. Value to review untested.
ideas.next: Test at zero tokens on the recorded defect chains, beside the touch-list test.

ideas.name: Specialist reviewers for offline sync, migrations, security
ideas.how: Three sourced skills with paired Opus reviewer agents, each refuting by default and running fixed commands only, never probing a live host.
ideas.problem: Our offline engine, populated-table migrations and security code have FixFlow-specific rules that generic checklists miss or tell agents to wrongly fix.
ideas.stands: Built: skills and Opus agents in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Use them on the P1, P2a/P2b, P6a and P7a reviews.
ideas.origin: Skills packages, after TanStack/db and OWASP ASVS

ideas.name: Fix-round contract: two rounds, revert, test per finding
ideas.how: Two rounds; a fail-before, pass-after test per finding; revert instead of patching a patch; fresh agent after two failed fixes.
ideas.problem: Our fixes add new stored state with untested endings, so they create new defects; 64 % [M] of reviews sent slices back.
ideas.stands: Designed into harness v2 phase 3; not yet run. Testbed record: 2.8 [M] review rounds per slice. First step is a replay on recorded chains under the seal.
ideas.next: Replay on recorded chains under the seal, then add the clauses to the fix-round brief.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile, Harness v2 design, Dex Horthy sweep

ideas.name: Review as a gate workflow with typed verdict
ideas.how: Reviewers run in a saved workflow, one gate at a time, and return a typed verdict naming the commit they read; the root keeps judgment.
ideas.problem: One root session is our serial gate for briefing, reading, checking and board edits, so nothing leaves faster than the root.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3; not yet run. Gain is bounded: the root is 15.3 % [M] of tokens. Target: no root compaction across five gates [T].
ideas.next: Probe that a workflow agent can run the check at all, then a dry run with stand-in agents.

ideas.name: Merge queue that refuses a wrong head
ideas.how: Local script merges one at a time under a lock, tests the merged result, checks the verdict names the head, requires a reader field.
ideas.problem: High-risk merges went in with nobody reading the final head, 5 of 6 [M], and the root merged and edited the board by hand.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3; not yet run. Record-only first: replayed over the 65 [M] recorded merges it must flag the unread heads of 10 and 11 November.
ideas.next: Build record-only and replay it over the 65 recorded merges; refusal waits for decision D15.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Claims file and verdict script per gate round
ideas.how: Each slice commits a claims file; a script runs each cited test at the fix's parent and at head, and flags weakened tests.
ideas.problem: Session reports cite tests or evidence that do not exist or match: 20-plus [M] recorded overstatements. A model re-reading its own claims has not caught them.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3; never built in the clinic repo, not yet run. Replay first over recorded gates; target false flags under 10 % [T].
ideas.next: Replay over the recorded gates beside the root's reading; add a rerun rule for flaky tests.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile, Dex Horthy sweep, BAML sweep

ideas.name: Preexisting-failure and fail-before claims must cite proof
ideas.how: Two brief clauses: a 'preexisting' excuse must show the same failure on the base commit; fail-before lines cite the command and result.
ideas.problem: Agents excuse a new skip or red test as 'preexisting' without proof, and a reviewer's 'test X fails on base' can be unverified and false.
ideas.stands: Adopted as proposals for the ship plan's routing rules; cost almost nothing; not yet tested. Pass bar: zero uncited merges over the first 5 [T] code phases.
ideas.next: Apply to the first 3 to 5 code-phase PRs; re-run one cited command per PR on the base commit.

ideas.name: One finding table and counting parser
ideas.how: Write P0 to P3 and each status once; parser takes allowed values from that table; unmapped status fails; it reports rows kept and dropped.
ideas.problem: Minor findings pile up uncounted: 183 [M] P3 ids carry no status, so we have no open count, and a parser can silently lose rows.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3; a script, no tokens, not built. Target: zero unmapped statuses, every dropped row explained, and an open count over the 183 [M] P3 ids.
ideas.next: Draft the one P0 to P3 table (decision D12) and generate the parser from it.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, Bottleneck compile, Harness v2 design

ideas.name: I read marked hunks on high-risk merges
ideas.how: Opus reviewer marks invariant-touching hunks; on high-risk merges I read only those, at the same head commit; the record names me and the commit.
ideas.problem: High-risk merges (money, stock, access, import, restore) went in with no human or fresh reader of the final head, and I cannot read every line.
ideas.stands: Designed as a live trial on three merges in harness v2 phase 3; not yet run. About 3 hours [E] of my reading. Direct fit to the 5-of-6 [M] unread number.
ideas.next: Pick three high-risk merges and have the reviewer mark the hunks; log any wait against my idle hours.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Break-even rule for extra review legs
ideas.how: Claude plans and implements, Codex reviews read-only, a human decides, Claude repairs; each leg judged by a break-even formula.
ideas.problem: Different models may catch different defects, and we need a rule for when the extra review legs are worth their time.
ideas.stands: Designed from a pasted routine; never trialled. An outside study reports 91.4 vs 82.8 percent on 116 tasks [S]. Break-even inputs F=120, o=12, s=5/25/60 minutes are illustrative [I].
ideas.next: Judge any proposed review leg with the break-even formula before trialling it.

ideas.name: Verdict lists suppressions and gate-config changes
ideas.how: The reviewer's verdict lists each added inline suppression and each edit to lint, type, import or CI config with reason, checked by diff grep.
ideas.problem: I want to know when a check was made to pass by suppressing it or editing its configuration, instead of fixing the code.
ideas.stands: Suppressions sentence adopted; gate-config naming and the mechanical file list are trials over the first 5 code PRs [T]. Not yet tested; the testbed gate already refuses added skips.
ideas.next: Over 5 code PRs [T], a scripted grep must find nothing the verdict omitted; fix the path set.

ideas.name: Blast-radius touch list for a fix
ideas.how: A script lists changed functions, callers, importers, co-changing files and touching tests, and attaches the list to the reviewer's brief.
ideas.problem: Fixes introduce defects in files nobody looked at, and we want reviewers shown what a fix could touch.
ideas.stands: Designed in v2 phase 3; not yet run. Zero-token test on ten recorded fix cases: kept if six of ten [T] fall inside and the list stays within about 15 files [T].
ideas.next: Run the zero-token test on the ten recorded cases; hubs need a depth limit and grouping.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; Graph test

ideas.name: Code yields candidates, device evidence yields conclusions
ideas.how: Label each finding in_field_apk (yes, no, unknown); a field protocol, not the audit, decides what phones do; main-branch findings are candidates.
ideas.problem: Reading code on main cannot tell us what an older build does on real phones, so confident code audits can mislead.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule in orchestration design v3; not yet tested. It needs me to run the device protocol on a phone.
ideas.next: Have the geofence analysis output the field protocol that separates the top three hypotheses.

ideas.name: Skeptic verdict rules with an unverifiable outcome
ideas.how: Confirmed needs the path traced from cited lines to the failing condition; refuted needs positive counter-evidence; otherwise unverifiable, stating what would settle it.
ideas.problem: A skeptic told to refute by default can delete true claims just by saying it could not tell.
ideas.stands: Designed in orchestration design v3, replacing the default-refute framing; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Include the rules in the verdict brief.

ideas.name: Demote, never delete
ideas.how: A 'fixed' result rewrites the Opus brief to 'claimed fixed at file:line, confirm or refute' rather than removing the analyst.
ideas.problem: A cheap register check saying an item is fixed could silently drop the deep analysis of it.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule for gate G1 in the orchestration design; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Apply at gate G1.

ideas.name: Diff-restricted register check with one-hop rule
ideas.how: An item is unchanged only if neither its cited files nor files one import hop away changed; otherwise it is checked in depth.
ideas.problem: Re-auditing every old register item is expensive, but 'unchanged' can be wrong when an imported file changed.
ideas.stands: Designed in orchestration design v3 as a Sonnet high task; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Feed it the git diff outputs.

ideas.name: Claims carry a failing condition; backlog field
ideas.how: Each claim gets file:line and a failing condition; analysts report freely and park what they cannot write up in a backlog; P0 and P1 never truncated.
ideas.problem: Claims with no stated trigger cannot be checked, and caps on what analysts report hide omissions.
ideas.stands: Designed in orchestration design v3, replacing the six-claim cap per analyst; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Include in the findings brief.

ideas.name: Verify a rewrite by content, not commit message
ideas.how: After a plan rewrite, compare the actual text with the intended text instead of trusting the commit message.
ideas.problem: A rewritten plan was reported done by its commit message while content had been lost; we want to catch that before anyone builds on it.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a plan rule, drawn from the program's one recorded state loss [M]. Not measured further.
ideas.next: Apply at every plan version bump; add it to the gate checklists.

ideas.name: Adjudication record so later sessions can disagree
ideas.how: At G2 we write down the conflicts the orchestrator adjudicated and why, plus the verified register and open risks.
ideas.problem: Without the reasons kept, a later session would have to re-run everything instead of disagreeing with reasons.
ideas.stands: Designed as part of the G2 output in the orchestration design; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Write it at G2.

ideas.name: Observed chains of fixes that created defects
ideas.how: Case studies of fixes that opened new defects; proposed per-round split into old, caused-by-fix and new, with a state table per new hold.
ideas.problem: We want to understand why fixes keep opening new defects, so fix rounds converge instead of looping.
ideas.stands: Proposed from an observation record, not yet a built mechanism: one clinic fix chain, the cutoff guards RS-2 and RS-5, took three rounds [M] with a new P1 in rounds 1 and 2. No tally of fix-induced findings exists yet.
ideas.next: Record per round: old still open, new caused by the fix, new independent.

ideas.name: Record who read the final commit
ideas.how: Each merge records who read its final head; high-risk merges cannot merge on 'none' or 'own'; a finding closes only on a harness-run test.
ideas.problem: Review is all a model reading code, and 5 of 6 [M] high-risk merges went in with the final head unread; nothing records it.
ideas.stands: Proposed; testbed structure measured: round three was read only by the root for 9 of 11 [M] slice gates. Target: unread high-risk merges from 5 of 6 [M] to zero [T].
ideas.next: Add the label to the merge table, then, once D19 allows code to go out, replay seven known misses with a second model family.

ideas.name: Second model-family review pass
ideas.how: One Codex review pass and one fresh Opus pass at the frozen commits of known misses, scored on misses caught; needs the replay seal.
ideas.problem: Code that Opus writes and reviews may share blind spots; a different vendor's model might catch what a same-model reviewer misses.
ideas.stands: Deferred under decision D19: code would leave my machine and six to seven [M] known misses give only an exploratory result. Never tested; no Codex CLI here.
ideas.next: Revisit once the replay seal exists; first I would approve the vendor and sending code out.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, Clinic testbed, Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Recurring defect shapes in the reviewer brief
ideas.how: Seven recurring defect shapes, plus an eighth for any new stored copy or flag, go in the Opus refute brief, one required line each.
ideas.problem: Defect shapes we already know sit in a checklist reviewers never see, so the same kinds of defect keep coming back.
ideas.stands: Trial: moved into the ship plan's top trial 6; not yet tested. First step is a look-back test on known-defect diffs, with and without the line.
ideas.next: Run that look-back test on 3 to 4 known-defect diffs [T]; count cases caught.

ideas.name: Deviations-from-Scope report and unrequested changes
ideas.how: A journal heading reports deviations from plan; the Opus reviewer lists unaccounted hunks, boxes ticked without a diff, and changes no Scope box requires.
ideas.problem: We want to see when a diff drifts from the planned Scope, or adds unrequested abstractions, since only the implementer checks that today.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested, over the first 3 to 5 Opus-reviewed phase PRs [T]. The bottleneck compile’s refuters narrowed two of the parts to FixFlow-only.
ideas.next: Add to the reviewer brief; count deviations the journal lists against ones the reviewer finds, across three PRs [T].

ideas.name: Reviewer-brief additions with no testbed counterpart
ideas.how: A bundle of eight FixFlow reviewer items: suppression and gate-config lists, deviation report, defect shapes, gate-file list, and a design audit.
ideas.problem: We want FixFlow reviewers to catch plan deviations, unnamed config exceptions, over-engineering and design flaws that the testbed never needed to handle.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested here. The bottleneck compile’s refuters narrowed five of the items to FixFlow-only; one would add a standing step for me.
ideas.next: Use the claims-file script (mechanism 2) for the gate-file list instead.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile, after the Dex Horthy sweep

ideas.name: One cumulative-drift audit after ten PRs
ideas.how: One fresh Opus audit after the 10th merged code PR, covering the diff from the P1 merge to main.
ideas.problem: Per-PR review cannot see drift that builds across PRs, such as a helper reimplemented twice, and we want one look at the whole.
