ideas.stands: Trial, one audit only; not yet tested. Pass bar is at least 2 findings I accept [T] after the 10th merged code PR [T].
ideas.next: Run the audit and count the drift findings I accept against the bar of 2 [T].

ideas.name: Pick among candidate fixes by executed test
ideas.how: Generate three candidate fixes per recorded chain; a frozen pre-written test plus a guard-removal check rejects the candidate that causes the defect.
ideas.problem: A single fix often creates a new defect, and choosing among candidates by a test that runs may avoid that.
ideas.stands: Deferred in harness v2, not run unless switched on. Outside, on SWE-bench Lite: 25.7% by vote, 27.0% with a regression filter, 32.0% with a reproduction test [S].
ideas.next: Decide after the fix-round contract's replay (D20); live only if the selector works.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design, after SWE-bench candidate selection

ideas.name: Audit the phase routine's seven obligations
ideas.how: A fresh Opus auditor sees only artifacts (PR, git log, edit history, results, OWNER-VIEW page, closing message) and scores 7 binary obligations per phase.
ideas.problem: Compliance with the phase routine is self-reported, so skipped steps look the same as done ones.
ideas.stands: Trial over P1 and P2a; not yet tested. The source evidence was one confounded anecdote, and a count-and-split version was refuted.
ideas.next: Audit P1 and P2a against the 7 obligations; add a short skill checklist only if a step was missed.

ideas.name: Pure prompt-input boundary for the skeptic
ideas.how: A function returns only claim, evidence and failing condition, with a replay test that the rendered prompt holds no forbidden field. About 10 lines [E].
ideas.problem: The skeptic must see only the claim, evidence and failing condition, but nothing in the code stops other fields leaking into its prompt.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested, not refuted. It is hygiene: no contaminated skeptic is on record.
ideas.next: Add the function and a failing-on-leak test; I decide if hygiene alone justifies it.

ideas.name: Saved script for the PR-review stage
ideas.how: One committed workflow script takes the register ids and head commit, calls the PR-reviewer agent with a verdict schema, and compares commits in code.
ideas.problem: The PR-review stage is prose steps, so commit binding and the per-id fail-and-pass table depend on the agent, and workflows get rewritten each time.
ideas.stands: Trial after P1; not yet tested. Only the deterministic part is to be scripted; the whole-routine version was refuted.
ideas.next: Run prose review in P1 and audit it, then use the script on the next 3 PRs [T].

ideas.name: Record-only rule checks over returned objects
ideas.how: A node script over the committed evidence JSON checks quote length, listed URLs, unique ids and evidence format, run record-only with no retry.
ideas.problem: Agent outputs are checked by judges or by eye; cheap rule checks could catch violations the gates missed without spending tokens.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested; downgraded from adopt. The refuter's naive pattern flagged 174 of 707 evidence strings [M], mostly legitimate, so the allow-list is the work.
ideas.next: Write it with an allow-list (about an hour [E]); adopt only if it finds a real missed violation.

ideas.name: List dimensions and covered combinations in review briefs
ideas.how: Add a line asking the reviewer to list the dimensions of the change and the combinations the tests cover, in the next 3 briefs [T].
ideas.problem: Defects can hide in combinations of changes that no test covers, as in BAML's own post-mortem.
ideas.stands: Parked: the refuter found one post-mortem is thin evidence, our briefs already name similar shapes, and the trial had no control.
ideas.next: Would return if several of our defects trace to uncovered combinations.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a BAML post-mortem

ideas.name: Agents audit run transcripts for wasted calls
ideas.how: An Opus pass reads the six lane transcripts and lists wasted calls and ignored rules; I or the orchestrator triage.
ideas.problem: We wondered whether briefs waste calls or ignore their own rules without anyone seeing it.
ideas.stands: Parked: the refuter found recorded quota failures came from fan-out size and effort, not waste inside agents; fixed overhead dominates. The earlier transcript audit found nothing that caused a mistake.
ideas.next: Would return if a transcript audit shows waste that caused a failure.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a talk on agent testing

ideas.name: Six-claim cap per analyst
ideas.how: Version 2 capped each analyst at six claims; version 3 replaced it with a backlog field and kept only the verification cap.
ideas.problem: We did not want caps on what analysts report to hide omissions.
ideas.stands: Parked: superseded in orchestration design v3 by the backlog field, after an external reviewer's objection that six findings per analyst hide omissions.
ideas.next: None; replaced by the backlog field.

ideas.name: Materiality skeptic and 1-in-5 sample
ideas.how: Two extra verification layers from the first design: a skeptic judging materiality and a one-in-five sample; the v2 rewrite removed both.
ideas.problem: We wanted extra assurance on findings, but the added layers cost spend without moving the plan.
ideas.stands: Parked: removed in orchestration design v2 because the layers added spend without moving the plan. Severity is now re-set by the main session at gate G2.
ideas.next: None.

ideas.name: Numbered evidence ids for verifiers
ideas.how: Evidence handed to verifiers and skeptics is numbered; they cite ids and the script rejects unknown ids.
ideas.problem: We worried a verifier could cite a fabricated URL or quote.
ideas.stands: Parked: it conflicts with the design, where a refuted verdict needs counter-evidence the skeptic finds itself, and the citation check already catches fabrication. No fabricated URL on record.
ideas.next: Would return if a fabricated URL shows up in a verification step.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a talk on short ids

themes.title: Planning parallel work
themes.covers: Running several lanes at once: footprints, collisions, how many lanes are worth it, waves, the coordinator and lane sessions.
intro: More lanes help only until the first limit is reached, the knee. Past it they add queues, tokens and collisions. In the testbed, ten lanes run at once hit the usage limit within about 15 minutes [M], while two at a time got further.

The ideas here decide before a wave starts which slices can run side by side, how many lanes are worth it and where they would collide. Since 13 November FixFlow’s ship plan runs a coordinator session with one lane session per phase, so this theme is moving from design into daily use.

ideas.name: Per-checkout isolation of worktree, port and database
ideas.how: Each checkout gets its own worktree, branch, compose project, port and path-hashed database; a second check of it is refused.
ideas.problem: Parallel sessions collided on branches, ports and test databases; two runs of one checkout dropped each other's test database.
ideas.stands: In use (testbed): supported 432 commits and 65 merges in eight working days [M]. A recorded failure: 115 errors [M]; 19 worktrees exist [M]; one database container per checkout.
ideas.next: Consider one shared database container with per-checkout databases; add a dry-run reaper for finished checkouts.

ideas.name: Lane sessions: one phase, own worktree, run together
ideas.how: Each lane is one Opus-led session in its own worktree off origin/main; one phase, one draft PR titled with the phase id.
ideas.problem: Version 8 ran one phase at a time, so for twelve days [M] no code phase started, because each waited behind my first phase.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow: eight lane sessions started 2026-11-13 [M], and PRs #187-#192 opened that day [M]. RAM, not CPU, sets the ceiling [M]; the wave plan has four waves [E].
ideas.next: Start wave B as soon as a wave-A PR is review-passed.

ideas.name: Build ahead by classifying each Entry clause
ideas.how: Class each Entry clause: code, value, deploy or evidence. Only code delays a build, and the lane stacks on the other phase's reviewed tip.
ideas.problem: Entry lines mixed code, value, deploy and evidence conditions, so every code phase waited for my work even when it could be built.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow: four phases built ahead on 2026-11-13 (P7a, P6a, P9-0a, P12a) [M]; none merged yet. It could free the queue behind P0a for 15+ code phases [E].
ideas.next: Rebase stacks with git rebase --onto origin/main after each squash merge.

ideas.name: Waves of parallel slices from the plan
ideas.how: Waves follow the plan's dependency graph: slice-owned apps and migration numbers, frozen shared vocabulary, own database and port per branch, root holding merge order.
ideas.problem: We need slices to run in parallel safely, never by guess, in an order that empties the queue, without migration or port collisions and within RAM.
ideas.stands: In use: clinic testbed waves 0-5 (S00 on 3 Nov, waves 3-4 done 4 Nov, wrap-up 10 Nov) [M], no serial comparison. FixFlow wave A started eight sessions on 2026-11-13 [M].
ideas.next: Start wave B when a wave-A PR is review-passed; keep a database per branch and frozen contracts before fan-out.

ideas.name: File ownership per lane with named shared files
ideas.how: A table gives each lane its folders. No two lanes edit one file in a wave, except listed shared files, each with a conflict rule.
ideas.problem: Parallel lanes editing the same files in the same wave cause rebase conflicts and lost work.
ideas.stands: In use: in force for wave A; review findings added shared files such as CLAUDE.md, config.py, conftest.py and specs.py. No conflict count recorded yet.
ideas.next: Watch the first rebases of P6a after P1.

ideas.name: Cross-lane contracts fixed in advance
ideas.how: The plan fixes shared values now: origin header, verdict fixture file, sorted telemetry events array, queue-discard and drain-manifest events, sampler event names.
ideas.problem: Lanes that depend on each other's outputs would otherwise wait on each other or guess names, headers and fixtures.
ideas.stands: In use: the contract values are fixed in the ship plan, section 7.3. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: P6a creates the shared contract files; P5a and P6b-2 then consume them.

ideas.name: Migration-numbering rule across parallel slices
ideas.how: One slice session at a time writes an app's migrations; a second branch regenerates after the merge; a graph test enforces one head.
ideas.problem: Parallel slices pick the same database migration number and collide.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed; it serialises per app. No collision count was recorded, so we have no measured effect.
ideas.next: One writer per wave; keep the single-head test. FixFlow's next free slot is 0047.

ideas.name: Flow limits for loops and work in progress
ideas.how: One open PR per loop; actors limited to safe directories with batch caps; widen frequency or batch only after clean review.
ideas.problem: Automated loops can flood review with parallel PRs, overrun review capacity, or touch unsafe areas.
ideas.stands: In use: the Dex Horthy sweep’s assessment found our work-in-progress bounds already in the ship plan and orchestration rules. We run no scheduled agent loops, so the one-PR-per-loop rule waits until we do. No measurement defined.
ideas.next: Keep the existing bounds; apply the one-PR-per-loop rule if we add scheduled loops.

ideas.name: PR title as resume key, with a lane board
ideas.how: Each PR title starts with its phase id and the body names the branch; a lane board maps phase, session, branch, PR and state.
ideas.problem: After a stop or crash we could not tell which session, branch and PR belong to which phase when branch names differ from the plan.
ideas.stands: In use: the lane board had 10 rows on 2026-11-13 [M], and all eight lanes resumed from their worktrees after the power loss [M].
ideas.next: Keep the board updated as lanes finish.

ideas.name: Bounded session tree: depth three, fan-out three
ideas.how: Root holds the board; slice leads, children and subagents sit below; at most three running children per node; each node owns one file set.
ideas.problem: A large build needs structure so many sessions run without losing work, colliding on files, flooding the reviewing parent or exhausting the shared session limit.
ideas.stands: In use (testbed): 12 slices and about 20 follow-up branches merged in 8 days [M]. No comparison with another structure; root became a serial gate; board reached 219,111 bytes [M] at sweep time.
ideas.next: Move the board off one 219 KB file; reuse file-disjoint ownership and merge-upward order for FixFlow lanes.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; adapted from FixFlow's tier guide

ideas.name: Merge-hold list for built-ahead PRs
ideas.how: A table names reviewed PRs kept draft and unmerged until a stated point, such as P4c done or every phone on v2.
ideas.problem: Until P4c deploys main HEAD, merging is not deploying; building ahead could ship half-finished mobile or accounting work into the fleet APK or drain window.
ideas.stands: Designed in the ship plan; rule accepted, held PRs not yet reviewed, so not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check each PR against the list before merging.

ideas.name: Lanes report; the coordinator writes program files
ideas.how: A lane never edits the program folder or the OWNER-VIEW page. Its closing message carries its deploy-train row and any plan defect; the coordinator records both.
ideas.problem: Many lanes editing the program documents at once would collide and bury my single view of progress.
ideas.stands: Adopted in the ship plan and in force for all lanes; it replaces the earlier rule that a lane amends the file in its own PR. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check that the first lane closing message carries the deploy-train row.

ideas.name: Planner that sizes lanes just below the knee
ideas.how: Before work starts, set the knee at the lowest limit (check, review, merge, tokens, memory) divided by one lane's rate; run 0.8 [S] of it.
ideas.problem: We chose how many parallel sessions to run by feel. Past the lowest limit, extra lanes only add queues, tokens and collisions, not speed.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; plan accepted 11 Nov, nothing installed. In the model, lanes past the knee only wait [I]. The testbed had about three lanes worth running [M] but ran six to nine [M].
ideas.next: Measure check and review times in phases 2-3; the planner then recomputes lane counts for each plan.

ideas.name: Plan check with footprints and collision graphs
ideas.how: Each slice declares its footprint and needs. We build needs and collides graphs, refuse two writers of one file, and feed real touches back.
ideas.problem: Nothing checked parallel slices for collisions; the first checks on merged main failed for the first two slices, from hand edits to shared documents.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; the written spec has all 8 steps but has not been run on a real plan. The testbed never used footprints, so no real plan can be replayed; the sample plan is made up.
ideas.next: Add the plan-check section to the orchestration document when I say so; run the touch-list test on ten recorded cases.

ideas.name: Scheduler that releases two sessions at a time
ideas.how: Turn the wave plan into sessions, release two at a time, park waiting slices outside any session, and bring sessions back after a stop.
ideas.problem: After a stop every session was released at once and waited together, holding context and burning tokens. One check waited 2,030 s [M].
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 with the resume list; I answered D06. In the record, two at a time got further: 18 of 48 agents done [M], a lean run 30 of 31 [M].
ideas.next: Build it with the resume list in phase 1; a waiting lane then burns nothing in the model [I].
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; answer to the 9 November mass release

ideas.name: No undeclared splits of a one-PR phase
ideas.how: One-PR phases stay one PR: P3a-2 is not started early, stub and heartbeat stay in P3a, P6a's web half keeps its own PR.
ideas.problem: Splitting a one-PR phase across lanes would touch the runbook and ci.yml ahead of their owners and make cherry-picks onto the release branch conflict.
ideas.stands: Adopted in the ship plan; P3a-2 was never launched. Not yet tested beyond that.
ideas.next: State any split in the plan before a lane starts one.

ideas.name: Gates in their own phase, long agents first
ideas.how: Long gates issue first in a separate Gates phase readers do not wait on; their writes are disjoint from what readers read.
ideas.problem: Test and build gates run 25 to 40 minutes [E] and must not block or collide with the reader agents.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design as part of the first workflow's contract; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Time the gates alongside readers in that first workflow.

ideas.name: READY signal: gh pr ready plus coordinator watcher
ideas.how: A lane that reports READY also marks its PR ready for review; a coordinator watcher polls that flag and wakes the binding review.
ideas.problem: The coordinator needs to know a lane is done without polling sessions or being messaged mid-turn, since messages arrive only when a lane's turn ends.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule in the ship plan; no READY has been recorded yet, so not yet tested.
ideas.next: Run the watcher when the first lane finishes.

ideas.name: Governor that slows lanes to last the window
ideas.how: Share = what the window can still carry ÷ what lanes would burn, from measured tokens per lane-hour; lanes slow instead of stopping.
ideas.problem: At the five-hour window's limit every lane stops at once; we had 14 limit episodes in October [M].
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2, to be built in phase 5 after the baseline. One window covered about 3.4 million subagent tokens [M]; subagents caused 91 of 104 limit errors [M].
ideas.next: Set the written budget from the one measured window (D07), then rerun it on November's tally.

ideas.name: Knowledge-store phases yield to ship phases
ideas.how: A store session starts only when no ship phase waits on Opus, or I spend spare quota; one that hits a usage limit yields.
ideas.problem: Knowledge-store sessions would compete with ship phases for Opus usage and for my attention, and I want no store phase to delay shipping.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design, as a rule for every store phase; not yet tested. KS-6a and KS-6b share the one Docker-gate slot.
ideas.next: Apply it at each store phase start.

ideas.name: Pipelined verification as each analyst finishes
ideas.how: Citation checks start as each analyst finishes, not after all are done; the fleet drain analyst runs pipelined after an earlier one.
ideas.problem: Waiting for all analysts before checking leaves wall-clock time idle, and we want the same checks to finish sooner.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design as part of the second workflow script's shape; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Implement it in the second workflow script and time it.

ideas.name: Orchestration as a distributed B+ tree: split, merge on context
ideas.how: Sessions form a distributed B+ tree: inner ones hold routing keys, leaves hold the work. A session passing about 40 % [S] of its window splits; small siblings merge.
ideas.problem: The orchestrator’s window grows until it must compact or clear, and the summary loses state: hallucination, re-read tokens and one overloaded root.
ideas.stands: Rule written and replayed over 97 [M] recorded session windows on 14 November; not tested live. 72, 32 and 26 [M] of them passed lines of 300k, 400k and 500k, holding 65.1, 44.6 and 36.8 % [M] of what sessions re-read. On tokens the record does not settle it against compacting earlier: 1.05–1.06 times on the middle of three sets of assumed costs with the work split evenly, 0.53–1.24 across all nine cases (each set with the work split evenly, unevenly or not at all) [E]. It writes 1.3–1.6 briefs for each summary an earlier compaction would write [E]. Hand-over quality is untested.
ideas.next: I said yes to one trial wave at 300k. First D07, then a reader’s check of the latest state on our recorded summaries.
ideas.origin: My idea, from database and distributed-systems study

themes.title: Spend fewer tokens per result
themes.covers: Where the tokens go and how to spend fewer: long windows, the fixed start of every agent, lookups, compaction, model tiers and one written budget.
intro: We counted every model call on this PC for both projects: 35,834 calls and 7.35 billion context tokens [M]. 97 % of those tokens were re-reads of a window the model had already read [M], so the number of calls times the size of the window is what we have to manage.

The ideas here are the four levers the token report found, the governor and the written budget of harness v2, and smaller habits that keep windows short. Each lever is sized as an exposure, the share of tokens it could touch, which tells us where to aim; the savings themselves are what the next measurements will show.

ideas.name: One phase per new session, state in repo
ideas.how: Each phase starts in a fresh session; state lives in the repo and draft PR body; lead sessions compact earlier.
ideas.problem: Late calls in long sessions re-read everything before them, up to 944k [M] tokens per call, and the main window is our largest token cost.
ideas.stands: In use in part: the ruling is in force and state lives in the repo; the 150-200k [T] cap is not yet applied. Slice sessions hold 66.4% [M] of tokens; saving untested.
ideas.next: Pick the cap (150k or 200k), start P0a fresh, then compare the share of calls past 200k.
ideas.origin: Harness review; Harness v2 design; Token report

ideas.name: Earlier auto-compact window of 400,000 tokens
ideas.how: Set autoCompactWindow to 400,000 [S] so compaction fires near 367k [S]; trial it on one wave of Sonnet slice sessions and check one summary.
ideas.problem: Long sessions carry huge contexts: 39.8% [M] of November's cache-read tokens were in calls past 400k, and we want later calls smaller.
ideas.stands: In use for Opus, whose sessions compact near 367k: 38 of 48 [M] compactions came at 366-387k, all on Opus; by 14 November 84 of the 117 [M] in session windows were Opus, 81 [M] of them at 366-385k. Sonnet ran to 963k [M] and is not set. What a compaction loses is unmeasured.
ideas.next: Set the window for one wave of Sonnet slice sessions, confirm it fires near 367k, and check one summary.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; Bottleneck compile; Harness review

ideas.name: Short, capped agent hand-backs
ideas.how: Agents return capped text, about 2,500 [S] characters with path:line evidence; noisy output goes to files; drops are logged, never silent.
ideas.problem: The main session fills with whole-document reads and long subagent reports, and we believed subagent writes were refused, so reports had to pass through it.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed as a returns-as-text rule; the hygiene rules file is built but not installed. No token figures. Partly replaced by reports on disk.
ideas.next: Apply the 2,500 [S] character hand-back rule in FixFlow briefs; check logged drop counts after W1.

ideas.name: Run small tasks inline before spawning agents
ideas.how: Counts, greps, hashes and git logs run inline and pass to agents as arguments; claims batch per verifier; discovery agents return facts, not verdicts.
ideas.problem: Every subagent pays about 7.5k [E] tokens of project instructions before working, so tiny tasks and per-claim agents cost more than they return.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed (cap sizes never quantified) and applied in the orchestration design v2. The overhead figure is approximate; no token figures yet.
ideas.next: Measure per-agent prefix tokens in the first run; run the pre-flight once Docker Desktop is started.

ideas.name: One token budget: two lanes at a time
ideas.how: Budget subagent tokens per window before launch; run two lanes at a time; write every step to disk; stop after the first empty result, which can signal a usage limit.
ideas.problem: Adding fresh reviewers, gate workflows and replays could recreate limit stops; a 10-lane run hit the five-hour limit in about 15 [M] minutes.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic; harness v2 applies it from phase 1. One window covered about 3.4M [M] subagent tokens, about 14% [M] of the weekly limit. Budget figure not yet set.
ideas.next: Set the written budget figure from the measured window (D07).

ideas.name: No PreCompact hook; keep idle compaction on
ideas.how: Add no PreCompact hook and no context-system install; leave Claude Code's idle compaction (default on, 200k threshold [S]) as it is.
ideas.problem: We had to decide how much compaction machinery to add, if any.
ideas.stands: In use as a binding ruling: a PreCompact hook can only block a compaction, and custom compaction instructions are not applied to automatic compaction. Idle compaction took 34 ms [M] and dropped one open loop (an unfinished thread of work).
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Lead implements the Opus work itself
ideas.how: In a lane, the Opus lead implements the Opus-owned work; Sonnet subagents get tests, screens, read models, infra files and runbooks.
ideas.problem: A long-lived orchestrator window that only briefs others was the largest measured token cost of the program, and every hand-off loses context.
ideas.stands: In use: applied to every lane started 2026-11-13. Its reason is measured (largest token cost [M]); the effect of the change itself is untested.
ideas.next: Compare lane token use with the earlier orchestrator-led runs.

ideas.name: Session-local file read cache
ideas.how: Cache file reads inside a session so a repeat read returns the earlier content instead of a new copy.
ideas.problem: We wondered whether agents re-open files they already read in the same window and so waste tokens.
ideas.stands: Tested against the token record, not built: exact repeats are 0.00 % [M], and content seen before in the window is 0.5-1.5 % [M]. ‘Opened again’ is mostly a different range of the same file.
ideas.next: None needed; it would save almost nothing [E], so we skip it.

ideas.name: Route by model tier, window and price
ideas.how: Pick the model by window size as well as by its token rate; spend Opus at xhigh only where evidence is thin; verify only where it moves a decision.
ideas.problem: A cheaper model with a bigger window can cost more tokens through larger re-read contexts, and routing alone does not cut the token count.
ideas.stands: Measured: Opus 65% [M] of calls and 52% [M] of tokens; Fable 6.5% [M] and 16% [M]; Sonnet 28% [M] and 32% [M]. Routing changes the rate, not the count.
ideas.next: Keep routing for quality and rate; weigh window size with the compaction trial; review after W2 spend.
ideas.origin: Token report; Harness v2 design; Orchestration design

ideas.name: Compact context packet for fresh agents
ideas.how: Freeze the required facts, build a smaller packet, count bytes at delivery including preparation, and require that a deliberately removed fact is rejected.
ideas.problem: We hand fresh agents large documents and want to know whether a smaller, fact-checked packet gives the same result with fewer bytes and faster work.
ideas.stands: Clinic testbed, small synthetic cases: bytes 10,010 to 7,947 [M], 20.6% fewer [M], 24 of 24 facts kept [M]; same acceptance, 193.1 vs 194.7 min [M]; no gain shown.
ideas.next: Reuse the method only: freeze facts, count bytes including preparation, reject any lost fact.

ideas.name: Compaction audit and count
ideas.how: An Opus audit of a live transcript measures each compaction; a search for compaction records counts them in the clinic root session.
ideas.problem: I feared compaction silently loses data and wastes tokens, and we did not know how often the orchestrator window overflowed.
ideas.stands: Review session: 971k to 22k in 131 s, 580k to 12k in 34 ms [M]; nothing lost caused rework. Clinic root: 3 compactions at 573,774, 974,246 and 967,210 tokens [M].
ideas.next: Re-run if a phase session passes 500k tokens [T]; restore declared task sections or split the board.

ideas.name: Codex adapter for snapshot and restore
ideas.how: Hooks save a checksummed snapshot before compaction and restore it after, with a search journal, under byte budgets; failure falls back to native.
ideas.problem: After the window is summarised, details are lost; we tried heavier machinery on a Codex-based project to see whether it beats native compaction.
ideas.stands: Tested in the clinic testbed: recall 15 of 15 and task success equal in all arms; tokens +6.1% over a notes file and +17.0% over native [M]. Nothing showed a saving.
ideas.next: Use a short notes file; reuse the engineering rules; revisit only if a case shows recall loss.

ideas.name: Plain-file immutable snapshot storage
ideas.how: One immutable checksummed file per snapshot, meta file written last as the commit point, recall by linear scan with no index or database.
ideas.problem: Memory tools often need a database; we wanted durable snapshots with no dependency and with tamper evidence.
ideas.stands: Clinic testbed: scan of 115 MB in about 1 s [M]; multi-process stress gave 464 events and 464 snapshots, exact [M]. No cost curve at larger sizes was found.
ideas.next: Reuse the commit-point pattern for any FixFlow checkpoint store.

ideas.name: Reading rules: grep first, then ranged reads
ideas.how: Never read a file over 300 [S] lines whole: grep the symbol, then read a range; follow imports one hop and list extra files read.
ideas.problem: Agents read whole large files and cite facts they never saw, so spend is invisible and evidence is second-hand.
ideas.stands: Built into the Android analyst, appsec, migration and explorer agent definitions; the design rule came in v3. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Audit the first W2 outputs for extra-file lists.

ideas.name: Read admission: first page plus outline
ideas.how: A hook rewrites a Read over 30,000 [S] bytes to the first 16 KB [S] plus an outline of up to 60 [S] entries.
ideas.problem: Reading a whole large file into the window costs tokens that stay there for the rest of the session.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed and unit-tested only; not installed, so no measured effect. Forensics show most window growth is the model's own output, which this gate does not touch.
ideas.next: Trial on the current Claude Code version and measure tokens saved per session.

ideas.name: Compaction snapshot, restore and recall hooks
ideas.how: Python hooks lower the trigger to 400k [S], snapshot declared task sections before compaction, restore them verbatim after, and offer exact-text recall over transcripts.
ideas.problem: Long sessions grow past 700k tokens [E], and their summaries can drop decisions; we want 300-400k [T] active tokens to carry an 800k [T] history.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed, never run live: 85 offline tests [M], 53 defects fixed [M], recall over 115 MB in about 1 s [M]. Restore quality not measured.
ideas.next: Keep it in its own repository; reuse its rules for any FixFlow checkpoint. A live A/B is needed first.

ideas.name: Cached Expo package sources instead of npm install
ideas.how: Pinned Expo sources are cached on disk; fall back to npm pack of the exact version, then unpkg; never the branch head.
ideas.problem: To answer native Android questions we would otherwise need an install or a network fetch, and the branch head is not the pinned version.
ideas.stands: Built in the orchestration design: the doc says the sources are already cached. Not yet tested. No install or native prebuild is needed or allowed for these questions.
ideas.next: Point the two named research steps at the cache.

ideas.name: Pull-only lookups with a 2,000-character cap
ideas.how: Nothing is pushed into context; a lookup returns one lead and one candidate within 2,000 characters [S], mid-window so the prompt cache survives.
ideas.problem: Fetched content is about 27-28.5% [E] of context and gets re-read many times; always-loaded lessons tax every call.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge store (KS-2); untested. 2,000 characters cost about 860 tokens [M]. Prompt caching already works: in the design’s sample, 98.2% [M] of context was cache reads.
ideas.next: Build the cap in KS-2, run the zero-token index replay, and log cost per lookup with cache reads.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design; Harness review rulings; Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Reports on disk: path, hash and short summary
ideas.how: After a 15-minute write probe, agents write full reports to one allowed folder and return a path, hash and short summary.
ideas.problem: Long subagent reports pass through the orchestrator's context, which averaged about 499k [M] per call; we want that window smaller.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3. A background subagent wrote and read back a file with no prompt [M]. Target: zero refused writes over 20 [T] runs. Not tested at volume.
ideas.next: Run the 15-minute write probe in the clinic's default mode; I decide if agents may write to one folder (D13).

ideas.name: No waiting inside a session
ideas.how: Park a waiting slice, and run the check in the background instead of a foreground polling loop.
ideas.problem: A waiting lane keeps its context and burns tokens; recorded waits had a median of 409 s [M] and a longest of 2,030 s [M].
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 2; not yet tested. A parked lane would burn nothing in the model [I].
ideas.next: Build the heartbeat and background checks in phase 2.

ideas.name: Keep Haiku prompts under about 100k tokens
ideas.how: Keep each Haiku extraction prompt under about 100k [S] input tokens and split large dumps; use Haiku only for literal extraction into typed schemas.
ideas.problem: Past a certain input size Haiku's price steps up, which removes its cost advantage on large dumps.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule in the orchestration design's tier table; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check the three Haiku extraction prompt sizes against the limit.

ideas.name: Net-zero CLAUDE.md edit, then trim
ideas.how: Rewrite CI row in place, adding no line; after the pilot, keep each rule sentence plus a store id and move diagnostics to entries.
ideas.problem: CLAUDE.md is loaded by every agent every session and must stay honest, yet the knowledge store adds a runtime that CLAUDE.md's own rule says to document.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; not run. Trim waits for a pilot go, one verified entry at a time. Line counts before and after go in the trim's PR body.
ideas.next: Make the net-zero edit now; the trim waits for the pilot (decision KS-D11).

ideas.name: Strip fixed prefix with a short tool list
ideas.how: Short tool list that always keeps Write, deferred tool schemas, fewer connectors and no skills for gate agents; adopt only after a with-and-without test.
ideas.problem: Every agent pays about 70,000 tokens [M] before any work, re-read on every call; fan-out multiplies this prefix, not the work.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 5; not run. Tool definitions are 34k [M] of the 70,000 [M] each agent pays. Pass bar: 20 runs [T], zero refused writes.
ideas.next: Take one context reading with and without the list, then run a sample of agents and tally prefix tokens.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; Dex Horthy sweep; Token report

ideas.name: Cost envelope by stage
ideas.how: A table of agents per stage and tier mix, from sixteen [S] first-wave agents down to none at gates.
ideas.problem: Running many agents multiplies tokens, so we want an order-of-magnitude spend expectation before we start.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design: orders of magnitude only, no actual spend recorded. The second-wave analysts are stated to be the main spend.
ideas.next: Record actual tokens per stage after the run and compare with the table.

ideas.name: Batch lookups into one command
ideas.how: Put two or more reads or searches in one command or one parallel tool-call block, so one re-read serves several lookups.
ideas.problem: 58% [M] of our calls only read or search, and each one re-reads the whole window.
ideas.stands: Idea from the token report, ranked third; untested. Batching two lookups would remove about a third of all calls [E] and a third of their re-reads [E].
ideas.next: Add a batch-lookups rule to agent briefs and compare calls per task; it could cut about a third [E] of calls.

ideas.name: Write big files by script; compact after writing
ideas.how: Write large files through a script instead of inline tool content, and compact after a write-heavy phase so written text stops riding along.
ideas.problem: The model's thinking, echoed commands and written files stay in the window and are re-read on every call: 31% [E] of clinic tokens.
ideas.stands: Idea from the token report, ranked fourth; untested. Own earlier output is 26% [E] of all context tokens, and 31% [E] in the clinic.
ideas.next: Add 'script big files, then compact' to briefs; 31% [E] of clinic tokens is carried own output.

ideas.name: Quiet gate wrapper for web and mobile
ideas.how: Extend the backend wrapper (log to file, one EXIT line, counts) to web and mobile gates if one green run shows output worth cutting.
ideas.problem: Verbose lint, test and build output floods an agent's window; the backend gate is already quiet but web and mobile are not.
ideas.stands: Not yet tried for web and mobile: the backend wrapper is in use, and the extension is a trial planned over the first two code phases. FixFlow only; the clinic check already has a wrapper.
ideas.next: Record characters/4 per gate; drop it if a full green run is at or below 3k [T] tokens.

ideas.name: CLAUDE.md names noisy commands and quiet wrappers
ideas.how: CLAUDE.md lists the noisy raw commands as off-limits and pairs each with its quiet wrapper.
ideas.problem: Raw noisy commands flood the window, and a bare prohibition gives the agent no alternative.
ideas.stands: Deferred: it sat over the per-group cap, so no refuter verdict; reviewers split between trial and skip, and it would lengthen CLAUDE.md. No measurement defined yet.
ideas.next: Run a refuter pass and define a measurement before deciding.

ideas.name: Model-keyed window for the Fable session
ideas.how: If a phase session passes 500k [S], add autoCompactWindow 500000 [S] for the Fable model beside the Opus entry in user settings.
ideas.problem: My 400,000 [S] window names only the Opus model, so it does not apply to the Fable session.
ideas.stands: Deferred: not set now; set only if a phase session passes 500k [S]. The setting mismatch is confirmed [M]; the effect of a Fable setting is untested.
ideas.next: Watch phase session size.

ideas.name: Resume-pointer hook after compaction
ideas.how: A SessionStart hook with matcher compact prints the branch, short sha, resume pointer and last three commits into context.
ideas.problem: After a mid-phase compaction the session may not know its branch, recent commits or where to resume.
ideas.stands: Deferred: not tested. One phase per session makes compaction rare, so the exact settings text is kept for later. Open checks: path expansion on Windows; it also fires after subagent compactions.
ideas.next: Install only if a phase session compacts mid-phase.

ideas.name: Trim skill and agent descriptions to 400 characters
ideas.how: Trim each of the 13 skill and 11 agent descriptions to at most 400 characters [T]: key use case first, one do-not clause.
ideas.problem: About 24k characters [E] of skill and agent descriptions load into every session's context, using tokens we want for work.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet run. The disable-flag half was refuted because it blocks subagent preload. Target: combined skill and agent lines fall by at least 50% [T] with nothing mis-triggering.
ideas.next: Compare /context before and after in a fresh session, plus a routing check; an hour-long trial.

ideas.name: Shape CLAUDE.md and skill descriptions
ideas.how: Narrow triggers on conditional CLAUDE.md blocks; directory files for single-runtime rules; trimmed descriptions with a routing check; a contradiction sweep; model-change adherence tests.
ideas.problem: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md and about 24k characters [E] of skill and agent descriptions may load more than needed or contradict each other.
ideas.stands: Trial, FixFlow only; not yet tested. The testbed's context trials were null, and no bottleneck is about the instructions file being missed.
ideas.next: Run the context-file experiment (E1) on FixFlow.

ideas.name: Cross-session digests of hot, often-read files
ideas.how: Keep a durable short digest of the most-read files that stands in for reading their lines, lasting across sessions.
ideas.problem: About a quarter of our tokens are fetched file content, and a small set of files is re-read across sessions while questions rarely repeat.
ideas.stands: Idea; digest untested. 72 paths (3.3% [E]) hold half the fetched tokens; paths read in 5+ windows hold 73% [E]. Estimated saving 5-24% [E] after refuters cut a 42% claim.
ideas.next: Build digests for the 72 hot paths and test whether answers stay correct.

ideas.name: Log context use at phase close
ideas.how: Log tokens, percent and compactions at phase close, checked against one transcript; over 5 phases [T] add peak context and correction positions.
ideas.problem: The 500k [T] context trigger has no sensor, and we do not know whether a fuller orchestrator window degrades its judgements; the advice to keep context under about 40 % of the window is anecdotal.
ideas.stands: Trial; not yet run. A near-free instrument that grounds the context ceiling in data, starting with a usage line (tokens, percent, compactions) on the first 4 [T] phase sessions.
ideas.next: Compare the recorded figure with the transcript for one session, then record peak context over 5 phases.

ideas.name: Library as a session's external memory
ideas.how: Keep what a session learned in the library and fetch it on demand, instead of carrying it in the window or a summary.
ideas.problem: Huge windows and lossy summaries both cost: the long-lived window is over half of all tokens [M], and compaction losses are unmeasured.
ideas.stands: An idea and use case from the library review; not measured and no fix agreed. Compaction dropped a fetched entry in 1 [M] case, while 4 [M] went the other way.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list before choosing any fix.

ideas.name: Outside tools that cap tool output
ideas.how: Static review of 19 [M] pinned outside repos: hooks that redirect reads, stub large outputs, rewrite results, or a proxy with a read lifecycle.
ideas.problem: We want a shipped tool that bounds what tool outputs add to the window, or trims repeated reads.
ideas.stands: Parked: none passed as a complete remedy and none installed; no efficacy measured. One maintainer claims about 50% [S] savings, not reproduced. Bypass list and stub-plus-retrieve design kept.
ideas.next: Use the bypass list to design a FixFlow output-capping hook; trial Bash output filtering and a Read gate with outline.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; outside projects (CCH, Headroom, squeez)

ideas.name: Project admission contract and ledger
ideas.how: Split resident input from tool admission; keep a ledger of bytes entering by route; planned test: 3 arms, 3 resumes, 2 repetitions [S].
ideas.problem: Runs refilled the window from about 700k [S] to 800k [S] after a state file and new chat; saved state does not control what tools admit.
ideas.stands: Parked: the clinic research's framing was withdrawn on 2026-10-09 and replaced by the context-system research. The 700k and 800k figures are user-reported; nothing was measured.
ideas.next: Reuse the ingress checklist and the resident-versus-admission split for a FixFlow session-size guard.

ideas.name: Context-size limit, split prompts, trimmed MCP tools
ideas.how: Restart at about 100k tokens [S]; split prompts of 50-85 instructions [S]; pick MCP tools per need; repeat key instructions at start and end.
ideas.problem: Models seem to degrade in very long contexts, long prompts skip steps, and MCP tool definitions use context we want for work.
ideas.stands: Parked: anecdotal. The author withdrew the flat 100k [S] figure in September 2026 and says experts go to 200-400k [S]. One MCP server costs about 5.7k tokens [S].
ideas.next: None.

ideas.name: Compact Instructions section for the summarizer
ideas.how: Add a Compact Instructions section that tells the automatic summarizer what to keep.
ideas.problem: Automatic compaction summaries can get the latest state wrong, and we hoped instructions to the summarizer would improve them.
ideas.stands: Parked: not tested. Native support for such a section is unverified and it adds per-agent overhead, so the harness review ruled to skip it.
ideas.next: Revisit only if native support is verified.

ideas.name: Test CONTEXT-block variants against each other
ideas.how: Run one task with current and trimmed CONTEXT blocks, three runs each; trim if no worse and at least 15% [T] cheaper.
ideas.problem: We never tested whether the CONTEXT block given to every agent is longer than needed and wastes tokens.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted before running. The block is a few hundred tokens [E] against a start above 63k [M], so a 15% [T] saving cannot be reached.
ideas.next: None.

ideas.name: Survey of outside memory and context tools
ideas.how: A source-pinned audit of about 20 outside tools against one need (800k [T] history in a 300-400k [T] window); no installs or trials.
ideas.problem: We wanted to know whether an existing hook, proxy or memory store could be adopted instead of building one.
ideas.stands: Parked: none adopted; local hooks were built instead. Vendor figures only, not reproduced: MemTree 68.7 vs full history 69.3 vs native compact 48.7 [S].
ideas.next: Use as design vocabulary; run our own A/B if needed, with Cairn as a comparator for cross-session memory.

ideas.name: Cairn: SQLite memory and tool paring
ideas.how: Each reply ends with a structured block that a hook stores in one SQLite file for later sessions; a proxy drops unused tool definitions.
ideas.problem: Carry memory across sessions and cut tool-definition overhead.
ideas.stands: Parked: audited from source only; not adopted or trialled, nothing measured.
ideas.next: Keep as a comparator for semantic cross-session memory.

ideas.name: Standing per-stage token and cost tracking
ideas.how: Attribute tokens and cost per stage, agent and model from recorded counts at pinned rates; use tokens per solve as a codebase-health signal.
ideas.problem: We cannot see spend per stage, agent and model, so it is hard to find where tokens are wasted.
ideas.stands: Parked: the evidence was vendor claims, one anecdote and a hypothesis. It would also reopen the skipped measurement pipeline, and per-agent data already sits in workflow transcripts.
ideas.next: None.

ideas.name: Take finished material out of a live window
ideas.how: A live window cannot give material up. Under the split rule (PAR-22) a new session starts from a one-page brief that points at the repository; finished material never enters it.
ideas.problem: Material a session no longer needs stays in its window and is re-read on every call; I asked for it to be pulled out.
ideas.stands: Settled inside the split rule on 14 November: finished material is whatever a new session’s brief does not name. No mechanism of its own; untested. A new session’s first call reads a median 79k [M].
ideas.next: In the trial, count what a new session re-reads and what it guesses.
ideas.origin: My request in a chat of 26 October

themes.title: Remember what we learned
themes.covers: Carrying what we learn from one session to the next: the knowledge store, the reasoning-cache library, lessons that become checks, staleness and privacy.
intro: Every new session starts without what the last one learned, unless something carries it across. The ideas here give the harness a memory: the knowledge store designed in PR #183, the reasoning-cache library of harness v2, and smaller habits such as turning a lesson into a check.

My goal for the library is that a cheaper model finishes more of our work at the same quality. The pathway map shows, step by step, where an entry can be lost before it helps, which tells us what to build first. Both designs are complete on paper and unproven so far; their first steps are cheap tests built to prove them.

ideas.name: Root orchestrator's lesson memory
ideas.how: The root session writes one lesson file (why, how to apply) after each failure or correction from me; every later root session loads them.
ideas.problem: We keep repeating the same failures across sessions unless something carries each lesson forward.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed, machine-local: 15 [M] files, 81,266 [M] bytes, one file 50,136 [M] bytes. Bloat audit cost 18 [M] agents, 1.5M [M] tokens; repeat mistakes unmeasured.
ideas.next: Promote recurring lessons into CLAUDE.md or a test, and add check dates.

ideas.name: Memory file as pointer, not state restatement
ideas.how: Memory holds pointers to where state lives (plan, PR body, repository) and does not restate the state itself.
ideas.problem: The memory file carried a stale next step, so a new session could start from outdated state.
ideas.stands: In use: memory was rewritten as pointers in the review pass, which found and corrected one [M] stale next step.
ideas.next: Re-check memory pointers at each phase close.
ideas.origin: Harness review, after the clinic harness

ideas.name: Documentation spine and where-state-belongs table
ideas.how: A README resume route, a command catalogue, a where-state-belongs table, a slice-to-document map, and an AGENTS.md page with an evidence-status vocabulary.
ideas.problem: Every session needs a start-here route and one named owner for each kind of information, so no second status summary appears.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed; routing tables are hand-maintained and drifted. No token saving was measured; the context map still named old id ranges after the plan moved on.
ideas.next: Add a drift test checking the routing doc against the plan; the where-state-belongs table is the part to carry.

ideas.name: Tests that assert documents match the code
ideas.how: Tests parse registry, routing and context documents and fail when they differ from the plan or the code.
ideas.problem: Shared documents drift from the code, and I want a test to catch that rather than a reader finding it late.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed for registry-like tables only; the agent guide and context map have none. Drift caught was not counted; root-document edits broke three tests at gates [M].
ideas.next: Extend to the generated board, and add a CI test for the CLAUDE.md tables.

ideas.name: Commit raw workflow outputs as evidence with sha256 manifest
ideas.how: Copy the cited raw outputs into the program evidence folder and record a sha256 manifest, so every register id traces to its raw source.
ideas.problem: The raw outputs our findings register cites lived only in a temporary scratchpad folder and could vanish.
ideas.stands: In use: done in the review pass, and the plan’s evidence folder holds the outputs with their manifest. Not otherwise tested.
ideas.next: Keep adding evidence at each gate.
ideas.origin: Harness review, after the clinic harness

ideas.name: Short disciplined notes file as context memory
ideas.how: A short notes file, blank at start and under 3 KiB, kept current by the agent; it survives compaction and is read to resume.
ideas.problem: We want to keep what matters across compaction and restarts without heavy machinery or a restore system.
ideas.stands: Tested as the control arm of a small, interrupted clinic study: recall 15 of 15 [M] and task 100 % [M], the same as the adapter and native arms; the adapter used 6.1 % [M] more input.
ideas.next: Keep notes short and current; keep task.md as the baseline any new memory mechanism must beat.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; FixFlow CLAUDE.md and memory index

ideas.name: Real-case walkthroughs through ten design steps
ideas.how: Sonnet agents find real cases in the record; Opus agents walk each through the ten library steps and mark works, strains or breaks.
ideas.problem: We wanted to see where the library design breaks on real problems, not only on thought experiments or one simulated pathway.
ideas.stands: Measured on a chosen sample: 59 cases [M], 590 step judgments [M], 69 limitations found [M]. Most breaks: check 38, use 31, afterlife 29, match 26 [M]. Shows where, never how often.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list, then weigh each against the guessed conditions before any build.
ideas.origin: Library review, I asked for diversity of pathways

ideas.name: Fresh-agent cold-resume trial
ideas.how: A fresh Sonnet agent must recover ten [S] frozen facts from the repository alone; misses are classed absent, ambiguous or present-but-missed.
ideas.problem: We wanted to know whether the repository alone carries enough state for a new session to resume work with no memory of earlier sessions.
ideas.stands: Run once (2026-11-13): a fresh Sonnet agent recovered 10 of 10 [M] frozen facts, so no plan edit was needed; it exposed six [M] plan defects; the miss rule was untested.
ideas.next: Re-run at later phases; edit the plan only for absent or ambiguous misses; confirm the six plan defects are fixed.
ideas.origin: Harness review; Ship plan §7; Dex Horthy sweep

ideas.name: Break-even sweep: how much work must repeat
ideas.how: With reach and entry quality set high, sweep the share of work that could hold an entry; find where library cost crosses the ladder's.
ideas.problem: We want to know what share of our work needs a usable library entry for the library to pay for itself.
ideas.stands: From guessed inputs [G]: cost crosses at about half the work (middle running cost) or a fifth (low running cost) [G]; the middle guess is a quarter [G]. Not on the page.
ideas.next: Decide whether to add a comes-back slider or break-even chart to the library page.

ideas.name: Exact-text recall with stable path:line references
ideas.how: ctx.py scans transcripts, subagent transcripts and the archive for terms with no model calls; 'show' reopens the exact record by reference.
ideas.problem: After a reset an agent re-reads or re-derives what earlier sessions already said, and we cannot easily check what a session really said.
ideas.stands: Built in the testbed: scans 211 [M] transcripts / 115 MB [M] in 1 s [M]. Token saving not yet measured; in the 2026-10-14 screen no arm used journal recall [M].
ideas.next: Try a lexical scan over FixFlow's project transcripts to check what a session really said.

ideas.name: Planted-fact A/B harness for memory mechanisms
ideas.how: A fictional project script plants facts, corrections and rejected approaches; four arms run in separate sandboxes; a deterministic scorer, no model as judge.
ideas.problem: We judged memory and handoff mechanisms by feel; I want a repeatable test that does not use a model as the judge.
ideas.stands: Built in the testbed; dry run only, never against a model: 175 checks in about 65 s [M], failing when faults are injected [M]. Forecast 156M to 512M tokens, three arms [E].
ideas.next: Keep the method; shrink the scale before any live run, since cost is the barrier.

ideas.name: Pathway map: graph of states, trees as views
ideas.how: A graph of 40 [M] states and 83 [M] branches; three ways of working run on the same work; trees show every route.
ideas.problem: One walked pathway is not a diversity of cases; I wanted the library's pathways mapped and measured before any fix is chosen.
ideas.stands: Built; numbers reproduce on a fresh check. A model, not a forecast: 51 [M] of 60 [M] drawn unknowns are guesses [G]. Only much-comes-back, high-reach, good-entries beats the ladder.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list with me; optionally add a comes-back break-even slider.
ideas.origin: Library review; I proposed trees, ensembles and graphs

ideas.name: Ensemble of runs with rank-correlation ranking
ideas.how: 1000 [S] runs per tie draw each unknown across its range; we report percentiles and each unknown's Spearman rank correlation with each ratio.
ideas.problem: Most rates are unknown guesses, so a single answer would mislead; I want the spread and which unknowns matter most.
ideas.stands: Built; spread from guessed ranges, not a library measurement. Cost vs ladder at tie 0: 1.04 [G]; cheaper and no more wrong: 0.3% [G] at tie 0, 6.1% [G] at tie 1.
ideas.next: Keep using it.
ideas.origin: Library review; I suggested ensemble models

ideas.name: Funnel of a hundred pieces of work
ideas.how: Start with 100 pieces the cheap model gets wrong alone; count how many survive each stage, from entry held to right attempt.
ideas.problem: We want to see where the library's benefit is lost between a task arriving and the cheap model giving a right answer.
ideas.stands: Built; bars match design steps by hand. Middle values fall 13.1, 4.8, 2.3, 1.3, 1.1, 0.97, 0.35 [G]; the all-good setting ends at 31.7 [G].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Three conditions and eight corners
ideas.how: Group unknowns into comes back, reach and entry quality; set each poor or good across eight corners and an 11-by-11 reach-by-quality square.
ideas.problem: We want to know which conditions must hold for the library to beat the ladder of cheap-to-strong models.
ideas.stands: Built; group placement is a judgment, corners move up to 0.2 [G]. Only the corner where much comes back, reach is high and entries are good beats the ladder: cost 0.82 [G], wrong 0.67 [G] (every library unknown at its good end gives 0.75 [G]). High reach with poor entries: cost 1.43-1.53 [G].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Two weights per limitation: alone and last
ideas.how: 'Alone' moves only a limitation's unknowns to their good ends; 'last' leaves only it at middle values with all else good.
ideas.problem: A fix tested alone looks like nothing because steps multiply; a limitation's real size shows when it is the last one left.
ideas.stands: Built; weights are shares of a guessed 30.6% [G] fall and do not add up. Entry quality: alone 6.0%, last 104.1% [G]; step 4: alone 10.9%, last 94.0% [G].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Stampede control by advisory claim
ideas.how: First claim wins a sequence number in one write; a second session sees the solver and may wait or switch. Nothing blocks.
ideas.problem: Two parallel sessions can miss on the same symptom and both pay to solve it; we want to pay once.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; not yet tested. The solver's record carries the sequence as a fencing token. No renewal or expiry policy until a view shows the problem is real.
ideas.next: Build the claim table in phase KS-2.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after single-flight and fencing-token practice

ideas.name: Reasoning-cache library for cheaper models
ideas.how: Verified solutions sit in a SQLite index over a git journal. A cheap model adapts a match; unsolved problems climb the ladder.
ideas.problem: Most of our tokens run on costly models, and sessions re-solve solved problems. I want equal output from a cheaper model by reusing earlier solutions.
ideas.stands: Designed, never built; model outputs from guessed inputs: cost 1.03 [G] and wrong rate 1.01 [G] of the ladder's at middle values, 0.75 [G] and 0.67 [G] at all-good.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list, then run the zero-token index replay and no-build tests before deciding on a trial library.
ideas.origin: My idea; Library review; Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Lessons become checks
ideas.how: An entry seen three times becomes a proposed lint, test or gate clause; once it lands, the entry retires and the gate catches it.
ideas.problem: The same defects keep arriving and notes alone have not stopped them: 38 of 71 [M] practised ideas failed as prose.
ideas.stands: Designed; modelled as its own pathway: 0.04 [G] more pieces caught per 100 at middle values, 2.8 [G] at all-good. One real check already protects every agent [M].
ideas.next: Build after the library's journal exists; this would stop a defect arriving rather than relying on a lookup.

ideas.name: Misses are written down; lookup keys fixed
ideas.how: If a session solves what the library already held, record the miss and cause, fix the lookup keys; every lookup logs hit or miss.
ideas.problem: A lookup library that fails silently never improves, and we would not know when it should have answered.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; not tested, no hit rate measured. Stop rule carried over: fewer than 3 [S] verified hits in 20 [S] encounters or 8 [S] weeks.
ideas.next: Pilot after the recurrence audit in the knowledge-store design; this could show whether the library earns its keep.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; Knowledge-store design stop rule

ideas.name: Knowledge store of solved problems (PR #183)
ideas.how: Record symptom, cause, failed attempts, fix, files relied on and a check. A cheap agent finds it, runs the check, reuses the fix.
ideas.problem: We re-pay an expensive model each time the same hard defect or build trap returns, because past diagnoses sit in prose nobody can query by symptom.
ideas.stands: Designed (v1.3.1, PR #183); nothing built. Same-cause repeats: 3 to 5 [M] among 48 [M] fix commits on main. Stop if fewer than 3 [S] verified hits in 20 [S] encounters.
ideas.next: I run the recurrence audit (KS-D1) and decide on KS-D1b; run the frozen validation contract before building.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after caching and case-based reasoning

ideas.name: Journal of event files plus SQLite index
ideas.how: Immutable sha256-named event files in a private git store are the truth; a disposable per-host SQLite file is rebuilt from them. A publisher writes each event as a new file and never renames over an existing one.
ideas.problem: Several sessions, worktrees and hosts must share one store safely, with full history and no lost writes, on Windows with no database server.
ideas.stands: Designed, not built. Measured here: renaming over an existing file failed 99-126 [M] times per 8x1,000 events; freshness check 23-35 ms [M] at 5,000 events; 18,300 [M] test writes, no corruption.
ideas.next: Build as phase KS-1 after the audit and my KS-D1b yes; test with 8+ processes and 1,000+ writes.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after Fossil, git-bug and Beads (version control and issue trackers that keep their records inside a repository)

ideas.name: Entries with diagnosis path, negative results, do-not-apply
ideas.how: Each entry holds symptom, cause, ordered diagnosis steps, fix and scoped failed approaches. Do-not-apply entries are found by action words or exact error text.
ideas.problem: What failed and why is the costly part to save, and agents retry it; some prescribed fixes are wrong; 'X failed' notes go stale.
ideas.stands: Designed, not built; eight examples rebuilt from git history. Walked savings are guesses: 36 [G] old-job messages the enable-dispatcher entry would flag; 16 [G] broken-main days a stranded-fix scan fits.
ideas.next: Seed the eight worked examples as the first entries (phase KS-4); I confirm only do-not-apply entries that encode my decisions.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after KEDB and case-based reasoning

ideas.name: Stale by code change, never by age
ideas.how: Each entry lists its dependencies (file hashes, config keys, versions). A change marks it suspect and re-runs its check; if valid, it is re-stamped.
ideas.problem: A stored fix goes stale when the code it relies on changes. Age is a poor stand-in, and our libraries fill with things no longer true.
ideas.stands: Designed in the store design and harness v2; not tested. Whole-file hashes first, symbol-level spans later. The board carried 183 [M] minor findings with no status.
ideas.next: Implement file-hash and config-key dependency items in phase KS-3; I decide D12 on when a finding goes stale.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after the build systems Bazel and Shake; Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Feedback loop that revises entries
ideas.how: Applied then resolved confirms an entry; not resolved suppresses it at that footprint and queues an Opus revision. New proposals need independent approval.
ideas.problem: I want entries to improve with use, without a model rewriting them freely or confirming wrong hits.
ideas.stands: Designed in section 4.3 of the store design; not built or tested. Proposals activate only on a different Opus approver or two independent confirmations.
ideas.next: Build it together with the record path.

ideas.name: Seed the store through the write gate
ideas.how: Seed eight worked examples and four CLAUDE.md traps through the write gate, each approved by another Opus session; later, seed on lookup misses.
ideas.problem: A new store starts empty, and bulk-copying old prose would import errors, contradictions and untested claims.
ideas.stands: Designed (phase KS-4), blocked on KS-1 to KS-3 and KS-D1b. The inventory to draw on: about 20 [M] solved entries, 21 [M] traps and 60 [M] negative results, of which the first seed takes eight examples and four traps; 128 [M] open defects stay in the register.
ideas.next: I rule KS-D1 and the recurrence audit runs first; seeding then starts the store with checked entries only.

ideas.name: Pull-only lookup, nothing pushed or hooked
ideas.how: Agents run the lookup on demand; nothing is pushed or hooked. The recurrence audit and my yes come first, then a pilot (kill criterion).
ideas.problem: A layer that pushes extra context into every turn showed no measurable gain in the clinic testbed and costs tokens on every call.
ideas.stands: Designed; not tested for the store itself. Clinic synthetic trials showed identical acceptance with and without a context projection [M]; that evidence concerns always-loaded files, not a lookup hook.
ideas.next: Measure through the prospective log at phase KS-9; an edit-time hook (KS-D21) stays off by default.

ideas.name: Scrub secrets and customer data from the store
ideas.how: A scrubber redacts secrets, token patterns, phone and CNIC (Pakistani national identity card) numbers, and refuses the write if scrubbing fails (fails closed). Raw tables stay local; only scrubbed aggregates are committed.
ideas.problem: Entries could hold secrets or customer data, everything an agent reads reaches Anthropic, and raw symptom text committed to GitHub would expose it.
ideas.stands: Designed for phases KS-0, KS-1, KS-5 and KS-9; not tested. A known-miss fixture will show the name and address limit in every test run. A second gitleaks pass is my call (KS-D5).
ideas.next: Build in KS-1 with must-survive fixtures; use the local-only rule in KS-0.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after the secret scanners secretlint and gitleaks

ideas.name: Knowledge store copied off the machine to my VPS
ideas.how: The journal lives in a private repo, pushed over SSH to a bare git repo on my VPS; a code allow-list refuses github.com.
ideas.problem: The store sits on one disk, so a lost PC means lost lessons, and no code or defect data may reach a third party.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Needs phase P3b (the VPS) first; stage one is a one-way backup. Backup under 4 writers kept integrity [M]; restore-drill digests must match [T].
ideas.next: Run ks init and ks doctor in KS-1; set up SSH once the VPS exists (about ten minutes [E]).

ideas.name: Store home at profile root, with doctor check
ideas.how: The store sits in a profile-root folder outside the repo, OneDrive and AppData; ks doctor refuses other places and dead locks; a never-do list.
ideas.problem: Windows can give the Claude desktop app’s processes a private copy of an AppData folder, so they and my own shell would silently write to two different stores.
ideas.stands: Designed; to be built in phase KS-1. Stress test: 2 to 4 SQLITE_BUSY (database busy) failures per 1,200 writes at 8+ writers [M]; no corruption in about 18,300 writes [M].
ideas.next: Write the doctor tests in KS-1; they should catch silent split-file failures.

ideas.name: SQLite via node:sqlite as the store engine
ideas.how: SQLite built into Node 24 (FTS5, JSON, WAL), one file per host outside all worktrees; other engines stay in reserve behind an abstraction layer.
ideas.problem: We need a store engine with no install, daemon or telemetry that runs on this Windows PC and a Linux VPS for a few hundred rows.
ideas.stands: Designed; a bounded engine trial was rejected because no two candidates were close. 4 writer processes, 12,000 rows [M], integrity ok; graph-style lineage queries 0.07-95 ms [M].
ideas.next: Use node:sqlite in the KS-1 core.

ideas.name: Diff lookup warnings quoted by the reviewer
ideas.how: The CLI matches changed-line identifiers against stored do-not-apply entries at key points; the reviewer runs it at the head and answers each warning.
ideas.problem: A forbidden change never raises an error, so error-text lookup cannot stop it, and a reviewer saying 'ran the check' could be vacuous.
ideas.stands: Designed; replay on 154 [M] past commits: first rule warned on 48.7% [M], strict handles 27-44% [M], ex4 on 13 commits against 47 for a file join [M].
ideas.next: Build the diff join in KS-3, replay history in the pilot, wire the reviewer in KS-7.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design; my critique and refuter pass

ideas.name: Write gate against duplicate records
ideas.how: Before a record is saved, the store checks for duplicates, refuses self-matches and looks for an already-existing entry.
ideas.problem: We want lookups to return the right earlier diagnosis, never a plausible wrong one, so what enters the store must be clean.
ideas.stands: Designed in phase KS-2; not yet tested. Sonnet implements and Opus reviews the scrubber as a security boundary.
ideas.next: Build it in KS-2 after KS-1.

ideas.name: Declarative gate runner with control pairs
ideas.how: Probes over parsed data need a control pair (present on a broken commit, absent on a fixed one), mutants, preconditions and a three-way verdict.
ideas.problem: A stored 'this fix applies' claim can be wrong: a probe may match a moved guard or comment and pass vacuously, and agents copy near matches.
ideas.stands: Designed for phase 3 of the knowledge-store plan; not built or tested. Refuters rejected the first polarity rule (which way a probe must read on the broken and the fixed commit) on both review lenses [M]. Target: zero acted-on false leads [T].
ideas.next: Build the probes over parsed data first (eas.json, app.json, lockfiles), after the first phase. This guards the config-trap class.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after Meta’s automatic bug-fixing tools Getafix and SapFix

ideas.name: Write-through record at solve time, Opus-confirmed
ideas.how: The solving session fills a fixed schema before PR-ready, for hard problems only; the PR's Opus reviewer tries to refute it, then approves.
ideas.problem: Entries written later from a transcript lose the diagnosis path or fill the store with junk, and a self-confirmed entry could be wrong.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Estimated cost about 10 to 20 minutes of the solving session per record [E]. It is policy plus review, not a technical lock.
ideas.next: Seed the store, then run the pilot to see whether records get written and hold up.

ideas.name: Do-not-apply entries with a proposed-change check
ideas.how: A check run on a proposed change has four outcomes: applies, protection changed, protection disabled, or inconclusive. The prohibition text is never withheld.
ideas.problem: A rule like 'a locked account must refuse even a correct PIN' needs a check that fires before the forbidden change lands.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. 3 of 3 past edits to the protective files were legitimate [M], so stops go to the reviewer, never to an automatic verdict.
ideas.next: Write fixtures for an inverted test, a deleted file and a skipped test. This would protect the deliberate PIN-lock rule.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, completeness critic and my critique

ideas.name: Teardown checklist for a stop verdict
ideas.how: One code PR and one docs PR remove the skill, hooks, CI workflow, ignores and tool, revert the CLAUDE.md edit, leave the journal read-only.
ideas.problem: If we stop an experiment, we want nothing left lingering in the repo.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. It would make the knowledge-store experiment safely reversible.
ideas.next: Write the checklist into the teardown PR if a stop or retire verdict comes; I merge two PRs.

ideas.name: ks close: anchor, rescan at main, four counts
ideas.how: At phase close one command re-points checks to the merged commit, rescans main, labels 'fix not on main' or 'regression', and prints four counts.
ideas.problem: A fix can be pushed after its PR merged and stay stranded off main, and entries drift after refactors. One fix sat stranded for 16 days [M].
ideas.stands: Designed for phase 3b; not built or tested. Its test must fire at every main tip across the stranded span [T].
ideas.next: Build it in the first knowledge-store phases. It would catch stranded fixes without extra effort from me.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, refuter and critic findings

ideas.name: Blind pilot against two incumbents, with a stop point
ideas.how: A non-seeding session writes 20+ blind queries, 40+ hard negatives; lookups race grep over CLAUDE.md and git log. Verdict: go, go-minimal or stop.
ideas.problem: Nobody has measured whether a lookup beats grep over existing prose in a young repo; we should know after about five build sessions [E], before the rest of the build.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Go needs recall at shown of 60 percent or more [T] and zero acted-on false positives [T]. 0 in 40 probes bounds the rate at 7.5% [S].
ideas.next: Run the git-history audit first (KS-D1); freeze thresholds, then pilot. It decides the build before about ten sessions [E] are spent in all.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, judge panel, clinic-project warning

ideas.name: Prospective checkpoint on real encounters
ideas.how: After 20 encounters or 8 weeks, read the logged views: verified hits, acted false positives, escalations without lookup, and lookup cost against solve cost.
ideas.problem: A pilot on replayed history says little about new encounters or how much solve cost the store really avoids.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Checkpoint at 20 encounters or 8 weeks [S], whichever comes first. It would give the first measurement of the solve cost avoided.
ideas.next: Starts when the first real encounter is logged; I give the verdict and rule on two deferred options (KS-D21, KS-D22).

ideas.name: Diff-handle selectivity gate and false-fire ceiling
ideas.how: Author-named handles are replayed over about 150 commits [S] and refused above about 5 percent [S]; go needs warnings on at most 1 in 10 commits [T].
ideas.problem: Common identifiers would make the warning fire so often that nobody reads it.
ideas.stands: Designed; to be built in an early phase. Under the first rule 48.7 percent of commits warned [M]; useState 31 percent, client_id 22 to 28 percent, job 58 to 66 percent [M].
ideas.next: Print each handle's historic fire count when recording. This keeps a go verdict for the diff warning meaningful.

ideas.name: Measure compliance: escalations made without a lookup
ideas.how: Closing messages report escalations made without a lookup; ks close checks a diff lookup exists at the final head; reviewers log unwarned forbidden merges.
ideas.problem: With a pull-only store, 'useless' and 'never consulted' look the same from outside, so we cannot tell which one we have.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Self-reported and cross-checked against dispatch records; no hook in the first version.
ideas.next: Add the evidence line with the plan bullet after a pilot go.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, judge panel and critic

ideas.name: Break-even model for the knowledge store
ideas.how: Saving per hard encounter = h·(solve cost S − lookup cost), less miss and build costs. Audit estimates h, pilot measures it, checkpoint measures S.
ideas.problem: A build of about ten sessions needs a stated condition under which it repays itself.
ideas.stands: Designed; my parameters until the checkpoint replaces them with measurements. Build cost about ten sessions [E]. The decision rests on h times S, with nothing spent on Docker, sync or wiring first.
ideas.next: Fill h at the audit and S at the checkpoint.

ideas.name: Prose contradictions become a corrections docs PR
ideas.how: Phase KS-4 resolves each contradiction against git and opens one docs PR of corrections, each linking its entry.
ideas.problem: Our docs disagree with each other and with git, so a store seeded from them would store errors.
ideas.stands: Designed for phase KS-4; not run. Seven [M] named contradictions are listed. I merge the PR (KS-D12, default merge); it ships even if the store track stops.
ideas.next: Draft the corrections docs PR in KS-4; cleaner docs for every agent, with or without the store.

ideas.name: Eight handle kinds with canonicalised error templates
ideas.how: Each entry carries several key types (error template, signature, frames, command, paraphrase, identifiers, doc pointers, actions); a mask pipeline scrubs ids and numbers.
ideas.problem: The same root cause appears with different error text, files and words, so one key per entry would miss or mis-merge symptoms.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; not yet tested. One check: ex6's diff gives 113 tokens [M] firing on 91% of commits [M], so handles are author-named, not derived.
ideas.next: Build the canonicaliser with golden fixtures from the repo's own traps in KS-2.

ideas.name: Abstaining retrieval: miss, candidate or lead
ideas.how: Scrub and canonicalise, exact-handle prefilter, BM25 ranking, then abstain on score-free features; output is miss, candidate or lead inside a 2,000-character [S] cap.
ideas.problem: At a few hundred entries a wrong hit acted on is the dangerous failure, and a lookup must never leak customer data into the store.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Starting thresholds: lead 0.5, candidate 0.3, margin 0.2 [S]; frozen in KS-4. The customer-name case is a known scrubber miss.
ideas.next: Prototype on a synthetic corpus in KS-2; calibrate on seeded entries in KS-4.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, after small-scale BM25 research

ideas.name: ast-grep syntax-tree reader for code probes
ideas.how: After the pilot, a pinned ast-grep tool anchors checks to code symbols and ignores comments, tested with refactor mutants; unparseable code gives inconclusive.
ideas.problem: Whole-file hashes flag too much, and text checks over code are fooled by moved guards, comments and renames. We want checks that read structure.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; not yet tested. It fixes one of four ways a code check can be fooled [M, per source]. A 360 Total Security smoke test is pending.
ideas.next: I rule on it when the pilot gives a go. If I decline, we use no code reader at all.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design, my critique (syntax trees); ast-grep

ideas.name: Docker test-id gate and Jest/Vitest phase signal
