ideas.how: A sandbox with locked dependencies, no network and a per-run database runs named tests; Jest or Vitest hook failures never read as test failures.
ideas.problem: Entries whose cause lives in code behaviour need a runnable check, and a setup failure must not look like a failing test.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Conditional on a pilot go and uses the single Docker gate slot. It would give runnable checks for four examples but largely duplicates CI for several.
ideas.next: I start Docker Desktop at this phase's entry; free-form scripted checks stay off (KS-D18).

ideas.name: Retrieval thresholds frozen before the pilot
ideas.how: A leave-one-handle-out replay over seeded entries and hard negatives freezes lead 0.5, candidate 0.3 and margin 0.2 [S]; the pilot cannot change them.
ideas.problem: If the pilot can tune its own cut-offs it grades itself, and no literature gives thresholds for this kind of store.
ideas.stands: Designed; not yet tested. Values are my inferred parameters, not design facts. Small samples bound only coarsely: 0 failures in 40 means 7.5 percent or less [S].
ideas.next: Run the replay at the end of seeding; I accept the thresholds (KS-D8). That keeps the pilot a fair test.

ideas.name: Decisions, ruled-out and corrections list in PR body
ideas.how: Each draft PR body holds a list of decisions, ruled-out options and my corrections, appended as events happen, so a fresh session can recover them.
ideas.problem: Decisions made mid-phase live only in chat, and a summary after compaction can lose or distort them.
ideas.stands: Adopted by the harness review for the plan's resume section; not yet tested.
ideas.next: Start the list on the first phase PR.
ideas.origin: Harness review, after the clinic harness

ideas.name: One ruling: accept all defaults for my decisions
ideas.how: 'Accept all defaults' means run the recurrence audit, then stop and ask; KS-D1b is a second yes before any build.
ideas.problem: Sixteen of the decisions for me were hard to read at a glance, and accepting every default would have started about four Opus-heavy build sessions without my noticing. I want to decide few things, at the right time.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design: only KS-D1 is needed now. Starred decisions mark the real calls for me, and each phase close updates one OWNER-VIEW line. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: I answer KS-D1; the recurrence audit runs, then I am asked again before any build. Defaults never cover installs, hooks, permissions, deletes or anything leaving this PC.

ideas.name: Cross-session and cross-project recall
ideas.how: The library serves entries across sessions and projects, so a lesson paid for once reaches later windows, including a second project.
ideas.problem: New sessions do not remember earlier sessions' mistakes, so the same error is re-hit across many sessions and across projects.
ideas.stands: Idea; no fix agreed. One missing-tool error was re-hit in 54 of 78 [M] sessions across 9 [M] projects; only config-value checks still run in another repo (5 of 50 [M] fixes).
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list with me first; no fix is agreed yet.

ideas.name: Review findings fed forward by slice type
ideas.how: Store review findings by slice type and serve them to the builders of the next slice of that type.
ideas.problem: Review sends work back often; if findings repeat an earlier class, we pay the same fix round again.
ideas.stands: Idea; not tested. Record: 2.8 [M] review rounds per slice and 64 % [M] sent back.
ideas.next: Measure the share of review send-backs that repeat an earlier finding class; this decides whether feeding them forward pays.

ideas.name: Plan templates and cross-project design decisions
ideas.how: Store plan templates for recurring slice shapes, design decisions with their reasons, research claims, and stack and machine traps.
ideas.problem: We re-derive recurring slice shapes, design 'no' decisions, research claims and stack or machine traps each time they come up.
ideas.stands: Idea; no fix agreed. Seen working through today's documents, not a library: a design 'no' held five [M] months; a later design reused one that cost about 15M [M] helper tokens.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list with me; no fix is agreed yet.

ideas.name: Similarity-based reuse: a hit is a hypothesis
ideas.how: Fetch the nearest stored solution, treat it as a hypothesis, adapt it, and let tests decide; entries are verified when written.
ideas.problem: Exact repeats are rare, but similar problems across projects and time may be common; we need to know whether a similar-not-same solution fits.
ideas.stands: Idea, untested here; coverage on my work is unmeasured. Outside: 17-45% of fixes follow recurring patterns [S]; 40% of this repo's commits fit six file shapes [E].
ideas.next: Run the similar-problem coverage labelling and the oracle-match trial.
ideas.origin: Library review; my objection, after outside coding studies

ideas.name: Merge partial solutions through a graph
ideas.how: Score how much of a problem each entry covers, then select entries whose parts together cover it; needs a split into parts.
ideas.problem: A new problem may be covered in parts by two stored entries, and returning one best match cannot use both halves.
ideas.stands: Not yet tested. In real walks two checked answers did not make a checked merge (6 cases [M]); merge cards needed four parts (2 cases [M]); the seam needed a new fact.
ideas.next: No fix agreed; scoring and the split into parts are the design work, and tests decide.

ideas.name: Oracle-match trial
ideas.how: On held-out past problems, run Sonnet with and without the best-matching earlier solution and score both by tests.
ideas.problem: We want to learn whether a cheap model given the best earlier solution reaches strong-model quality, before we build the library.
ideas.stands: Proposed, not run. It would test the matching and use steps with no build.
ideas.next: Pick held-out past problems and best matches, then score by tests. It could settle whether to build the library.

ideas.name: Similar-problem coverage labelling
ideas.how: Label about 200 [E] recorded exploration runs by whether an earlier session had already answered the same or a similar question.
ideas.problem: Nobody has measured how much of our work an earlier session already answered, and that sets the ceiling for any library.
ideas.stands: Proposed, not run; needs no build. It decides the ceiling: halving exploration needs about 3 in 4 steps to repeat [E].
ideas.next: Label the runs. The result tells us whether a library can pay at all.
ideas.origin: Library review, refuters' cheapest decisive test

ideas.name: Fix withholding and optional journal deny rule
ideas.how: The CLI withholds a stored fix until the gate passes; the skill bars reading the journal; KS-D20 adds an optional deny rule.
ideas.problem: Cheap agents may apply a stored fix without verifying it first, and we want the check to happen before the fix is used.
ideas.stands: Deferred in the knowledge-store design: the journal is plain files, so withholding is a convention, not a lock. KS-D20 defaults to off. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: I may enable KS-D20, a settings deny rule on reading the store.

ideas.name: Thin MCP wrapper over lookup verbs
ideas.how: A small stdio MCP server wrapping the lookup and show commands.
ideas.problem: Agents might misuse the command-line tool, and we want a safer route if they do.
ideas.stands: Deferred in the knowledge-store design (KS-D15): the answer is no for now. Add it only if the lookup log shows misuse. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check the lookup log at phase KS-9.

ideas.name: guarded_refs advisory (allowed-site lists)
ideas.how: An optional author-named list of allowed sites per entry; the diff lookup reads it as a hint that never changes a verdict.
ideas.problem: We can detect a new reference to a guarded identifier, but cannot tell whether an existing check covers it.
ideas.stands: Deferred, default off; to be built in a later build phase after the pilot, or after that. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Measure its false-alarm rate from git history first; I rule on it at the checkpoint (KS-D22).

ideas.name: Automatic footprint capture for knowledge-store entries
ideas.how: Three captures: what the agent read (hooks or transcript), what the check executed (coverage), and a fixed environment probe.
ideas.problem: Authors may forget to list what an entry depends on, so we want the list captured, not guessed.
ideas.stands: Deferred. The pilot uses only the fix diff, check inputs, environment probes and transcript reads; coverage capture waits (KS-D5) and needs two small dev dependencies. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: I decide on the two dependencies (KS-D5). Coverage capture could then tighten when entries go stale.

ideas.name: Edit-time warning hook
ideas.how: A fail-open hook (one that lets the edit through if the hook itself fails) on Edit and Write diffs the edited path through the same lookup and shows one short warning. It never blocks.
ideas.problem: We want a forbidden edit to warn at edit time, not only in review.
ideas.stands: Deferred, default off; not yet tested. Its known blind spot is edits made through Bash or PowerShell.
ideas.next: Waits on harness decision D17 (hooks stay off) and on KS-D21 at the checkpoint, if the warning rate is within the ceiling.

ideas.name: Temporal knowledge graph
ideas.how: Store facts with validity intervals, from one commit until superseded, and record when each was learned; start with a tool-written temporal view.
ideas.problem: I want recall to say when a fact was true and when it was recorded, so we never return a stale conclusion.
ideas.stands: Idea, not tested here: our graph test had one snapshot per commit and no validity intervals. Outside study: context cut from 115k [S] to 1.6k [S] tokens, against full context; benchmark disputed.
ideas.next: Cover it in the wider test, building the temporal view first; I decide whether it is included.
ideas.origin: Graph test, after Graphiti and Zep

ideas.name: SQLite graph library for a self-evolving repository
ideas.how: Not built in the clinic lane: no SQLite file, graph or self-modifying part exists; nearest pieces are exact-text recall, agent notes and outside tools.
ideas.problem: I remembered a graph-based library with fast, token-minimal recall that improves itself; we wanted to know where it lives and whether it works.
ideas.stands: Idea only: no graph or SQLite recall measured, and nothing in the clinic line learns or rewrites itself. The knowledge-store track (PR #183) is where it would come from.
ideas.next: Use LCM and Virtual Context as design references; I pick which outside designs to test against the plain task file.

ideas.name: Scheduler-system knowledge graph (Pulse)
ideas.how: A scheduling assistant writes structured JSON episodes into a temporal graph (Graphiti on Neo4j), skipping model extraction at write time.
ideas.problem: A candidate source of my recollection of a graph-based memory; we wanted to see whether it is the one.
ideas.stands: Idea only: a README-level look at a different project of mine; no benchmark found and not tested.
ideas.next: Keep as a pattern reference only.
ideas.origin: My project (scheduler system); Clinic testbed sweep

ideas.name: Embeddings behind a measured trigger
ideas.how: None in v1. Only if vocabulary misses reach a stated trigger: add sqlite-vec and a local embedder; dense-only hits stay candidates, never leads.
ideas.problem: Keyword search misses paraphrases with no shared words; we do not know if vectors would help at this size, and installing them carries risk.
ideas.stands: Deferred (KS-D16), not yet tested. Trigger: at least 3 [S] misses on 3+ [S] entries among 10+ [S] lookups, with a 95% lower bound on k/n of 5% [S].
ideas.next: Report k, n and the bound at KS-9 from the missed-existing view.
ideas.origin: Knowledge-store design; my critique and refuter pass

ideas.name: Trained tree ensemble over recorded episodes
ideas.how: Train a tree ensemble on a few hundred labelled episodes from session records to predict which route a task takes through the design.
ideas.problem: We want predicted routes from our own recorded sessions instead of from guessed rates.
ideas.stands: An idea for a later phase; not started. Members must make different mistakes and need a sampled audit for branches they cannot see. The tool-error scan already exists.
ideas.next: Label a few hundred episodes, then decide whether to build it.

ideas.name: Rejected storage engines and memory products
ideas.how: Candidates were scored on local-only data, Windows, telemetry off and one-developer cost; Cassandra, ClickHouse, Neo4j, Qdrant, hosted products: rejected or reference only.
ideas.problem: I asked that we neither re-invent decades-old solutions nor fake a database with Markdown, so engines had to be ruled in or out.
ideas.stands: Rejected as components; Postgres, DuckDB and Dolt stay reserve targets. Cassandra needs an 8 GB [S] RAM floor; the Postgres-container design scored 222 of 360 [M] and is unreachable with Docker off.
ideas.next: None; revisit only if a logged trigger fires.

ideas.name: Push memory, age expiry and self-rewriting rules
ideas.how: A layer that pushes context into sessions, retires notes by age, matches headings by keyword, and lets rules rewrite themselves.
ideas.problem: We want a memory that stays current by itself, without someone tidying it, so sessions start with what is still true.
ideas.stands: Parked: rejected in the knowledge-store design and listed as not built in harness v2. It was not tested here, so we have no result either way.
ideas.next: Nothing planned.

ideas.name: Hand-written code lexer for span anchoring
ideas.how: A zero-dependency lexer for Python, TS/JS, JSON and YAML, with span anchors, planned to let code checks skip comments and strings.
ideas.problem: We wanted code checks that ignore comments and strings and anchor to function spans without installing a heavy parser.
ideas.stands: Withdrawn after my critique: nobody had evaluated it and its spec left out JSX. Never built. Replaced by the ast-grep reader.
ideas.next: None; the ast-grep reader (decision KS-D5b) replaces it. It could return only if a lane evaluates it.

themes.title: Find the right code fast
themes.covers: Finding what a change touches: indexes, the typed code store, graph engines, co-change, search baselines, touch lists and a what-is-true-now view.
intro: Before an agent can change code it has to find what the change touches. On 75 held-out FixFlow commits, a typed store of code facts put 0.700 of the touched files and definitions in front of the reader within an 8,000-token answer [M], ahead of a scripted search at 0.625 [M]. The gain sits in the mobile app; outside it the two are still too close to call.

The three engines we tried, one relational and two graph, gave identical answers, so the engine can be chosen on speed, size and effort. The test was a fixed script with no agent in it. Next comes a zero-token index replay; the wider test I asked for, with an agent in the loop, knowledge graphs, time and caching, follows under a written budget once I settle GT-1.

ideas.name: Existing code maps: import contracts, CODE-MAP, Haiku locator
ideas.how: Import-boundary contracts (import-linter on the backend, ESLint on the web), a hand-written code map document and a Haiku locator agent.
ideas.problem: Agents need to find where a feature lives without a call-graph tool.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow. Not measured. Mobile code has no boundary enforcement yet.
ideas.next: Add mobile boundary rules with dependency-cruiser.

ideas.name: Slow grep-and-model search over optimised retrieval
ideas.how: Prefer reliable agentic search, grep plus a model, over optimised retrieval; a learned reranker was passed over.
ideas.problem: We want to pick a retrieval design for code understanding that is reliable rather than clever.
ideas.stands: In use: it matches what the harness already does. A learned reranker is a skip. Taken as a stated preference, not a measured result.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Same-facts cross-check between engines
ideas.how: Given identical facts and algorithm, two engines must return the identical answer; a mismatch is a bug, not a result.
ideas.problem: We want score differences to come from facts, algorithm and output form, never from an engine bug.
ideas.stands: In use in the graph test: typed arms identical on 770 of 770 [M] held-out tasks; the two hypothesis differences were exactly 0 [M].
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Podcast RSS feeds for transcripts
ideas.how: Read the feed's transcript tag; otherwise fetch the audio file attached to the episode (its enclosure).
ideas.problem: Show pages expose only part of a podcast's transcript, so research on outside ideas is incomplete.
ideas.stands: In use for two podcasts: one feed gave a 12,100-word [M] transcript against 1,800 words [M] from the site.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: X timeline via fxtwitter; charts read as images
ideas.how: Page the fxtwitter timeline endpoint for a user's posts and self-replies; give chart images to a reader agent.
ideas.problem: X posts could not be read (HTTP 402) and benchmark numbers sat only in chart images.
ideas.stands: In use: 197 statuses since 1 September [M], 159 [M] the author's own, plus 7 [M] charts read. Replies under posts are not captured.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Typed symbol-level graph of the repo
ideas.how: A model-free script extracts about 2,500 symbols and 19+ edge kinds [M] from each task's parent commit; queries rank neighbours within hop budgets.
ideas.problem: We want a short ranked answer to what else must change with this code, using typed links across web, mobile and backend that flat search cannot.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: recall in an 8,000-token [S] answer 0.700 [M] vs 0.625 [M] for a scripted search. The gain is on mobile seeds (+0.151 [M]). No agent was run.
ideas.next: Decide on the agent pilot, to see whether the graph helps an agent.
ideas.origin: Graph test; my objections to the first test

ideas.name: Co-change floor (files that changed together)
ideas.how: From earlier commits only, count files changed together, rank by support (how often the two files changed together), confidence (the share of the seed file’s commits that also changed the other) and recency, and return the top files within the token budget.
ideas.problem: We need a cheap baseline for what else changes with this file, taken only from git history, that any graph must beat.
ideas.stands: Measured on held-out commits: recall 0.638 [M] (tuning split 0.752 [M]). Typed graph beats it by +0.063 [M], but only on mobile seeds; on backend seeds co-change 0.709 [M] vs typed 0.699 [M].
ideas.next: Keep reporting every graph result beside this floor and its sensitivity checks.
ideas.origin: Graph test; strongest signal in the research round

ideas.name: Same-directory floor
ideas.how: Return the other files in the seed file's folder, packed to the token budget, with no graph and no history.
ideas.problem: We want to know whether our vertical-slice folder layout already carries most connection information, so any graph must beat files in the same folder.
ideas.stands: Measured on held-out commits: recall 0.549 [M] (tuning split 0.719 [M]). Typed graph beats it by +0.151 [M]; on web seeds same-directory scored 0.773 [M] vs typed 0.664 [M], interval includes zero.
ideas.next: Keep as a floor in every future retrieval test.

ideas.name: PageRank and community priors for ranking
ideas.how: Personalised PageRank from the seed, optionally with a stored community grouping, ranks neighbours; iterations run in our code, only grouping comes from the engine.
ideas.problem: We want the most relevant neighbours of a changed file first inside a token budget, using ranking a flat table lacks natively.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: no gain of 0.05 or more; +0.015 [M] on the main task, interval spans zero. Five random re-draws of the Louvain communities moved recall about as much as the effect (standard deviation 0.008 [M]).
ideas.next: Revisit only on a larger task set or in an agent pilot.
ideas.origin: Graph test, after Aider's repo map

ideas.name: Hop sweep with per-edge-kind budgets
ideas.how: On tuning commits only, sweep hop depth, direction, per-edge-kind budgets and hub cuts; pick the simplest setting within one standard error and freeze it.
ideas.problem: One global hop limit returns either too little or a flood. We want depth, direction and hub handling chosen per kind of link.
ideas.stands: Tested on tuning commits: import neighbours reach recall 0.38, 0.72 and 0.87 [M] at 1, 2 and 3 hops, with 9, 45 and 90 [M] files. Hop depth moved the score most.
ideas.next: Report whole curves, never one point.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; my question on hop count

ideas.name: Output form and token-budget packing
ideas.how: One shared packer and tokenizer return the same output forms (paths, signatures, line ranges, snippets) at 2k, 4k, 8k and 16k [S] token budgets.
ideas.problem: We want to score an answer by value per token, not stored size, so the form the model receives is itself tested.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: typed beats search by +0.070 and +0.102 [M] at 2,000 and 4,000 [S] tokens; recall at 16k [S] is 0.832 [M]. Every answer filled its budget.
ideas.next: Measure tokens in an agent run, not only in the packer.
ideas.origin: Graph test; my point on how facts are stored

ideas.name: SQLite as the relational arm
ideas.how: SQLite with typed node and edge tables, covering indexes, full-text search, a co-change table and depth-capped recursive queries.
ideas.problem: We want the graph engines to face a strong established relational opponent, and a possible plain home for the facts, so the test is fair.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: recall 0.700 [M], identical to both graph engines; 0 mismatches on 7,040 [M] random configurations. First test: 0.05 ms [M] per query.
ideas.next: Report engine speed, size and effort from the timing run.

ideas.name: LadybugDB embedded graph engine arm
ideas.how: The same facts loaded in LadybugDB 0.22.3 (a maintained Kuzu fork), queried with Cypher and its PageRank and Louvain extension, inside a Linux image.
ideas.problem: We want to test an established embedded graph engine with native typed paths and ranking, rather than compare graph and relational designs through code we wrote ourselves.
ideas.stands: Tested: 0 mismatches in 47,244 [M] comparisons against the reference; recall 0.700 [M] on held-out, equal to the relational arm. Native ranking slow, about 0.7 s [M]. About 16 MB [S] install.
ideas.next: Report engine speed, size and effort from the timing run.
ideas.origin: Graph test; I approved it on 2026-11-12

ideas.name: DuckDB with DuckPGQ graph layer arm
ideas.how: DuckDB 2.0.0 with the DuckPGQ extension loaded with the same facts; one edge table per kind, since edge filters are unavailable inside paths.
ideas.problem: We want to test a graph query layer on a relational engine, holding the engine fixed and changing only the query layer.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: shown answers identical to the relational arm on 770 of 770 [M] tasks; recall 0.700 [M]. No PageRank or Louvain, so rankings fall back to SQL. About 63 MB [S] install.
ideas.next: Report engine speed, size and effort from the timing run.

ideas.name: Traversal cache for what-depends-on-this
ideas.how: A cache over graph traversal results for dependency lookups.
ideas.problem: We wanted to avoid recomputing what-depends-on-this-file queries, if they were slow enough to be worth caching.
ideas.stands: Tested on the first graph: all 477 [M] dependency queries together take about 1 ms [M], so there is nothing to save. The replacement test did not re-test the cache question.
ideas.next: None. It would return only if lookups became slow at larger scale.

ideas.name: Code-reading question set (50 questions)
ideas.how: 50 [S] structured questions answered by one reader with evidence lines and checked blind by a second; 20 for tuning, 30 held out.
ideas.problem: We want to score structured lookups, such as which tables a screen writes, with truth read from the code rather than from the extractor.
ideas.stands: Tested on 30 held-out questions: typed minus search +0.100 [M], inconclusive. On 23 untouched questions +0.189 [M]. Median typed answer 31 vs 695 [M] tokens search read, not like for like.
ideas.next: State both token views and name the typed side's uncounted costs.

ideas.name: Graphify outside code-graph tool
ideas.how: A PyPI package builds a knowledge graph from code and mixed corpora; extraction may send file contents to a model API.
ideas.problem: We search code by grep and a hand-written map. I want to know why this tool looks good while our graph experiments showed modest gains.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed over an 11-file snapshot: 92 nodes, 127 edges, 10 communities [M]; no query result. Its 71.5x [S] token claim is self-measured. Not installed for FixFlow.
ideas.next: Run as shipped in the wider test: throwaway clone, isolated install, version 14+ days old, ten fixed questions against grep.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; Harness review; raised by me

ideas.name: Corpus map of typed edges for planning documents
ideas.how: A versioned map of 11 planning files as typed edges with exact line spans, one status per record, a coverage ledger and hash-based refresh.
ideas.problem: Planning documents are hard to navigate. Fresh agents need bounded, source-cited context from the plan with known gaps, not whole documents.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed as design plus prototype; no coding agent used it. 3,361 records for 167 KB [M]; extraction recall 0.52 [M] against an earlier reading; validation never run.
ideas.next: Run the frozen validation contract before building any map; carry over the status discipline and recompute-from-base rule.

ideas.name: Context packet query with frontier and gap lists
ideas.how: Breadth-first expansion from a named start within a token budget; each record carries a quote and file lines, plus unresolved, frontier and coverage lines.
ideas.problem: We want to give a fresh agent a small, cited evidence packet by named start, not whole documents.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed; never compared with routed reading, so delivered tokens and task quality are unknown. Extraction recall 0.523 [M] exact, 0.588 [M] loose.
ideas.next: Run the validation contract before building a packet tool for FixFlow.

ideas.name: Coverage ledger and stale-label freshness
ideas.how: A ledger lists read and unread chunks per file version; queries check file hashes, label changed records stale, and refresh supersedes rather than deletes.
ideas.problem: A derived index silently goes out of date when source files change, and we cannot tell what was actually read.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed as a manual command, tested on synthetic cases only; the changed-source case was not run. 4,053 dangling endpoints at levels 1 and 2 [M].
ideas.next: Wire chunk-hash plus stale labelling to a hook or CI, to catch CLAUDE.md drift.

ideas.name: Candidate index: similarity proposes, never decides
ideas.how: Similarity and alias proposals sit in a separate candidates file that no query reads; a test deletes it and checks packets are byte-identical.
ideas.problem: Similarity retrieval can leak guesses into answers that are meant to carry evidence. We want guesses kept apart.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed with its deletion test; precision not measured. 1,906 candidates [M] in the store, 93 [M] open for one file.
ideas.next: Copy the separation rule into any FixFlow recall tool.

ideas.name: Slice fragments generate board and true-now view
ideas.how: Each slice writes a small state fragment; tools generate a short board and a true-now view; the board diff becomes a check step.
ideas.problem: Slice status and findings go stale and get re-read; one writer edits an 800-line board by hand and sessions carry a 221 KB document.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3; nothing built. Target: board from 221 KB [M] to under 20 KB [T]; root edits at merge zero [T].
ideas.next: Write the fragment format and generator; add SQLite tables only if a query needs more.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; Bottleneck compile; knowledge-store design

ideas.name: Doc-context small language model with hash staleness
ideas.how: A local small model builds a bounded doc-state summary, each statement pointing to its source; stale summaries are flagged by source hash.
ideas.problem: Our evolving documentation goes stale and costs context to read.
ideas.stands: Designed in the clinic testbed; nothing run. Premises: one task-state file 17,174 chars [M] against a 9,000 [S] budget (one case); docs about 1.36 MB [M].
ideas.next: Build the cheap, testable part first: hash-based stale detection.

ideas.name: Pull graph output, never push; build per worktree
ideas.how: Return graph output only as a tool result, never in the system prompt or CLAUDE.md; build the graph per worktree at query time.
ideas.problem: We want to stop a graph or memory layer from breaking the cached start of every window or describing the wrong working tree.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule for any future retrieval build; not itself built or tested. Agents work in five [M] worktrees with uncommitted files, so a shared graph would mislead.
ideas.next: Write into the design of any retrieval tool we build.

ideas.name: Neo4j and other server graph engines
ideas.how: Neo4j Community, FalkorDB or Postgres with Apache AGE run through Docker, loaded with the same typed facts.
ideas.problem: We want to know whether the market-standard graph database is a better home for the repo graph and its algorithms.
ideas.stands: Deferred: not installed, not tested. A server adds 1 to 2 GB [E] of memory on a PC short of memory, and I chose embedded engines instead.
ideas.next: Revisit only if the agent pilot shows graphs help and an embedded engine proves too small.

ideas.name: Embedding-search arm (vector index)
ideas.how: A vector index over code and docs, queried by similarity; needs a model download.
ideas.problem: We want the strongest non-graph baseline from the literature in the test, so graph gains are not credited to the index.
ideas.stands: Deferred: not in the frozen protocol and not tested. It needs a model download, which is my decision to approve.
ideas.next: Add to the wider test if I approve the download.

ideas.name: Model-built knowledge graph and graph database
ideas.how: A model reads code and docs and writes entities, relations and cluster summaries, possibly served from a graph database server or paired with embeddings.
ideas.problem: We want semantic relations parsers miss, so an agent fetches small context fast and recalls facts through a rich graph.
ideas.stands: Deferred, not tested here. Outside, model-built graphs cost about a thousand times [S] vector indexing and often lose to plain retrieval; the one big gain was against full context.
ideas.next: Test inside the wider test via Graphify; index replay decides whether a small index earns a trial.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; GraphRAG-style systems

ideas.name: Agent-in-the-loop pilot
ideas.how: Replay 24 to 30 [E] fix commits with one fixed agent: grep alone, plus SQL, a graph tool or BM25; record tokens, calls, success.
ideas.problem: I want to know whether a graph or knowledge layer lets an agent finish with fewer tokens, calls and mistakes than ordinary search.
ideas.stands: Deferred, not run; it needs model tokens and many agents. One outside study cut tokens 17 to 39 % [S] on two benchmarks and raised them on a third.
ideas.next: I decide on the pilot and its token budget; start with the wider-test protocol.

ideas.name: Wider graph test protocol
ideas.how: Five research lanes, an assumptions audit and strongest-architecture design, a refuter, a protocol draft and a design check; no installs.
ideas.problem: I want to test the architecture I described, with knowledge layer, time, caching, an agent and Graphify as an arm, not only the scorable part.
ideas.stands: Idea stage: research and protocol draft were in progress when last recorded; nothing tested. The earlier test's narrow scope must be stated up front.
ideas.next: Read the draft protocol and decide on Graphify and the agent pilot.

ideas.name: File-level connection graph (first test)
ideas.how: A model-free script builds a file-to-file graph from imports, test mocks and doc citations, held as JSON or SQLite, and answers everything that depends on this file.
ideas.problem: We wanted one small answer to what depends on this file, instead of several search rounds or reading many files.
ideas.stands: Parked: I asked for the strongest form of the idea to be tested instead, and this first version’s verdict was withdrawn. It had 618 files and 1,119 links [M]; answered 1 of 200 [M] searches fully. Replaced by the typed graph test.
ideas.next: None; the idea lives on in the typed graph and the contract map.

themes.title: How we orchestrate
themes.covers: How the main session plans, briefs and judges: model tiers, judgement-free discovery with citations, fresh-context checks, workflow shapes and recovery when an agent fails.
intro: Our method is written down in the orchestration design of 31 October: a main session that plans and judges, cheaper models that discover with citations, and fresh-context reviewers that try to refute what was found. This document was made that way.

The ideas here are how we brief agents, shape workflows, choose a model for each job and recover when an agent fails or returns nothing. Many are in use every day; the rest are refinements we have designed and can now test.

ideas.name: Root as the only writer of shared documents
ideas.how: Only the root edits shared documents. Slices propose changes in their own record as exact old and new text; registry files are append-only.
ideas.problem: Several sessions editing the same shared documents conflict and give us divergent truth. We want one source for each.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic build, and it became a bottleneck itself: board state 221 KB [M], root edits caused failing checks at two slices, and docs were stale at wrap-up.
ideas.next: Replace with slice-written fragments and a generated board; add a test that fails when lock-step edits diverge.

ideas.name: Infrastructure failures kept apart from content failures
ideas.how: A null is never a result; fresh nulls suggest a session limit; zero tests is never green; coverage reads 16/16 or carries a waiver.
ideas.problem: A flaky provider or a run that tested nothing must not read as a pass, or as a bad brief.
ideas.stands: In use as program law in the orchestration design, and confirmed in the BAML sweep. BAML's own optimiser documents that it does not cover this.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Models give verdicts; code computes counts and scores
ideas.how: Models give yes/no or enum verdicts; code computes scores, logs dropped counts, applies no silent caps; each phase gets a cheap human-checkable proof.
ideas.problem: Holistic model scores are unreliable and I cannot read all the logic; a script that filters or asks a model to count can lose items silently.
ideas.stands: In use as program law: enum verdicts roll up into buckets by script, and the findings backlog means nothing is silently dropped. Confirmed in the BAML sweep.
ideas.next: Optionally add a rule to report received and kept counts for any filtering step.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design, Dex Horthy sweep and BAML sweep

ideas.name: Coordinator session that never implements
ideas.how: One session on the plan branch owns the ship plan, results file, OWNER-VIEW page, contracts and merge-ready calls. It dispatches reviews and never implements.
ideas.problem: With many sessions at once, we need one place that owns the plan, shared results and merge calls, kept free of implementation work and its token cost.
ideas.stands: In use since 2026-11-13. The coordinator woke and resumed eight [M] lane sessions after the power loss. It lets 8 [M] lanes run at once; no measured effect on speed yet.
ideas.next: Keep the lane board current; dispatch binding reviews as lanes report ready.

ideas.name: Plan on a branch, tagged before lanes read
ideas.how: Lanes read the plan branch by absolute path or git show. The coordinator commits, pushes and tags every plan edit before telling a lane.
ideas.problem: The plan, design notes and evidence live on a PR branch, not main, so a lane could read uncommitted text or miss the files.
ideas.stands: In use: tags plan-v9 and plan-v9.1 exist, and the results file cites the plan at v9.1. No measured effect yet.
ideas.next: Tag each later plan edit before briefing lanes.

ideas.name: Defer phase plan and recipes to Stage 3
ideas.how: One session per phase; Sonnet for well-specified fixes; Opus for outbox, lifecycle, ledger and migration code; Opus reviewers refute by default.
ideas.problem: Phase design before verified facts would be built on guesses, so we wanted it designed only after the deep-dive.
ideas.stands: Applied: the orchestration design deferred the phase plan on purpose, and it was designed later as the ship plan, after the second gate.
ideas.next: Done: the ship plan took this over.

ideas.name: Staged workflows with judging gates between them
ideas.how: Pre-flight, cheap discovery, gate, Opus deep-dive, gate, phase plan. The main session reads results by id at each gate and writes a record.
ideas.problem: We want cheap wide discovery, narrow expensive deep dives and a recorded decision between stages, so the plan is designed only after a verified picture exists.
ideas.stands: Both gates written 2026-11-01. Discovery: 16/16 [M] areas, about 1.67M [M] tokens, 14 min [M]. Deep-dive: 8 [M] analysts, 139 [M] findings, about 3.3M [M] tokens, 23 min [M].
ideas.next: Keep using a gate record after each later stage.

ideas.name: Model tiers by role, raise effort before tier
ideas.how: Haiku extracts; Sonnet maps and runs gates; Opus analyses, refutes; the main session judges. Name model and effort each start; raise effort before tier.
ideas.problem: Model choice is our main cost lever. We want the strongest model only where mistakes are expensive, and no agent at an unchosen strength.
ideas.stands: Used in FixFlow and the whole clinic build; 12 [M] agent definitions built: 6 Opus and 5 Sonnet on PR #185, and the Haiku explorer. Tiering has no cost measurement yet; every clinic slice needed 2-4 [M] review rounds.
ideas.next: Record actual spend per tier against the design's cost envelope so the split can be tested.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design; Clinic testbed; Skills packages

ideas.name: Brief contract and CONTEXT block for every agent
ideas.how: A brief names goal, files, branch, settled facts and what done returns, in one paragraph. A fixed context block with rules is prepended verbatim.
ideas.problem: Our agents re-derive project facts, start without a clear task, drift and overstate what was proved. We want every brief complete and every claim cited.
ideas.stands: Used on every brief in the clinic build. No before/after of rework was measured. It does not stop overstated reports: the clinic S11 gate found two unsupported claims.
ideas.next: Keep the block short and refresh it per run; reuse the three provenance tags.

ideas.name: Typed output schemas, forced and validated
ideas.how: Agents return a fixed JSON Schema object, validated and retried by the workflow tool. A blocked agent returns a named code, not a guess.
ideas.problem: Free prose from agents is costly to read and invites unchecked claims. We want results the orchestrator and scripts can read by a fixed shape.
ideas.stands: In use: twelve schemas in the design, all 11 [M] agent definitions reference them; forced output is how the harness works. Strict validation has no silent-drop failure; BAML repair has one [S].
ideas.next: Validate the schemas against the first real outputs.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design; BAML sweep; Skills packages

ideas.name: State in the repository, parents judge by diff
ideas.how: Each node keeps one task record (status, next action, evidence). A parent reads the diff and record; resume from branch plus record.
ideas.problem: Work state lived in chat context and was lost on compaction or restart. We want a stopped session resumable, and parents not trusting a child summary.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic: 37 [M] task folders; no real dead-session recovery timed, resume tooling only synthetic. FixFlow skips it, since plan, PR body, results file and git already own state.
ideas.next: Split current state from archive to avoid the 829-line board read; reconsider the single-owner rule.

ideas.name: Wave board as single current-state file
ideas.how: One file holds the current-state table (slice, status, session, tier, gate), dated gate sections, wrap-up, next actions and open questions. Root edits only.
ideas.problem: We want one authoritative place for what is built, in review and next, so any session can pick up the build.
ideas.stands: In use to wrap-up in the clinic: 829 lines, 219,111 bytes [M] at sweep time. Append-only gate sections let earlier statements go stale, and nothing gave me a live progress view.
ideas.next: Split a short current-state file from an archive of gate sections.

ideas.name: Parallel research agents each own one report
ideas.how: A delegation template names question, scope, ownership, return form and stop condition. Research agents each own one report file; four [S] workers at most.
ideas.problem: Delegated agents return unfocused or overlapping work. We want each worker with a clear question, its own file and a stop condition.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed. Delegation cost was not measured; more workers is not evidence of better results. The root integrates and cross-checks, not by vote.
ideas.next: Verify in the FixFlow tool setup whether subagents can be given a writable path.

ideas.name: Short stable handles instead of hashes
ideas.how: Agents use short labels such as H-01 and S-07b; long hashes are checked by git in code, so a mis-echo fails loudly.
ideas.problem: Agents echoing long ids or commit hashes can mis-aggregate them silently.
ideas.stands: In use in the harness. An outside measurement on id aggregation had a small sample, two runs per arm [S], so we rely on the practice, not the figure.
ideas.next: Keep using it.
ideas.origin: Harness practice, confirmed by BAML sweep

ideas.name: Same-tier retry; only infrastructure changes tier
ideas.how: Structured-output retries stay inside the same subagent; scripts retry at the tail with the same task and model.
ideas.problem: Silently escalating to a stronger model after a schema failure hides cost and masks a defect in the brief.
ideas.stands: In use by construction: retries already stay on the same model, so the rule holds today. A design rule could state it.
ideas.next: Optionally write the rule into the orchestration design.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after Pydantic AI and DSPy

ideas.name: Escape-hatch values in every schema
ideas.how: Schemas carry values such as UNVERIFIABLE, untestable, UNCLEAR, unknown or empty, and an unknown is recorded as unknown.
ideas.problem: A forced schema can make a model invent a conforming answer when the input does not fit.
ideas.stands: In use: already in the output schemas and a research rule. Agents wrote 'undated' honestly in the BAML sweep.
ideas.next: Audit the contracts for required fields that have no unknown path.
ideas.origin: Practitioner advice, confirmed by BAML sweep

ideas.name: Briefs in git; contract shapes frozen
ideas.how: Briefs live in git, runs cite commit hashes, and the fixed return contracts keep their shape so only prose is edited.
ideas.problem: We want prompt changes to be reviewable and every result traceable to a version.
ideas.stands: In use and confirmed in the BAML sweep.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: Compare structures on the problem case, not pieces
ideas.how: Build one deep-dive lane BAML's way, compare both structures on ten dimensions with a second agent, then verify headline claims at source and rule.
ideas.problem: Fitting BAML's pieces under our structure could hide where its whole structure serves the work better or worse.
ideas.stands: Done; our structure served the case as well or better on all ten dimensions (judged). It corrected one card, found two stale lines, and showed borrows of 10 to 40 lines [E].
ideas.next: Decide whether the five borrows earn a refuter pass; none has had one.
ideas.origin: My question during the BAML sweep

ideas.name: Map store with bounded chunk readers
ideas.how: Chunk by heading (6,000 characters at most [S]); fresh reader per chunk writes a file; script validates; one writer ingests; resume from pending state.
ideas.problem: We want relations extracted from a big document set without one agent reading everything or long reports passing through the orchestrator.
ideas.stands: Built in the clinic testbed: 51 chunks over 11 files read and ingested [M]; 3,361 records [M]; 11 synthetic tests pass [M]. Tokens, time and build cost were not measured.
ideas.next: Reuse the file-handback and single-writer pattern for bulk extraction, for example FixFlow invariants from docs.

ideas.name: Hypothesis table and challengeable settled facts
ideas.how: Hypotheses H1-H18 carry a status, basis and owning analyst. Settled rows go into args as given; an analyst may challenge one with evidence.
ideas.problem: We want open questions tracked with an owner and what would settle each, while agents skip resolved points but can still correct a wrong settled fact.
ideas.stands: The table is in use, updated at the first gate. The challenge channel is specified in design v3 only. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Update as my answers arrive; pass the settled rows into args.

ideas.name: One fact, one command
ideas.how: One command checks a fact before it becomes a rule, recorded verified or contradicted. Each first-deploy step carries command, expected result and planted-failure run.
ideas.problem: An unchecked agent report once produced a false harness rule, and first-deploy steps can be ticked without proof. We want facts backed by evidence.
ideas.stands: Adopted from phase 1 of harness v2; costs one line in a brief. Not yet tested. Planned baseline: count which of the root's 15 [M] lessons are environment facts one command could check.
ideas.next: Run the default-mode write probe before that build; add the line to briefs.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; Harness v2 design

ideas.name: Scripts before agents
ideas.how: Models find things; scripts decide whether a finding is closed. The gate, audit, planner and parser are scripts that spend no tokens.
ideas.problem: In the testbed, ideas kept as prose in a brief or model re-checks mostly failed. We want scripts, not models, making every check a script can.
ideas.stands: Standing rule of harness v2. Testbed record: 33 [M] practised dropped ideas worked and 38 [M] failed, mostly as prose. The scripts themselves have not run live.
ideas.next: Build the six no-token scripts in phase 3 order.

ideas.name: Plan-check section in the orchestration document
ideas.how: Add a plan-check section, lane arithmetic in the cost section and machine limits in constraints; no plan runs before it passes.
ideas.problem: The orchestration document has no dependency graph, footprint check or lane arithmetic, and states capacity facts as rules instead of measured limits.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 section 0. Nothing has changed in the document yet; the edit belongs to the ship plan's PR.
ideas.next: I decide whether and when to write it.

ideas.name: Knowledge-store steps in the phase routine
ideas.how: A plan section 0 bullet: look up before escalating, diff lookups at first commit and PR-ready, record before PR-ready, close at phase end.
ideas.problem: A store nobody consults helps nothing, and escalating a tier without a lookup pays the top tier for a repeat.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design: proposed text only, not applied, conditional on the pilot saying go. Compliance is self-reported, no hook. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Add the bullet to the ship plan after a pilot go (decision KS-D10).

ideas.name: Knowledge-store log and CLAUDE.md trim
ideas.how: A prospective log with a checkpoint date in the OWNER-VIEW page, and a CLAUDE.md PR that swaps verified narratives for one-line rules.
ideas.problem: A store nobody consults helps nothing, and the always-loaded CLAUDE.md file stays long.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design, conditional on a pilot go; not applied and not yet tested. Under go-minimal only declarative entries are wired in and trimmed.
ideas.next: Run it as the wire-in step after the pilot, once decisions KS-D10 and KS-D11 are ruled.

ideas.name: Orchestrator decides; subagents only gather and verify
ideas.how: Main session sets hypotheses, reads every result, makes calls. Subagents gather, analyse, verify; a cheaper verdict may narrow a deeper brief, never remove it.
ideas.problem: We want all judgement in one place, so a cheap agent's first impression never becomes a decision by inertia and never silently cancels a deeper investigation.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design (v3) as a rule. The records show the main session judging, but no subagent output has yet been audited for being treated as a decision.
ideas.next: Run the first workflows under this rule and check no subagent output is treated as a decision.

ideas.name: Judgement-free discovery
ideas.how: First-stage agents return constants, lines, names, commands and exit codes, never a comparison, severity or verdict. The gate or analyst compares values.
ideas.problem: We want to stop a cheap first-stage impression from becoming a top-priority finding by inertia, and keep what the orchestrator reads bounded by schema, not prose.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design and applied to every discovery brief; this compile also states the rule. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: After discovery, check that no map fact carries a severity or verdict.

ideas.name: Return contract: value or null, with coverage count
ideas.how: Every run resolves to a value or null. The script returns results, missing, not-started and coverage; the first gate re-runs or waives each gap.
ideas.problem: A missing or crashed agent result must never be read by us as 'nothing found'.
ideas.stands: Designed as a rule at the first gate. Not yet tested as a rule; the discovery stage reported 16/16 [M] coverage.
ideas.next: Implement and test the contract in the discovery script.

ideas.name: Write the gate record before the next workflow
ideas.how: The gate record is written to the repo and confirmed on disk before the next workflow starts, so every analyst gets the settled facts.
ideas.problem: The deep-dive analysts started without the first gate record, because a shell quoting failure delayed it. We want the decision trail never lost.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a plan rule and stated as a lesson from both gates. No analyst's output depended on the missing file, because the substance was in the brief (qualitative).
ideas.next: Check the file exists before each dispatch; make the gate record a required step.

ideas.name: Plan sha in PR body, with resume fetch
ideas.how: The PR body starts with the plan commit id. On resume, fetch origin, diff from that id to origin/main and re-read only changed sections.
ideas.problem: A restarted or compacted session does not know which plan version it used, and can miss an amendment because git updates origin/main only on fetch.
ideas.stands: Reviewer ruling adopt; the fetch line is adopted in its narrow one-line form. Not yet tested. Pass test: each recorded sha equals the remote main head at that moment.
ideas.next: Add the fetch line to the plan's resume section; use it on the first phase draft PR.

ideas.name: Phase opening, precedence and journal rules bundle
ideas.how: Small written rules: document precedence, explicit skill start, fetch before resume, pasted opening block, cause tags, three-push CI stop, live PR body fetch.
ideas.problem: Our phase routine can skip steps or trust the wrong document. I want small written rules so each phase opens, runs and closes the same way.
ideas.stands: Designed from the Dex Horthy sweep; not yet tested here. Umbrella over many single rules, eight adopt and the rest trial. FixFlow only; no bottleneck record names these skips.
ideas.next: Fold the adopt lines into ship plan section 0, then test each as its own record shows.

ideas.name: One-sentence source-precedence rule in ship plan
ideas.how: One sentence in plan section 0 ranks my correction, plan on main, Plan @ sha, design note; CLAUDE.md and code win on stack facts.
ideas.problem: When the journal, the plan, a design note and CLAUDE.md disagree, a fresh agent has no stated order for which one wins.
ideas.stands: Designed, not yet tested. It stays out of CLAUDE.md on purpose to keep that file short. The test plants two conflicts in the P1 cold-resume fact set.
ideas.next: Plant two conflicts; a fresh Sonnet agent passes if it reports the journal value and stricter rule with source.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; refuter split it by domain

ideas.name: Move 'Start here' pointer to ship plan
ideas.how: One-row swap in CLAUDE.md's doc map so 'Start here' points to the ship plan section 0 instead of the July handoff.
ideas.problem: CLAUDE.md still sends a fresh session to the July handoff, so a cold agent starts from the wrong document.
ideas.stands: Designed, not yet tested. Pushing context into every session was looked at and set aside; only the one-row edit stays.
ideas.next: Fresh Sonnet agent, neutral prompt: pass if it opens ship plan section 0 first in 3 of 3 runs [T].

ideas.name: Phase id comes from me, never inferred
ideas.how: One line in the orchestration skill's start step: the phase id comes from my opening message or skill arguments; if missing, the session asks.
ideas.problem: Concurrent phases are allowed and branch names do not name phases, so a session could pick the wrong phase.
ideas.stands: Designed as a one-line edit; not yet tested. Pass is zero sessions naming a phase different from my opening message across the next 5 phase sessions [T].
ideas.next: Make the edit, then count mismatches over 5 phase sessions [T].
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; skills as routine

ideas.name: Fetch live PR body before every body-file write
ideas.how: One clause in section 0: before each body-file write, fetch the live PR body with gh and edit that text, never a rebuilt copy.
ideas.problem: Rewriting a PR body from a stale copy silently loses journal lines and ticked boxes.
ideas.stands: Designed, not yet tested. Check at the close of P1, P2 and P3 by reading each PR body's edit history; pass is zero unexplained losses [T].
ideas.next: Add the clause, then read the edit history of 3 PRs [T].

ideas.name: Save-rule, run provenance and skill retirement
ideas.how: Keep a script only after a second use or a failure; save it as run with args and brief; run skill retire checks.
ideas.problem: Workflows are written per task and not saved, and without the script, args and reviewer brief a run cannot be re-run or audited.
ideas.stands: Adopted in narrowed form, not yet tested. Pass by P10 [T]: every saved script names at least 2 dated uses or a failure id.
ideas.next: Write the rules into the evidence rules; run retire checks at the phase closes the plan names.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; ad hoc practice since one commit

ideas.name: Explicit effort on every reviewer and implementer launch
ideas.how: One line in section 0: launch reviewers and implementers with an effort from the plan, via a Workflow agent call, never an inheriting path.
ideas.problem: An agent launched with no effort setting silently inherits the orchestrator's effort, so reviewers may run at the wrong level and cost more.
ideas.stands: Listed as adopt, narrowed, though both reviewers scored it trial; not yet tested. Check over the first 3 phase PRs that every launch shows explicit effort [T].
ideas.next: Check whether the Agent tool or agent-definition settings accept an effort field.

ideas.name: Secrets passed by variable name in briefs
ideas.how: In four phase briefs, secrets are passed by variable name; records name the variable, never the value; agents never read a .env file.
ideas.problem: Phases that handle secrets, such as the backup dump and Cloudflare calls, could leak values into records, PR bodies or agent context.
ideas.stands: Designed for four named phases only; not yet tested. At each close a local exact-value scan of diff, PR body and evidence must find 0 [T].
ideas.next: Accept the clause for the four phases, then run the scan at each close.

ideas.name: Escalation ladder: Sonnet, then Opus, then Fable
ideas.how: Cheap model first; a caught failure gets one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable. Solve once at the lowest capable tier and store it.
ideas.problem: I want the cheap model first, yet it will fail some hard work outright, and the average gap between tiers hides that hard tail.
ideas.stands: Modelled on guessed inputs: at middle values 25.7 [G] cheap-call equivalents and 21.2 % [G] wrong per piece, against 29.9 [G] and 11.2 % [G] for the strong model alone.
ideas.next: No fix agreed yet; the gate and ladder are shared by all three ways of working, so report them separately.

ideas.name: Five-phase harness build order with dependencies
ideas.how: Phase 1 machine, 2 check, 3 gate and review scripts, 4 first use, 5 token budget. Hard order: 1 before 2, 2 before 4.
ideas.problem: We have 21 problems to fix and want to build them in the order the evidence supports.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; phase 1 has started with read-only work and its findings exist. The order follows the record: machine first (24 [M] power-offs), review third, tokens last.
ideas.next: I take the phase 1 actions that need me.

ideas.name: Machine-appliable patches for shared docs
ideas.how: Children write their proposed shared-document edits as a patch that a script applies, so the root no longer rewrites each one.
ideas.problem: Only the root writes shared documents, and that makes the root a serial bottleneck we want to remove.
ideas.stands: Idea only, suggested in a sweep card's transfer note. Not built, not tested.
ideas.next: Prototype it with tests that catch documentation drift.

ideas.name: Advisory CI check on PR bodies
ideas.how: A dependency-free workflow checks PR bodies for a resolving plan line, task list, journal heading and a reviewer verdict naming the head commit.
ideas.problem: Whether the phase routine ran is self-reported, so a missing plan line, journal heading or reviewer verdict raises no alarm.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. Top trial 3 of the Horthy sweep; about 40 lines of YAML [E]; advisory on drafts, failing when ready.
ideas.next: Build in P1-ci; over the first 5 code-phase PRs [T] count real catches against false alarms.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, checks into code

ideas.name: Gate-script hygiene: tagged results and clean inputs
ideas.how: Tag agent results null, error or value; build skeptic inputs by pure function; check self-listed reads against the transcript; rename 'reasoning' to 'explanation'.
ideas.problem: A schema failure could look like a usage-limit null, a skeptic could get contaminated inputs, and a script could trust an agent's own list of reads.
ideas.stands: Trial, unrefuted and not yet tested. Refuters narrowed all four to FixFlow only: no dead reviewer read as clean and no contaminated reviewer is on the testbed record.
ideas.next: Probe what the agent call returns on schema exhaustion, then a stubbed run with one schema error and two nulls.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, borrows from its typed failures

ideas.name: Shape block: signatures and call stack in PR
ideas.how: Before the first code commit, the Opus implementer drafts public signatures and the call stack in the draft PR body. No tool is built.
ideas.problem: On phases that change control flow or add surfaces, design mistakes show up only after the code is written.
ideas.stands: Trial, narrowed, not yet tested. Candidates are the first 4 Opus-owned phases that change control flow [T].
ideas.next: Run it on the first 4 qualifying Opus phases [T]; see whether design mistakes surface earlier.

ideas.name: Script-generated document provenance
ideas.how: A script writes metadata frontmatter (git commit and branch) and citations use commit-pinned permalinks; only that script is pre-approved.
ideas.problem: Documents may carry placeholder or unverifiable provenance, so a reader cannot tell which commit a claim was written against.
ideas.stands: Deferred: it went over the sweep's cap, so no refuter has ruled on it and no measurement is defined.
ideas.next: Decide whether to give it a refuter pass; that would settle trial or park.

ideas.name: Paste-to-open-a-phase block
ideas.how: A 5 to 8 line block in plan section 0, with separate code and operations first steps, naming only steps that leave no trace.
ideas.problem: A new phase session can skip the steps that leave no trace, and nobody can tell afterwards.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. The evidence behind it is a single anecdote, so we test it on our own phases first.
ideas.next: Open the first 4 phases with it [T]; a cheap extraction plus gh and git checks verify each named step.

ideas.name: 'Mirror these files' field in Sonnet briefs
ideas.how: Each Sonnet implementation brief names 1 to 3 existing files to mirror, which the explorer agent can fill in.
ideas.problem: Sonnet implementers write code that does not match the patterns already in the repo.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. The test is a blind paired probe rather than a PR count: 4 tasks, each with and without the line, 8 sessions [T].
ideas.next: Run the 8 sessions [T]; a blind Opus judge scores each diff; scores decide if we keep the field.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; refuter narrowed it

ideas.name: Two failed corrections, then a fresh session
ideas.how: After two failed corrections: commit and push, journal the failure, resume in a new session; a failed subagent gets a fresh brief.
ideas.problem: Repeated corrections pile failed attempts into one session's context, and the box still does not close.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. It aims to keep long windows short. Applies to the first 10 phase sessions from P0a [T].
ideas.next: Log each firing; record whether the fresh session closes the box with zero further corrections.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; restart rather than correct

ideas.name: Script the mechanical phase-close sequence
ideas.how: Script only the mechanical close steps (Plan @ line, OWNER-VIEW page updated, verdict names the commit); a cheap extractor counts omitted steps.
ideas.problem: Phase-close steps are done from memory and can be left out.
ideas.stands: Gated trial, not yet tested. Six mechanical close steps are counted after the first three phases [T]. A whole-phase driver was considered and set aside.
ideas.next: After P1 and the next two closes, count omitted steps among six [T].
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep; control flow in code

ideas.name: Rename VERDICT.reasoning to explanation
ideas.how: Grep committed transcripts for refusals (costs zero tokens), then rename the verdict field to explanation at the next brief edit.
ideas.problem: A required 'reasoning' field in the skeptic's verdict can trigger a documented refusal, a billed reply that may not match the schema and costs a verdict.
ideas.stands: Trial, not applied, not yet tested. The twelve skeptic verdicts [M] all came back, so no refusal is on record. Benefit unproven; cost is one word.
ideas.next: Grep the skeptic and lost-refuter transcripts for refusals; propose the rename at the next edit either way.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after Anthropic refusals docs

ideas.name: Add description text to output schemas
ideas.how: Test whether a schema property description reaches the model; if so, define each severity and verdict value once in a shared constant.
ideas.problem: Our output schemas carry no description, so P0 to P3 are defined nowhere and word limits live only in script comments the model never sees.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. Baseline to beat: 8 of 12 skeptic verdicts lowered a severity [M]; 4 of 12 survived [M]. BAML's own rendering evidence was judged not to transfer.
ideas.next: Run the one-agent probe; drop it if descriptions do not reach the subagent, otherwise edit the schemas.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, reframed by the refuter

ideas.name: One constants table for verdicts and buckets
ideas.how: A single table of about 15 lines [E] generates both the schema enums and the bucket mapping, with citation statuses folded in.
ideas.problem: A verdict value could be added to a schema without a matching bucket in the gate script, leaving results unclassified.
ideas.stands: Trial, unrefuted and not yet tested. It would make bucket totality structural: a verdict cannot exist without a bucket.
ideas.next: In the stub harness, add a verdict with no bucket and confirm the test fails.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, structural borrow from exhaustive matching

ideas.name: Fix stale analyst-cap lines in the design
ideas.how: Edit two lines of the orchestration design so they match the current version, which never truncates a P0 or P1.
ideas.problem: The design says findings are sliced to 12, but a later section says the script never cuts a P0 or P1, so two readings coexist.
ideas.stands: Idea, not yet applied. The BAML structural comparison found the two stale lines; the ruling names them for the design's next edit.
ideas.next: Apply at the next orchestration-design edit.

ideas.name: Give sweep assessors the design text and rules
ideas.how: The next sweep's assessment brief carries the output-schema text and the RT-01 to RT-07 rules, so overlap with program law is caught at assessment, not left to the refuter.
ideas.problem: Our assessment stage did not read the design documents, so ideas that were already program law were rated as new and only the refuter caught it.
ideas.stands: Idea, not yet tested. Observed cost: 8 of 24 adopt calls were already program law [M]. Fewer repeated assessments are expected, not measured.
ideas.next: Add the note at the next orchestration-design edit and use it in the next sweep brief.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, ruling on the assessment stage

ideas.name: Verify facts I state, inline
ideas.how: The orchestrator checks a checkable fact with a grep or command and journals verified or contradicted; contradictions return to me, no research agent.
ideas.problem: A mid-phase correction from me about code or environment can be wrong, and agents may act on it unchecked or silently override it.
ideas.stands: Trial over phases P1 to P3, not yet tested. The test target is that 100% [T] of checkable-fact entries carry a verified or contradicted line.
ideas.next: Classify every correction during P1 to P3 and count entries with the line.

ideas.name: Invoke the orchestration skill at phase start
ideas.how: A zero-cost habit: call the orchestration skill at phase start and prompt the close step explicitly, with no new phase-start or phase-close skills.
ideas.problem: A skill may not load from its description alone, so a phase's instructions might never be read.
ideas.stands: Trial, not yet tested. It measures whether auto-loading works by checking 3 plain-prompt sessions [T] for a skill call before the first brief or commit.
ideas.next: Open 3 sessions with a plain prompt and count those where the skill loaded first.

ideas.name: Thought structures (tree, forest, graph) rejected
ideas.how: Branch and merge several reasoning paths in a tree, forest or graph, with a judge or vote, before answering.
ideas.problem: We hoped structured multi-branch reasoning would improve agent output and fixes over a single chain.
ideas.stands: Parked: outside studies show gains on puzzles with a 2023 model [S], and at equal compute plain sampling matches them [S]. Not built, not tested here.
ideas.next: Use candidate fixes chosen by an executed check; the three-candidate replay at frozen commits stays my call (D20).

ideas.name: Scale process weight to task size
ideas.how: A one-line change needs only a prompt, small issues skip research, and the process weight is calibrated by repetition.
ideas.problem: A one-line change should not carry the full research, plan and implement process.
ideas.stands: Parked: the evidence is anecdotal, and the orchestration guide's section 3 already scales work by task size, so nothing new is needed.
ideas.next: None; revisit only if measured evidence appears.

ideas.name: Autonomous refactor loop (Ralph) for style rules
ideas.how: A loop on a cloud VM ran about 6 hours [S] from style rules and produced 20 commits [S].
ideas.problem: Repetitive refactors cost human time, and we wanted to hand them to a loop.
ideas.stands: Parked: the outside result was a PR of about 20,000 lines [S] that was never merged and had about 100 conflicts [S] two days later.
ideas.next: Reopen only if phase-sized loop PRs are measured.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep, after Geoff Huntley's Ralph

ideas.name: Outside observer and ban-expensive-model controls
ideas.how: One Claude watching another through tmux, per-task requests for the costly model, and borrowing HumanLayer's research-plan-implement skills.
ideas.problem: We wanted an outside check of worker state, a spend control, and no dependence on one vendor's tooling.
ideas.stands: Parked: tmux is absent on this PC and phase sessions are not tmux panes; with one developer requester equals approver. Nothing taken as a dependency: pin and copy, never depend.
ideas.next: None; reopen if we add a second approver or tmux sessions.

ideas.name: Brief lint and dry-run flag in scripts
ideas.how: A pure in-script check runs before any agent call, and a dry-run flag returns assembled prompts and schemas instead of calling agents.
ideas.problem: I want hand-edits to a brief to be safe and reviewable before we spend: no dropped context block, no leaked tier word, no pasted raw schema.
ideas.stands: Parked after a refuter pass. The agent call already rejects bad schemas, one concatenation adds the context block, and diffing the saved script gives the text diff. No brief edit has broken anything on record.
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if a hand-edit of a brief ever breaks a run.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after its offline build and parse companions

ideas.name: Categorical rubric instead of numeric likelihood
ideas.how: Replace model-asserted 0 to 1 likelihood numbers in schemas with a defined enum such as slow, medium or fast.
ideas.problem: Fields like likelihood for this fleet carry a number the model asserts and that may mean little.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted on committed data. 53 values fell over 17 distinct ones; the top three cover 15 of 53 (28%) [M]. The trial threshold already fails; no script decision reads the number.
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if a script decision starts reading the number.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a community talk on categorical grading

ideas.name: Evidence fields before verdict in every contract
ideas.how: In each return contract, put explanation and evidence properties before verdict and severity, all required.
ideas.problem: Format-restricted output may lower accuracy if the answer key comes before the reasoning, so we wanted reasoning first.
ideas.stands: Parked after a refuter pass. Agents already work through a tool loop before one final structured-output call, and a reasoning-style first field is a known refusal trigger. The evidence was 2024 non-reasoning models [S].
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if agents start answering without a tool loop.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, after a 2024 paper and practitioner threads

ideas.name: Report directive text found in fetched pages
ideas.how: A research-contract rule and field so a reader reports instructions found inside a source instead of acting on them.
ideas.problem: BAML's docs open with an instruction addressed to an AI reader, which is an instruction inside fetched content; we want that noticed and reported.
ideas.stands: Parked after a refuter pass. Subagents already treat tool output as data and handled the notice correctly. We have no injection incident on record.
ideas.next: Nothing now; it returns if a fetched page ever steers an agent.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, observed in its docs

ideas.name: Prompt optimiser (GEPA) over a test corpus
ideas.how: BAML's beta optimiser rewrites prompt text and type descriptions, scored by the project's tests.
ideas.problem: We tune our briefs by hand and would like a way to improve them against a score.
ideas.stands: Parked as premature: it needs a scored test corpus we lack, an install and API keys. Not tested. Its one useful rule is already kept as infrastructure failures apart from content failures.
ideas.next: Revisit once we hold a scored corpus of brief runs.
ideas.origin: BAML sweep, from the DSPy authors' optimiser

ideas.name: Fast mode for a fleet of subagents
ideas.how: Switch the faster output mode on for the subagents of a large fan-out, so the run takes less time on the clock.
ideas.problem: A large fan-out takes long on the clock even when its token cost is accepted.
ideas.stands: Asked for on a run of 132 [M] agents on 3 November; fast mode was on for that session, and its effect on time and tokens was not measured.
ideas.next: Time one fan-out with it on and off, and note what it does to usage.
ideas.origin: My request in a chat of 3 November

ideas.name: Borrow from distributed systems, databases and parallel computing
ideas.how: Treat agent problems as known systems problems first: caching, consistency, indexes, scheduling, trees. A lecture list maps each harness problem to its lectures.
ideas.problem: Agent engineering is too new to have its own textbooks, and vendor guidance did not stop me needing a harness.
ideas.stands: Built on 11 November: 52 [M] research agents checked 44 [M] course series; a list and transcript library cover six core courses. PAR-22 applies one such structure.
ideas.next: Use the list when a package starts; record which lecture an idea came from.
ideas.origin: My brief in chats of 1, 2 and 11 November
