themes.title: Skills, agents and tools
themes.covers: Skill packages, saved project agents, tool lists and outside tools worth borrowing.
intro: A skill package teaches agents one domain; a project agent is a saved agent definition with its own model, tools and instructions. PR #185 holds 13 skill packages and 11 project agents for FixFlow.
The ideas here cover what to package, how to keep each agent’s fixed start small, how to know a skill is used, and which outside tools are worth borrowing.

ideas.name: Local GPU speech-to-text for blocked recordings
ideas.how: Download audio-only streams and transcribe them with faster-whisper distil-large-v3 in a throwaway uv environment on the RTX 5070. Nothing is installed system-wide.
ideas.problem: YouTube blocks caption requests from this machine's address, so talks cannot be read from captions.
ideas.stands: In use: 9 recordings, about 7 hours, 172 MB [M], transcribed in about 12 minutes [M] on GPU at 19-45x real time [M]; CPU with other sessions loading managed 2.7x [M].
ideas.next: Reuse it for the 12-Factor Factories talk when published.

ideas.name: Recovery runbook skill and recovery operator agent
ideas.how: A runbook skill: dump inventory, paused-project restore policy, throwaway Postgres 17 restore with count and sequence checks; a Sonnet agent runs local steps only.
ideas.problem: Production is down; we must find which database backups survive and prove a dump restores before rebuilding anything.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and Sonnet agent in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. R2 listing and live restores stay with me. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Run it on P0a; I run the R2 listing and restores.

ideas.name: Android background-execution skill and analyst
ideas.how: A sourced skill on library internals and maker autostart paths, plus an Opus analyst citing findings and claiming no field reliability without device evidence.
ideas.problem: The geofence, on-duty ping and job-travel tasks can fail silently on Android 12-15 and maker-customised phones, and analysts need cited facts on library internals.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and analyst in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. Covers expo-location 18.0.10 [S], expo-task-manager 12.0.6 [S] and expo-modules-core 2.2.3 [S]. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Run it on plan phase P5-spike.

ideas.name: Android field-debugging skill and device debugger agent
ideas.how: A sourced read-only skill for adb, dumpsys and logcat capture; a Sonnet agent returns a device-evidence table, never installing, clearing, force-stopping or judging reliability.
ideas.problem: The truth about geofencing and offline queues lives on phones, and the field APK is older than main, so reading code gives only candidates.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and agent in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. Not yet run on a device.
ideas.next: Use it in drain sessions P4a and P4b.

ideas.name: Self-hosting skill and architect agent
ideas.how: A sourced skill (restore-and-triage, tunnel guardrails) plus FixFlow's design content; a Sonnet high-effort agent drafts compose files, tables of my steps and local restore drills.
ideas.problem: Moving production to my own box needs compose, tunnel, backup and power-loss steps drafted and checked without agents touching the host.
ideas.stands: Built: skill and Sonnet agent in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. I run every host step. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Use it for P3a.

ideas.name: Turn sourced skills into pinned project agents
ideas.how: Each sourced skill is distilled into a .claude/agents file with prompt, tool list and pinned model; workflows and sessions call it by agent type.
ideas.problem: Our subagents lack domain knowledge (Android background work, Odoo, recovery, security review), and outside skills must reach them at the right price tier without manual loading.
ideas.stands: Built: applied to 11 agent definitions [M] in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. Not yet run, so no results. The design notes Haiku could take extractors, scans and table generation.
ideas.next: Call the agents from workflows and measure; source the four priority-1 skills.

ideas.name: Agent file: pinned model, tools, preloaded skill
ideas.how: Frontmatter sets name, tools, model (haiku, sonnet or opus), skills and effort; the body is a read-only-unless-told, cite-everything prompt naming a return schema.
ideas.problem: A subagent inherits the session's model and loads nothing unless told, so its role, price tier and tool access need to be fixed in one file.
ideas.stands: Built: 11 fixflow agent definitions [M] in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov, plus the older Haiku explorer already in the repository (12 in all); fields checked against the Claude Code docs on 2026-11-03. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Call the agents from a workflow and measure.
ideas.origin: Skills packages; Claude Code subagent feature

ideas.name: Skill package layout with provenance files
ideas.how: Each package has a SKILL.md, an UPSTREAM.md (repo, commit, paths, licence, taken/changed/rejected), the verbatim licence and references, kept under about 150 KB [S].
ideas.problem: Skills copied from other repos must stay traceable, licensed and small enough to load, so a maintainer can tell what was taken, changed and rejected.
ideas.stands: Built: applied to all 13 packages [M] in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov, conventions written 2026-11-03/04. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check each package against the size and layout rules before merge.

ideas.name: Three skill statuses: sourced, authored, researched
ideas.how: Each package gets one index status: sourced (from an upstream repo), authored (written here) or researched (from fetched web sources, with URL and date).
ideas.problem: A reader needs to know whether a skill's facts came from an outside repo, were written by us, or were gathered from the web.
ideas.stands: Built: the index in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov lists 10 sourced, 1 researched and 2 authored packages [M]. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Keep the index current as packages are added.

ideas.name: FixFlow facts first, cited to path and line
ideas.how: Generic advice shrinks to a rule and reason; words go to repo specifics. Claims cite path and line; web facts cite URL and date.
ideas.problem: Generic outside advice wastes tokens and can mislead agents on this repo, and stale line numbers or vague dates make claims impossible to check.
ideas.stands: Built: the rule set is applied across the packages in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov; facts were re-read on 2026-11-04. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Spot-check the cited lines after the next rebase.

ideas.name: Skills never contradict CLAUDE.md
ideas.how: Any upstream conflict with CLAUDE.md gets a 'Where upstream disagrees' block in the skill and a 'Rejected' line in the provenance file.
ideas.problem: Imported skills carry rules, such as deleting failed queue writes, that would break our project's invariants if an agent obeyed them.
ideas.stands: Built into three skills (offline sync, Expo release, self-hosting) in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov; untested. An upstream rule to delete failed queue writes was rejected, since our outbox never deletes a write.
ideas.next: Keep using it as new skills are added.

ideas.name: No secrets in skills: key names and fingerprints
ideas.how: Real values are cited by path and key name only; a committed value appears as a 12-character [S] hash fingerprint. Agents never open .env files.
ideas.problem: Agents reading config files such as eas.json or .env could copy real tokens or keys into skills, briefs or outputs.
ideas.stands: Built: written into every agent definition checked (PR #185, merged on 13 Nov). Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check it holds when the agents first run.

ideas.name: Read the skill first, even when preloaded
ideas.how: Every agent body opens with an instruction to read its SKILL.md and references first, even though the skills field already preloads it.
ideas.problem: A host that does not preload skills would leave the agent without its rules, so the agent must fetch them itself.
ideas.stands: Built: present in every agent definition read (PR #185, merged on 13 Nov). Not yet tested. CLAUDE.md loads into custom subagents by default.
ideas.next: Check it holds when the agents first run.

ideas.name: Orchestration skill and repo-conventions skill
ideas.how: One project skill carries the context block, schemas, reading rules and routing table; a second packages CLAUDE.md and the deploy traps for implementation sessions.
ideas.problem: Every session's agents need identical briefs, and implementers need the deploy traps, migration numbering and slice boundaries put in front of them.
ideas.stands: Built in part: the orchestration skill is authored in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov (see the main-session contract skill). The repo-conventions skill is not confirmed built. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Confirm whether the repo-conventions skill exists.

ideas.name: fixflow-explorer Haiku-pinned locator agent
ideas.how: A read-only agent pinned to Haiku greps first, reads at most 40 lines [S], and reports path and line for each match, with no verdicts.
ideas.problem: The built-in Explore agent inherits the session's model (Opus here), so a simple where-is-X lookup runs on our most expensive tier.
ideas.stands: Built: the agent file exists in the repo and predates PR #185. Not yet tested; no usage or cost figures.
ideas.next: Measure its cost against the built-in Explore agent.

ideas.name: Odoo import and Pakistan accounting skills with analyst
ideas.how: A sourced Odoo skill (JSON-2, external IDs as idempotency key, reversals) plus a researched Pakistan books skill; an Opus analyst preloads both.
ideas.problem: Money postings must reach Odoo exactly once with Pakistan tax records right, since wrong guesses double-post or drop entries.
ideas.stands: Built: two skills and one agent in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. Every Pakistan fact carries a URL and date. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Use it in phases P9-0a and P9-0b; the accountant and I decide the tax position.

ideas.name: [owner] stop markers in agent procedures
ideas.how: Steps only I may do carry an [owner] marker; the agent stops, hands me the exact command, and resumes from my pasted output.
ideas.problem: Agents must never deploy, restore over live data, rotate keys, message people or install on a phone; those steps need me.
ideas.stands: Built: used in all 13 skills [M] and the agent definitions in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check it holds when the agents first run.

ideas.name: Orchestration contract skill for the main session
ideas.how: An authored skill the main session loads each phase: routing table, agent registry, context block, schemas, script contract, plan rules. Not preloaded into subagents.
ideas.problem: The main session must recall tier routing, output schemas and session rules each phase without re-reading long design documents.
ideas.stands: Built: authored on 2026-11-04 from the design and ship plan; in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Check it holds over the first phases that load it.

ideas.name: ks command-line tool plus skill as the agent interface
ideas.how: A zero-dependency Node command-line tool called through Bash (lookup, verify, show, outcome, claim, record, close), with a skill carrying the procedure.
ideas.problem: Subagents and workflow agents need one way into the knowledge store that works with no configuration or approval prompt.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; nothing built. No hook in v1. A skill description at its ceiling would add about 620 tokens per call [E].
ideas.next: Build the tool in KS-2, the skill after; I decide KS-D15 (MCP wrapper) and KS-D21 (edit-time hook).

ideas.name: CI check for skill and agent frontmatter
ideas.how: A Node CI step fails bad skill frontmatter (name equals folder, description under 1024 characters [S]) and agent fields; flags a stale head number.
ideas.problem: Skill files can rot silently: a missing name, a name that differs from its folder, a stale Alembic head number.
ideas.stands: Adopted in the Horthy sweep, to be added to P1-ci or P1. Not yet built; a one-off version of the gate was run once.
ideas.next: A commit dropping the name must fail CI; adopt for good once at least 1 [T] real rot is caught.

ideas.name: Hooks: stop hook and tool-event heartbeat
ideas.how: Settings-based Claude Code hooks: a stop hook blocks a session on a failed claim check, and a heartbeat is fed by tool events.
ideas.problem: We want claims checked and progress shown automatically; today nothing blocks a session on a failed claim check or shows progress from tool events.
ideas.stands: Deferred: harness v2 keeps hooks off for now (decision D17). Root-gate versions of the same checks need no hook. No gain shown yet.
ideas.next: I decide D17 on reopening hooks for two uses.

ideas.name: Wrap conditional CLAUDE.md rules in 'important if'
ideas.how: Conditional rules sit in important-if tags, always-true content stays bare, in the wrapped arm of the CLAUDE.md trial (E1), plus 3 [S] oblique probes (which test a rule without naming it).
ideas.problem: Long CLAUDE.md files get skimmed, and rules that matter only for certain tasks dilute the always-true ones.
ideas.stands: Trial: only as one arm of E1; the technique alone fell to the ruling that keeps every rule. Horthy's adherence claims carry no measurements. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Run E1's wrapped arm with 10 direct and 3 oblique probes (which test a rule without naming it) [S]; compare pass rate with the bare file.

ideas.name: Split CLAUDE.md by runtime with nested files
ideas.how: Move one-runtime material to backend and mobile CLAUDE.md files; keep cross-runtime rules and a pointer index in the root. Test briefs and diff-only reviewers too.
ideas.problem: Our CLAUDE.md is 390 lines [M], about twice the length where adherence is said to fall, so every task pays for detail it may not need.
ideas.stands: Trial: a split arm of E1 on a branch. A nested file was seen attaching in a workflow subagent on Read here. Pass rate not yet compared.
ideas.next: Compare probe pass rate, split versus full, with the frozen probe set plus 3 oblique probes (which test a rule without naming it) [S].

ideas.name: One-off sweep for contradicting instructions
ideas.how: One fresh Opus sweep after the skills land, over CLAUDE.md, memory, the ship plan, the orchestration design and each skill; a refuter checks hits.
ideas.problem: Always-loaded instructions can contradict each other (CLAUDE.md points fresh sessions to the July handoff, not the ship plan), and fact-drift checks do not catch that.
ideas.stands: Trial: run once, no standing check. Each hit quotes both texts and the different action an agent would take. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Count refuter-confirmed contradictions and fix each at its source.

ideas.name: Phase-scoped skill trigger tally
ideas.how: At each phase close, search transcripts for skill calls and skill-preloading agents; tabulate against the phases each description names.
ideas.problem: Skills may never load in the phases their descriptions name, and nothing shows it.
ideas.stands: Trial: to run over the first six phase sessions [T]. A cap and pruning were refuted in the sweep. Not yet run.
ideas.next: Tally across P0a, P0b, P1, P2a, P2b-1 and P2b-2 against the plan's phase table.

ideas.name: A ks guide command printed from command definitions
ideas.how: The guide command would print guidance from the same command definitions as the tool, with a test that every subcommand appears.
ideas.problem: We worried knowledge-store documentation could drift from the tool's real commands.
ideas.stands: Parked: the tool and its skill live in one repo and one commit, so version skew cannot arise; the store is also unbuilt. Not tested.
ideas.next: Nothing needed; the refutation rests on the tool and skill shipping together.

ideas.name: Install BAML language and CLI in the harness
ideas.how: BAML generates a client and parses replies with schema-aligned parsing; the Claude Code route needs a canary-only client running one claude -p per turn.
ideas.problem: We hoped for typed prompt functions, lenient parsing of agent outputs and built-in tests.
ideas.stands: Parked, not installed. Three grounds: a second billing path or opaque orchestrator, no resume in its runner, a parser that silently drops list elements. Its distinctive ideas already exist here, stricter.
ideas.next: Would come back only with a client running Claude Code subagents with tools and a recorded failure class it addresses.

themes.title: Measure, model and test ideas fairly
themes.covers: How we measure and test: transcript tallies, number tags, replays on recorded data, held-out protocols, system-dynamics and pathway models, and fair tests.
intro: Every number in this document carries a tag that says how sure we are of it. That habit, and most of the measurements in it, came from this theme.

The ideas here are how we measure and how we keep a test fair to the idea it tests: tallies from our own transcripts, replays on recorded work, held-out test sets frozen before the run, models of the whole system, and rules such as testing the strongest form of an idea against the strongest baseline.

ideas.name: Worker sweep and load sampler
ideas.how: Sweep workers (6, 9, 12, 16) while a sampler logs CPU and free memory to CSV; test a pair before approving a second slot.
ideas.problem: We want worker and slot counts chosen from measurement, and memory and CPU visible during checks and drills.
ideas.stands: In use on checks: 6 workers 137.5 s [M], 12 workers 104.7-135.1 s [M]; knee between 6 and 12. Two container checks run together took 266-267 s [M] each, against 220 s [M] for one run alone in the same test.
ideas.next: Run the sampler on the Windows PC itself to diagnose shutdowns and idle-session memory.

ideas.name: Limitations first, no fixes until agreed
ideas.how: List and weigh limitations first; the record and map carry no fixes; we use the ranking to agree the list together.
ideas.problem: Fixing before we agree the limitations would hide which ones matter.
ideas.stands: In use in the library review: 69 [M] limitations listed and weighed, no fixes agreed. A nine-agent solve round was started and stopped at my request; no fix from it was adopted.
ideas.next: Agree the limitation list with me, using the ranking.

ideas.name: Number tags on every figure
ideas.how: Tag every number as measured, estimated, guess or outside figure, with target and illustrative tags added by the harness.
ideas.problem: Readers could not tell a measured number from a guess, so a guess could pass as a result.
ideas.stands: In use across the program documents: [M] measured, [E] estimated, [G] guess, [S] outside figure, plus [T] target and [I] illustrative.
ideas.next: Keep tagging.

ideas.name: Pre-registered, sealed held-out test protocol
ideas.how: Fix the protocol before any arm exists: split commits by date, tune on one part, one main metric, a smallest worthwhile difference, named wording.
ideas.problem: We want every test to settle something, so tuning, the held-out set and the scoring rule are fixed first and wording cannot overclaim.
ideas.stands: In use on the graph test: 65 tune and 75 held-out commits [S]; run clean; smallest detectable difference about 0.09 recall [E]; every arm lost 0.05 to 0.17 [M] tune to held-out.
ideas.next: Reuse the same rules for the wider test and each new experiment.

ideas.name: Evaluation protocol with Amdahl bound
ideas.how: Measure accepted tasks per active human hour; freeze the baseline; change one mechanism at a time; randomise order; keep all attempts; apply Amdahl's bound.
ideas.problem: We had no agreed way to judge whether a workflow change is an improvement.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed; no 3x or 5x claim is established. 20 % avoidable effort gives at most 1.25x [I]; 8 [M] run records are schema-valid but carry null telemetry.
ideas.next: Size the review and orchestrator bottlenecks with the bound before building.

ideas.name: Slow-path diagnosis: Windows to Docker port
ideas.how: Measure machine, worker and VM CPU during a parallel pass, and per-query latency from Windows against inside the container.
ideas.problem: Adding test workers stopped helping, and we wanted to find where the time actually went.
ideas.stands: Testbed measurement: machine at 42 % [M] of 24 processors; six workers used 2.45 [M] cores; a trivial query took 0.63 ms [M] from Windows, 0.13 ms [M] in the container.
ideas.next: Check whether workers wait on a network hop before adding more; it points to running tests beside the database.

ideas.name: Window-fill analysis: what fills the context
ideas.how: Classify each context token from growth between calls, weighted by re-reads: fixed start, own output, fetched content, summaries. Also count lookup-only calls.
ideas.problem: Knowing the token total is not enough; we did not know what content fills the windows, so claims about levers were guesses.
ideas.stands: Measured, checked by two refuters: FixFlow fetched content 27-28.5 % [E], 43.6 % [E] re-read by lookup-only calls; testbed own output 53-69 % [M] of growth. Exposures, not savings.
ideas.next: Replay recorded windows with an index; rerun the fill after any lever; run the testbed breakdown on FixFlow orchestrator sessions.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Token report; Clinic testbed

ideas.name: Fixed context overhead measurement
ideas.how: A usage tool breaks down each agent's overhead (tools, MCP, skills, system prompt, memory); a script measures how documentation grows.
ideas.problem: Every session or subagent carries tokens before doing any work, and we did not know how large that fixed start is.
ideas.stands: Measured in the October testbed: about 70k [M] tokens before work (system tools 33,968, MCP 16,599, skills 9,059 [M]). Docs about 338,816 tokens [E].
ideas.next: Trim MCP servers and skills in agent sessions; keep the routed pre-read small.

ideas.name: Replacement graph test with a real engine
ideas.how: Vary facts, algorithm, output form and engine separately; sealed tasks from 140 commits and 50 questions; hops 1 to 6; search, SQLite, graph arms.
ideas.problem: Our first graph test used the weakest query and no real engine, so it could not tell us whether a repo graph helps.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits, run clean, scripted search arm, no agent run. Typed store was ahead of scripted search by +0.076 recall [M], interval +0.036 to +0.118 [M]: clear of zero, though below the 0.09 [E] the protocol had planned as detectable; SQLite and two graph engines gave identical answers [M].
ideas.next: I choose which graph engine to install; then run an agent arm in the pilot.

ideas.name: Scripted search baseline arm
ideas.how: A fixed script does text search for the task's names, paths and route strings, in one and two rounds; not an agent.
ideas.problem: We need to compare every graph against what our sessions do today, which is plain text search.
ideas.stands: Tested on held-out commits: recall 0.625 [M] one round, 0.634 [M] two rounds, median 6 to 8 [M] lookups; tune 0.759 [M]. No agent was run.
ideas.next: Replace it with an agent using ordinary search tools in the pilot.
ideas.origin: Graph test, after the Aider repo map

ideas.name: Pilot of the attested-only map on four files
ideas.how: Four frozen files read under the design by a skeptic and an independent annotator; counts compared, then re-applied under a revised design.
ideas.problem: We wanted to check whether a strictly sourced map recovers the dependency chain a human annotator saw.
ideas.stands: Tested in the testbed: first design 427 attested edges [M], chain not reproduced; revised design 692 edges [M] with 1,166 dangling endpoints [M]. Links through a shared value cannot be joined.
ideas.next: Use grep plus a drift check for repeated constants such as the money limit and Alembic head.

ideas.name: Token tally from session transcripts
ideas.how: Read-only scripts parse every transcript, count each call once per message id, and total calls, tokens and compactions per group and per slice session.
ideas.problem: We did not know where our tokens went or why usage limits hit, so any cut would have been a guess.
ideas.stands: Measured for October and November. November: 4,252.9M [M] cache-read tokens over 184 files; slice sessions 66.4 % [M] by one count; re-measurement agreed within 0.3 % [M].
ideas.next: Rerun the October script on November for per-slice figures, and again after any lever to see its effect.
ideas.origin: Clinic testbed; Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; Token report

ideas.name: Fit-screen the idea sweeps against bottlenecks
ideas.how: Opus mappers placed kept ideas, Sonnet readers screened dropped ones, adjudicators ruled on flags, refuters attacked claimed fits, and a script checked every id.
ideas.problem: Both idea sweeps scored ideas against the FixFlow ship plan, never against our 21 bottlenecks, so their verdicts could not carry over.
ideas.stands: Tested in three workflows with 19 agents, models reading documents only: 87 kept ideas gave 29 fits [M]; 868 dropped gave 142 flagged and 1 promoted [M].
ideas.next: Compile the surviving mechanisms into the build order.

ideas.name: Throughput record from git history
ideas.how: Count commits per day on all branches and first-parent merges onto main with light git log commands, and note gap days.
ideas.problem: We had no before-and-after baseline of how much work lands per day.
ideas.stands: Measured in the testbed: 426 [M] commits since 1 Nov, peak 150 [M] on 6 Nov, 36 [M] first-parent merges onto main. Commit counts are not a quality measure.
ideas.next: Compute before and after any harness change; pair with per-slice token counts.

ideas.name: System-dynamics model of the harness
ideas.how: Eleven stocks with flow equations, nine switchable controllers and four limits; assumptions listed. It shows behaviour, not a forecast.
ideas.problem: Which limit binds first depends on rates, so we want to see how each controller changes the machine before building it.
ideas.stands: Built in the harness v2 page; a refuter checked claims. At October's window of about 2.5 lane-hours [E], tokens are the first limit at any lane count [I].
ideas.next: Replace guessed inputs with measured rates.

ideas.name: Trial harness: transcript accounting and blind scoring
ideas.how: Scripts build per-arm workspaces, read agent transcripts for tokens and peak context, check citations, and blind the arm labels before scoring.
ideas.problem: We want per-agent tokens, tool calls and file reads measured after the fact, and runs scored without knowing which arm they came from.
ideas.stands: Built in the testbed; not yet run on trials, only an extraction comparison exists. Its token figures are characters divided by 4 [E].
ideas.next: Adapt the measuring script to Claude Code's transcript format; it could give FixFlow sub-agent cost per task.

ideas.name: Replay before live
ideas.how: Accept a mechanism by replaying it on the recorded history where possible, and run it record-only before it may refuse anything.
ideas.problem: A gate or review mechanism could refuse good work or miss defects, so we want proof on the record before it can block us.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a standing rule of harness v2, to apply to mechanisms 1 to 6. No mechanism has yet run live under it.
ideas.next: Apply the rule to mechanisms 1 to 6 (decision D15).

ideas.name: Sealed replay with read log
ideas.how: Replay in a clone with no later refs, answer key hashed first, read log from the transcript, one head commit and brief per arm.
ideas.problem: Replaying an old fix chain to test a review method is unfair if the agent can peek at the later fix, finding tables or board.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 3 (mechanism 1), first script at zero tokens; never run. Proof planned: one recorded fix chain, sealed clone against plain worktree.
ideas.next: Write the clone-and-read-log script and test it on two [T] runs; makes replay evidence for B01, B12 and B17 fair.
ideas.origin: Harness v2 design; Dex Horthy sweep

ideas.name: Recurrence audit before any knowledge-store build
ideas.how: Sonnet classifies 72 [M] fix commits, counting a repeat only under three strict tests; an Opus refuter rechecks every counted repeat.
ideas.problem: We have not shown that the same cause ever hits twice in a way a symptom-keyed store could serve, so a build might repay nothing.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design; not yet run. A raw count already shows 3 to 5 same-cause repeats among 48 fix commits on main [M].
ideas.next: I answer KS-D1 (run the audit); Sonnet extracts, Opus refutes. It gives the prior that decides whether to build.

ideas.name: Missed-existing detector with blind re-rule
ideas.how: At record time the author lists prior lookups; detectors flag matches against the store’s existing entries (its roster); author rules same/related/new; reviewer re-rules blind. Unknown stays NULL, never zero.
ideas.problem: A miss of an entry that existed looks the same as a store nobody consulted, so we cannot measure recall or whether embeddings are needed.
ideas.stands: Designed in the knowledge-store design (build planned in KS-2 and KS-3, read at KS-9); a lower bound by construction. Not yet tested; expected under about 0.2 per 8-week window [E].
ideas.next: Build with the write gate (KS-4/5), fixtures in KS-2; counts then give the embedding decision (KS-D16) a real denominator.

ideas.name: Zero-token import-and-caller index replay
ideas.how: At each recorded window's start commit, build an import-and-caller index, count lookups it would answer, and check it lists the files later edited.
ideas.problem: Our sessions spend many calls only reading; we want to know cheaply whether a code index would have answered them before spending agent tokens.
ideas.stands: Designed, not yet run: 54.7 % [M] of calls only read or search. Co-change half is weak, only 432 commits [M]. Proposed pass marks 3 % of tokens, recall 0.8 [T].
ideas.next: I set the pass marks (D23); then run the replay in phase 3 and go live only if it passes.

ideas.name: Record unknown as unknown, never zero
ideas.how: Store an unmeasured value as unknown, and write decisive checks with explicit if-and-raise rather than bare assert.
ideas.problem: If we record missing data as zero, a gap looks like a measured absence and we draw the wrong conclusion.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a stated lesson from the CureFound research results; it matches the repository rule that an unknown evidence value is not zero. Not separately measured.
ideas.next: Apply to every tally and check script.

ideas.name: Frozen validation contract for any map or store
ideas.how: Sealed: 5 [S] cases, 3 arms (map, routed reading, Graphify), 2 [S] runs each, blind scoring; better needs a 0.10 [T] gap in 4 of 5 cases.
ideas.problem: We built maps and stores without testing whether they beat the routed reading we already have, so we want a fair A/B first.
ideas.stands: Designed and frozen in the testbed, never run: 30 runs [S], 16,000 tokens [S] per run; the runs folder is empty. Work moved to context-admission research.
ideas.next: Run it, or a FixFlow copy, before building any map, store or graph; it gives a reusable A/B template.

ideas.name: Measured-rates table feeding planner and governor
ideas.how: The check, merge queue and transcript tally write measured rates (check time, waits, tokens per lane-hour, rounds per slice); every wave updates them.
ideas.problem: We lay out plans on guessed times and an unknown token budget per five-hour window, so we cannot tell which limit comes first.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2; not yet tested. First rates are the check timings 367 s and 230 s [M]; the planner and governor depend on it.
ideas.next: Take phase 2 container gate timings, then the phase 5 per-slice baseline.

ideas.name: Pre-registered evaluation plan with gates and staged budgets
ideas.how: Four arms, gates written in advance, staged budgets with caps, inconclusive at budget exhaustion, and all overhead charged to the treatment.
ideas.problem: We want to stop a harness declaring its own win, so gates and budgets are settled before anything runs.
ideas.stands: Designed in the testbed; stage 1 and a screen ran, stages 2 to 4 did not. Input gates -50 % and -25 % not met: adapter +10.31 % [M], +17.02 % [M].
ideas.next: Copy the template for the next FixFlow memory or token experiment; it accepts the simpler workflow as a valid result.

ideas.name: Tool qualification and G0-G8 gates
ideas.how: Qualify maintained tools (Promptfoo, Langfuse, Phoenix) before writing a runner; use independent oracles, hold-out inaccessibility and a trap list for green-but-empty results.
ideas.problem: Measurement tools can report green or zero when nothing was checked, so we want to catch that before trusting a number.
ideas.stands: Designed in the testbed; no tool installed or run. Registers cover 27 methods and 44 tool source groups [M]; four Promptfoo traps were read from source, not reproduced.
ideas.next: Audit FixFlow's gates for zero tests, skipped tests and defaulted cost fields.

ideas.name: Effectiveness review F01-F10
ideas.how: Four separate measures (quality, context, productivity, cost), a context freshness test, a frozen baseline, and a throwaway synthetic deployment with backup and restore.
ideas.problem: A claim of 3x measures productivity, not quality, and we lacked early proof the system runs and restores.
ideas.stands: Designed in the testbed as proposals only; not yet tested. The illustrative hosting cost stayed under its cap [I].
ideas.next: Walk a clean install and restore early.

ideas.name: Honest cold-resume trial with hashed answer key
ideas.how: Record a hash of the answer file in the PR journal first, commit the file after judging, run on a checkout without it, then check the read log.
ideas.problem: The one test of whether a fresh session can resume our work could pass just by the agent reading the answer file.
ideas.stands: Adopted for phase 1 (P1), narrowed after refuter review; n=1 [S], one rerun if contaminated. Not yet run. Pass: hash first, zero reads of the key.
ideas.next: Apply it in the P1 cold-resume trial; it makes that single resume test trustworthy.

ideas.name: Symmetric reading rule for single-run gaps
ideas.how: A zero-cost reading rule: a single-run gap of a few strict passes counts as no detectable difference for either effort level; cost and task fit then decide.
ideas.problem: One benchmark run per setting cannot separate an effort effect from noise, so we risk over-reading small gaps.
ideas.stands: Adopted for this review's effort decisions only. Source: medium 28 against xhigh 25 of 196 [S] strict passes, one run each, read as no detectable difference.
ideas.next: Apply when the effort dispositions are written; pass is zero statements treating a single-run gap as evidence.

ideas.name: One provenance line in each evidence README
ideas.how: Each evidence README gets one line: exact model id, ids the aliases resolved to, tool version and run date.
ideas.problem: Someone re-running or disputing an evidence folder later cannot tell which model and tool build produced it.
ideas.stands: Adopted, narrowed to one line; standing re-runs on every release were dropped. Not yet tested; pass is 2 of 2 [T] next folders carrying the line.
ideas.next: Add the line to the next two evidence READMEs.

ideas.name: Adoption audits of reference repositories
ideas.how: Source-first audits of six outside projects; adopt small fields (code-shape block, boundary trace, fail-before/pass-after, error retirement) and reject installing runtimes.
ideas.problem: We needed to know which ideas from outside agent projects are worth adopting.
ideas.stands: Adopted narrowly in the clinic testbed; runtimes, webhooks and vector databases rejected. 1,658 [M] files rehashed, none missing; no upstream tests run.
ideas.next: Do not equate a stored token field with spend; verify instruction loading.

ideas.name: 'Sessions:' line in the PR journal
ideas.how: One plain line listing session ids, copied from the scratchpad path, goes into the existing PR journal.
ideas.problem: Transcripts of resumed or multi-session phases are hard to find when we want to audit them.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, run alongside the transcript tally; not yet tested. Audit at least 7 days [S] after close.
ideas.next: On the first 3 [T] closed PRs, check the transcript is found from the branch alone and every session is listed.

ideas.name: Transcript-derived read audit of analysts
ideas.how: A short Node script compares an analyst's self-listed extra reads with the Read and Grep calls in its subagent transcript.
ideas.problem: Analyst reading rules are brief text and extra reads are self-reported and unenforced, so we cannot tell whether an analyst obeyed them.
ideas.stands: Trial from the BAML sweep, unrefuted. Feasibility shown: one lane reader's transcript holds 115 [M] tool-call entries. Mismatch rate not yet measured.
ideas.next: Measure the mismatch rate on one analyst from a committed run; make it standing only if self-reports under-count.

ideas.name: Medium-vs-xhigh effort trial, pass bar first
ideas.how: Replay 12 [S] frozen verifier briefs at medium and xhigh, 3 times each, with an xhigh repeat as noise floor; write the pass bar first.
ideas.problem: Choosing a model effort for reviewers and verifiers is guesswork, and without a rule fixed in advance a comparison can be bent to its result.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, one-off: 12 [S] briefs plus 5 [S] fixtures from closed defects, blind-graded. Not yet tested; the testbed has no effort benchmark.
ideas.next: Select 12 briefs and build 5 fixtures, once I decide that FixFlow should settle its effort choice this way.

ideas.name: Medium-effort verifiers via blind paired shadow runs
ideas.how: A blind medium-effort shadow reruns each non-P0 verifier's brief; 30+ [T] pairs, pass bar set first, 3 repeats per arm, scored against final adjudication.
ideas.problem: Most of our verifiers run at xhigh effort, which costs more, and one outside report says medium often matched or beat it.
ideas.stands: Top trial 1 in the Dex Horthy sweep; not yet tested. Targets: agreement at least incumbent minus 1 [T], medium tokens at most 0.6x [T]. Outside evidence is weaker than first read.
ideas.next: Start in the next review workflows; costs about 30 [E] extra agents; decides whether the xhigh default stays.

ideas.name: Send-back repeat share
ideas.how: Count the share of review send-backs that repeat a class of finding already found earlier.
ideas.problem: We do not know how often a review send-back repeats a finding class we have already seen, so we cannot tell if lessons are being captured.
ideas.stands: Proposed in the library review; not run, so no repeat share exists yet.
ideas.next: Count repeats across the recorded review rounds.

ideas.name: Rerun knowledge-store refuter set at high effort
ideas.how: Rerun the committed refuter workflow on frozen inputs at Opus high effort twice and compare with the xhigh outcomes.
ideas.problem: We do not know whether verifiers run at xhigh need to be that expensive.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, conditional: runs only if xhigh verifier spend is at least 20% [T] of use. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Wait for the usage-recording figure; if spend clears 20% [T], run it.

ideas.name: Transcript tally at phase close
ideas.how: A read-only Node script scores 8 [T] routine steps from session transcript tool calls and compares them with the closing message.
ideas.problem: Routine steps that leave no git or GitHub trace look the same whether done or skipped, so we cannot check compliance from outside.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep (top trial 2); about 100 lines [E]. Not yet tested. Must run within 7 days [S] of a phase close, before transcripts are pruned.
ideas.next: Run after the first three phases within seven days; shows whether an outside compliance check works without hooks.

ideas.name: Cause tag on journal entries for my corrections
ideas.how: A one-word tag (harness, plan or product) on each journal entry that records one of my corrections; count harness-tagged shapes that repeat.
ideas.problem: When I correct an agent, we cannot tell a harness failure from a plan or product error, so repeats stay invisible.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep; a weekly trace-mining loop was dropped. Not yet tested. Covers the first 5 [T] executed phases.
ideas.next: Tag every correction at each close; it passes if at least one harness shape repeats.

ideas.name: Per-PR rework rate as health metric
ideas.how: Track the share of each PR's diff changed after review; under 5% [T] is the quality bar.
ideas.problem: We have no measure of whether review is converging or code keeps changing after review.
ideas.stands: Deferred in the Dex Horthy sweep. No refuter verdict, reviewers split between trial and skip, and no measurement is defined. Not tested.
ideas.next: Decide whether to send it to a refuter; defining how to measure it would bring it back.

ideas.name: Re-run CLAUDE.md probes on model change
ideas.how: At a recorded model change, run 10 [S] probes with the full CLAUDE.md on a frozen commit, old against new model, 3 [S] fresh sessions each.
ideas.problem: A new model behind the Sonnet or Opus tier may follow CLAUDE.md rules differently, and nothing would show it.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, narrowed by the refuter; runs only after the first CLAUDE.md probe set has run once. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: At the first model change, run the 10 probes with a frozen rubric, old against new.

ideas.name: Record weekly-window usage per phase
ideas.how: At phase open and close, the closing evidence line records weekly-window percent from usage data, plus subagent tokens and agents lost to a usage limit.
ideas.problem: Outside dollar figures do not fit a flat subscription where weekly limits bind, so we do not know the verifier spend share.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep, narrowed to phases 1 to 3; not yet tested. Its figure decides whether the high-effort refuter rerun runs (threshold 20% [T]).
ideas.next: Record at the next phase open.

ideas.name: Record true peak context and reversal positions
ideas.how: For 5 [T] phase sessions a Haiku extractor sums input, cache-creation and cache-read tokens per call, records the peak, and logs where reversed decisions sit.
ideas.problem: A 40% [S] context rule is untested here, and the on-screen percentage includes the autocompact buffer, so we mislocate decisions made at high context.
ideas.stands: Trial from the Dex Horthy sweep; the counting method was corrected in its 2026-11-09 addendum. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Run on the first 5 [T] phase sessions.

ideas.name: Lean-workflow reassessment
ideas.how: Nine dispositions on a proposal I pasted: keep root authority, reject dropping the documentation, treat file-size limits as triggers for review, reject an allow-list of hooks; primary sources checked.
ideas.problem: We wanted to know whether a minimal-surface setup would beat our documented workflow.
ideas.stands: Parked: no change adopted; comparison never run. Root instruction file is 28 lines, 6,709 bytes [M]; outside: context files raised cost over 20% [S].
ideas.next: Measure before trimming; one owner per rule.

ideas.name: Measurement ledger and pipeline M00-M06
ideas.how: An append-only log with hash manifests and an identity hierarchy, an optional rebuildable SQLite index, and seven build slices.
ideas.problem: We had no standing way to measure whether harness changes help; all eight exports had null tokens, effort, cost and resume time.
ideas.stands: Parked: designed in the testbed, never built. I ruled it low priority and the review rated it skip, because a month of research found no measured gain. Eight [M] exports lack tokens.
ideas.next: Log per-session wall time, usage and rework in a small append-only file, with no pipeline.

ideas.name: Judge models by corrections per conversation
ideas.how: Judge a model by loop or goal outcomes and the corrections needed per conversation, not one-shot answers.
ideas.problem: One-shot answers are a poor way to judge a model for loop-style work.
ideas.stands: Parked: skipped in the Dex Horthy sweep; my corrections are already journalled and tallied elsewhere, and land on the orchestrator, not a routing tier. Source's five-to-two figure is illustrative [I].
ideas.next: None.

ideas.name: Standing regression re-runs for briefs and models
ideas.how: Run 10-30 [S] past inputs on old and new brief 3 times each, score with deterministic checks, review only disagreements; re-run on each model release.
ideas.problem: Editing an agent brief or changing a model could silently change results, with no test to show it.
ideas.stands: Parked: not now. Inputs are live repo and web, not fixed cases; cost about 60-180 [E] agent runs per brief edit; a standing re-run would rebuild the measurement pipeline we set aside.
ideas.next: Reopen only after a recorded brief edit flipped a verdict; none is on record. Useful parts live in the effort trial.

ideas.name: Schema-retry count as a brief-quality signal
ideas.how: Log structured-output rejection counts per brief over 3 [S] runs; flag any brief above a 10% [G] retry rate.
ideas.problem: A brief that makes agents fail the output schema often may be defective, but our scripts cannot see retry counts.
ideas.stands: Parked: refuted in the BAML sweep because the program has never recorded a schema rejection; its failures are usage and session limits. The 10% [G] threshold is not yet calibrated. Not tested.
ideas.next: None.

ideas.name: Seven-metric lens for every bottleneck and idea
ideas.how: Sort each record by the metric it moves most: throughput, efficiency, token count, token cost, time taken, quality of output, hallucinations.
ideas.problem: The first compile sorted bottlenecks by where they showed up in our build, so the PC outranked what limits agentic work itself.
ideas.stands: In use from this edition: agents sorted all 606 [M] earlier records on 14 November; a blind second reading agreed on the main metric for 80 of 101 [M].
ideas.next: Give hallucinations and quality a measured rate (WP8).

ideas.name: Where the time goes: model step against disk
ideas.how: Time one file read, one repeat read, one search of the repository and one model step on this PC, and compare them.
ideas.problem: I expected fetching from disk to be the slow part, as in database design, and a cache to be the fix.
ideas.stands: Measured on 11 November: one model step took 6,600 ms (median of 10,658 steps) [M]; a 93 KB file read 0.5 ms (possibly a warm read), a repeat 0.05 ms, a search of 618 files 124 ms [M].
ideas.next: Count steps saved, not milliseconds, when judging an index or cache.
ideas.origin: Measured in a chat of 11 November

themes.title: First use, real devices and real hosts
themes.covers: Finding last-day gaps on day one: zero-seed walks, rehearsals on a real host, load drills, Android builds, the emulator and the device lab.
intro: The clinic testbed’s last-day gaps were production paths hidden behind test data, and none of it had run on a real host. The ideas here find those gaps on day one: a walk from a clean install in every gate, a rehearsal on a real host, and a rerun of the load drill.
For FixFlow the same theme means real Android builds and real devices. The lab emulator already boots on this PC with Android 14 and the lab app installed.

ideas.name: Local staging VM rig with fifteen drills
ideas.how: Script-built Hyper-V Debian VM (2 vCPU [S], 2 GB [S]), versioned releases, fifteen re-runnable drills: deploy, upgrade, backup and restore, load, security probe, reboot.
ideas.problem: We had never tested restore, deploy, upgrade or failure behaviour outside development, and had no production-like host to rehearse on.
ideas.stands: In use in the testbed, synthetic data: fresh VM serving in 109 s [M], upgrade 7 s [M], 781,505 rows restored in 14 s [M], security probe 99 pass, 0 fail [M].
ideas.next: Run the fresh-VM restore and first-deploy checklist with me present; reuse clean-install-first and restore row-checksum compare in FixFlow.

ideas.name: Volume load and page-speed drill
ideas.how: Grow synthetic data through the app's services, time persona pages, make reads set-based, count queries at two sizes, hash page bodies before and after.
ideas.problem: Pages were slow at volume, it was unknown whether 12 concurrent users worked, and an optimisation had to be proved not to change figures.
ideas.stands: Measured in the testbed: pages 9-13 s down to 0.1-0.5 s at 75,016 documents [M]; queries on one page 29,346 to 28 [M]. The 12-clerk load run was not repeated after the fix.
ideas.next: Rerun the 12-clerk drill on current main, then a bulk generator to 250,000 [T] stock movements, then the rented host.

ideas.name: Maestro on-device smoke tests with runner agent
ideas.how: Sourced Maestro skill with foreground smoke flows (carry-in, offline intake, arrival pair, drain report, read-only) for one phone; a Sonnet agent runs and reports.
ideas.problem: The app has no screen-test harness, so we never exercise carry-in and arrival flows on a real device automatically.
ideas.stands: Built in skills packages in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov; not yet run. A pass would prove only the foreground smoke, never headless delivery or field reliability.
ideas.next: Add test IDs, then run the first smoke test (P2c) on a phone; the design calls this the cheapest route.

ideas.name: EAS release skill and release operator agent
ideas.how: Skill under rulings (no expo-updates, never prebuild, SDK 52, same certificate, install over); a Sonnet agent checks preconditions and records per-phone before/after build receipts.
ideas.problem: Fleet APK builds can ship the wrong host, certificate or version, or wipe the offline queue if uninstalled, and JavaScript fixes wait in the build queue.
ideas.stands: Built in PR #185, merged on 13 Nov; not yet run. The design asked whether expo-updates should ship; the built skill rules it out. Builds and installs stay with me.
ideas.next: Use it for the next fleet build and first phone install (P2b-1, P2c).
ideas.origin: Orchestration design; Skills packages; Expo/EAS docs

ideas.name: Real-data switch and money-setup command
ideas.how: An append-only, default-off authorisation table that only the host console can switch (audited), plus a second command that creates accounts and tills.
ideas.problem: A fresh install could not take real data or create accounts and tills, which is how the clean-install gap surfaced.
ideas.stands: Built on a clinic testbed branch, unmerged and ungated: 39 files, 2,552 insertions, 71 deletions [M]; 2570 tests passed [M].
ideas.next: Run a fresh-database walk early in the next build so this kind of gap shows up on day one.

ideas.name: User-folder Android toolchain, verified on disk
ideas.how: Install into a user folder, loaded per terminal, nothing on PATH; the installer reports success only for files found on disk.
ideas.problem: The device lab and the first-use device step need a JDK, adb, apksigner, an emulator and a system image on this PC without changing system settings.
ideas.stands: Built; installed 13 November, 8.6 GB [M] on disk: JDK 17.0.21, adb 1.0.41, build-tools 37.0.0, emulator 37.2.13, Android 14 image, one virtual device [M]. WHPX reported usable [M]. One emulator DLL stays absent: the antivirus blocks it, and BLOCKED-FILES.txt lists it.
ideas.next: Reuse the recorded emulator boot (plan section 7.5) for device lab L3 and P0a item 10.
ideas.origin: Ship plan §7; My yes on 13 November

ideas.name: Drain branch cut at the pre-merge commit
ideas.how: Cut release/drain at the main commit before the first merge; add P1, P2b-2 and P3a squash commits by cherry-pick; the log shows only those.
ideas.problem: Version 8 cut the drain branch at P1's squash commit; under build-ahead, anything merged below P1 would leak into the image we ship.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a rule in ship plan section 7.7 after a refuter found it the one blocker; branch not yet cut, not yet tested. The web variant adds P12a and P12.
ideas.next: Cut the branch and verify the log shows exactly the listed commits.

ideas.name: Zero-seed first-use walk in every gate
ideas.how: Each gate runs install, first user, tills, a real-shaped import, one transaction and close of day on a fresh container database with no seeder.
ideas.problem: Gaps surfaced only on the last day: nobody walked a clean install, so the app refusing real data and missing tills stayed hidden.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 4; not built. Adds 2 to 3 minutes [E] per gate and needs phase 2. Half of this gap was closed on 11 November.
ideas.next: Build the journey on a fresh container database, then replay it on the 11 November gap after phase 2.
ideas.origin: Bottleneck compile; Harness v2 design; Clinic testbed

ideas.name: Rented-host rehearsal
ideas.how: Free steps first with me present for one administrator prompt (restore, deploy checklist, off-site push, planted alert), then one rented-host day on made-up data.
ideas.problem: So far everything we built has run only on my PC, so certificates, off-site backups, alerts and restore are unproven outside my PC.
ideas.stands: Designed in harness v2 phase 4; not run. Today there is no certificate script, no off-host backup push and no alert channel [M]. Target: a result file per checklist gap [T].
ideas.next: I decide D21 (approve a one-day rented host); first, be present for one administrator prompt to run the free steps.

ideas.name: List of what never ran on real hosts
ideas.how: A 'cannot be proven here' list: off-site store, certificates, hosted CPU speed, alerts, second-host restore, second maintainer, each tied to a closing drill.
ideas.problem: We want to stop assuming that local rehearsal proved how things behave on a real host.
ideas.stands: Designed as a list only; none of it has run on a real host. No real-host measurement exists; only desk evidence such as a hosting cost estimate read on 5 November.
ideas.next: Keep the list in the handoff and name one closing command per drill; I choose a host and pilot frame.

ideas.name: Local Android compile gate (L2)
ideas.how: Docker container with JDK 17 [S] and Android SDK copies the app in, runs prebuild there (never in the repo), builds a release.
ideas.problem: No check catches native Android compile breaks, because the JavaScript-only export misses them and an EAS build queue is slow.
ideas.stands: Designed in ship plan section 7.5; the lane is running as PR #188. Not yet tested. It will also answer whether the background-geolocation library builds on SDK 52 / RN 0.76.9.
ideas.next: Record time, size, certificate and the yes/no compile fact, aiming for compile checks in minutes rather than an EAS queue.
ideas.origin: Ship plan §7, closing a gap CLAUDE.md names

ideas.name: L3 device lab on a native emulator
ideas.how: A native emulator (Windows Hypervisor Platform) runs three scripted protocols: drain rehearsal, adb field steps, offline matrix. Lab builds cannot reach a real server.
ideas.problem: Drain logic and field-reliability steps meet a real phone with real data without any earlier rehearsal, and Docker has no /dev/kvm to run an emulator.
ideas.stands: Designed; L3a started 13 November, stacked on L2. The emulator boots on this PC with the lab app installed. No check run yet; each must be shown failing once.
ideas.next: L3a reports each tracker check as reproduced, not reproduced or inconclusive, so a field session confirms instead of explores.

ideas.name: L4 deploy-train and restore rehearsal
ideas.how: Per behaviour-changing PR: restore newest dump into Postgres 17 [S], run start.sh migrations to the new head, run its post-deploy check, log a rehearsal row.
ideas.problem: Behaviour-changing PRs deploy together at P4c, and the first run of an untried sequence would be on the restored production data.
ideas.stands: Designed in ship plan section 7.5 (wave C); not started, not yet tested. The plan's claim is that P4c then replays a sequence already tried.
ideas.next: Use a seeded database until P0a item 4 supplies the real dump.

ideas.name: Device evidence across phone brands before reliability claims
ideas.how: Any geofencing reliability claim requires device evidence across the phone brands in the fleet; an adb-based field protocol separates the top hypotheses.
ideas.problem: One phone can tell hypotheses apart but cannot validate a fix across the phone brands our fleet uses.
ideas.stands: Designed as a constraint on the phased plan; not yet tested. The field protocol itself is still to be produced, and I run it on devices.
ideas.next: Have the first investigation output the protocol, then I run it on devices.

ideas.name: Early performance and recovery proof
ideas.how: Small performance and recovery proof in early slices: p95 timing under load with optional parts off, slow or failed, plus an A/B/C form comparison.
ideas.problem: Production-readiness claims go unmeasured until the very end of a build, so we want proof early.
ideas.stands: Designed from an AI red-team review of the clinic guide; untested. Proposed gates: posting p95 under 1 s [T], list and report pages under 2 s [T], memory under 3.2 GB [T] of 4 GB [S].
ideas.next: Bring a small proof into the early slices of the next build.

themes.title: Owner-facing outputs and decisions
themes.covers: What reaches me: visual pages, decision boards, readability rules, notices and the standing rules that need my yes.
intro: I decide quickly when I can see the choice on one page. The ideas here shape what reaches me: visual pages I can read on my own screen, decision boards that show the options and what each one unblocks, and rules that keep anything reaching outside this PC behind my yes.
This document is one of them: one place where the whole team can see the ideas, the bottlenecks and the work.

ideas.name: One-page view for me beside agent packets
ideas.how: One page with a diagram, derived from the plan and refreshed at each phase close, beside small task-specific packets for agents.
ideas.problem: I cannot see program progress without reading the whole plan, and agents need small task-specific context rather than my page.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed: AGENTS.md is 10,698 bytes [M] against a 6,709-byte baseline [M], with no productivity or token saving shown. Adopted for FixFlow as OWNER-VIEW.md, not yet tested.
ideas.next: Refresh each phase close; tie routing documents to code with a hash or CI check so they cannot drift.
ideas.origin: My idea; Harness review; Clinic testbed

ideas.name: Decision cards D01 to D23 for me
ideas.how: Each of 23 cards shows options, the design's lean in bold, bottlenecks touched and my answer; only six are needed to start.
ideas.problem: I need to see exactly what I must decide, by when, and which way the design leans, without reading the whole design.
ideas.stands: In harness v2 design: D01 to D06 were answered on 11 Nov (phase 1 yes, encrypted drive, logger allowed, resume list); D07 to D23 are still open.
ideas.next: Answer D07 before the first replay.

ideas.name: Numbered decision form for me, issued at a gate
ideas.how: At gate G1 each design task gets a numbered question form; my answers become parameters, not assumptions. Tasks O-07 and O-08 wait on them.
ideas.problem: Design agents on Odoo and self-hosting cannot be right without my answers, and spending Opus before I answer is spending on a guess.
ideas.stands: In use: issued at G1 as two forms, Odoo and self-host. My answers are still pending, so the forms have not yet fed a design.
ideas.next: I answer the form; R-02 answers the plan question first.

ideas.name: W0-results.md as the single working board
ideas.how: One file holds P0a steps, my decisions with defaults, deploy train, lane board and notes. Unknowns are written 'unknown, because ...', never 0.
ideas.problem: The coordinator and I need one compiled place to see what is done, what is open and who is doing what.
ideas.stands: In use in FixFlow: on 2026-11-13 the lane board had 10 rows [M], recording 8 running lanes [M] and 2 done phases [M].
ideas.next: I fill the answers column or accept the defaults on my decisions table.

ideas.name: I delegate merges and phase starts to the coordinator
ideas.how: Coordinator squash-merges when CI is green, its binding review passed that commit, no hold applies and the predecessor is merged. Merging deploys nothing.
ideas.problem: Waiting for me to approve every merge and next-slice start would slow a parallel program and stall work while I am away.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed, without numbers; a usage limit plus the start-on-my-turn rule halted work for three days [M]. In FixFlow the coordinator has merged under it since 13 November.
ideas.next: Merge the first review-passed PR; write the authority as a standing instruction with explicit exclusions.
ideas.origin: My idea; Clinic testbed; Ship plan §7

ideas.name: I review design and plan; models check research
ideas.how: My effort goes to plan critiques, the decisions journal and OWNER-VIEW.md; Sonnet citation checks and capped Opus refuters check research output.
ideas.problem: My reading time is limited, so I spend it where a mistake costs most.
ideas.stands: Already in use. The 3x multipliers in the source are asserted, not measured.
ideas.next: Count post-merge defects traced to discovery output after the early phases.

ideas.name: Design answers in a flat file, not ask-question tool
ideas.how: Answer design questions in a file. Our PR-body journal and my critique sections already do this.
ideas.problem: Transient prompts lose design decisions and cannot point at code.
ideas.stands: Already in use: it is the harness's habit through the PR-body journal and the sections for my critique.
ideas.next: Keep using it.
ideas.origin: Dex Horthy sweep (voice into a file)

ideas.name: Archiving and progress-visibility rules
ideas.how: The root archives nothing without my word. Each slice gets a board row, and a task file holds status and next action.
ideas.problem: I rely on one large board file, and sessions pile up with no live view of their status.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed: the board is 219,111 bytes [M] at sweep time with 19 worktrees [M]; no live status mechanism was found.
ideas.next: Add an automatic expiry list and a short progress file.

ideas.name: Wrap-up called by me, carried P3 tables, pilot backlog
ideas.how: Gate tables end with 'Remainders carried' and owners. On 10 Nov I ordered wrap-up: five branches merged, the rest into a pilot backlog.
ideas.problem: We want review rounds that end, and low-severity findings kept visible without blocking the release.
ideas.stands: In use in the clinic testbed: 111 P3 findings returned in round 1 [M]; five branches merged, 7/7 checks, 2520 tests in 726 s [M], 0 skipped [M]. No stop rule written.
ideas.next: Define a stop rule up front, with never-deferred P1 classes; store findings as structured records.

ideas.name: My P0a pre-flight kit
ideas.how: Five Git Bash scripts I run in order; each has --dry-run, writes outside the repo, reads keys from the environment, never opens the app.
ideas.problem: My P0a was the critical path and nothing could reach a phone or host without it; the steps were scattered and risky.
ideas.stands: Built: self-tested on an empty stand-in database, which produced a 131 KB dump [M]. I have not run it on real data, so real items are unknown.
ideas.next: I run tools-check, then r2-archive and supabase-dump; this unlocks P3b and the Odoo decision once item 4 is done.

ideas.name: Fleet hold notice to technicians
ideas.how: A notice in English, Urdu and Roman Urdu: do not open the app, clock in, start travel, discard, update, uninstall, clear data or reset.
ideas.problem: Technicians opening the app, tapping Discard or uninstalling could destroy records that have not synced and are the only copy.
ideas.stands: Built: the notice is drafted but not yet sent. The kit's scripts only read from phones and never open the app. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: I send the notice and record the date.

ideas.name: Six interactive demos on my harness v2 page
ideas.how: Six demos on my harness v2 page: power-off, check queue, fix round, merge nobody read, where tokens went, root as only gate.
ideas.problem: I read mechanisms better by moving sliders than by reading prose.
ideas.stands: Built in my harness v2 page. Each demo explains a mechanism and lists its assumptions; none is a result.
ideas.next: None recorded.

ideas.name: My W0 pre-flight before agents spend tokens
ideas.how: A short checklist for me (fleet notice, hostname control, APK signing, service status, workshop coordinates, Docker started) runs first; its outputs decide the G1 branch.
ideas.problem: Agents cannot learn facts only I can see (dashboards, devices, billing), and spending tokens on guesses uses our limited usage on unchecked inputs.
ideas.stands: Designed in the orchestration design: a ten-item checklist of about 30 minutes [E] that runs before any agent spends tokens. Not yet tested; later carried into FixFlow's P0a kit.
ideas.next: I work through the ten W0 items.
ideas.origin: Orchestration design, added after the Opus critics

ideas.name: Six-question phase-closing message
ideas.how: At phase close the message answers six questions: goal, fit, choice, before and after, evidence including skipped counts, and remaining work.
ideas.problem: I need a consistent, short account of what each phase did and what remains.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a message format, not a file. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Use it at the close of P0a.

ideas.name: Report tokens only, lead with the mechanism
ideas.how: Answer a which-or-why spend question with the ranked mechanism and one table. Report in tokens, with no dollars and no comparison framing.
ideas.problem: A repo-comparison page and dollar figures were a tangent from what I asked.
ideas.stands: Adopted and applied: the dollar figures were removed from the token record after my feedback on 2026-11-12.
ideas.next: Keep reports to mechanism, size and levers.

ideas.name: Standing rules: ship plan first, my yes for outside actions
ideas.how: FixFlow P0a goes first. No hooks, installs, scheduled tasks, permission changes or outbound data without my decision; no harness agents during a FixFlow phase.
ideas.problem: Harness work could delay FixFlow or take shared limits without my consent.
ideas.stands: Adopted as a standing rule in the harness v2 design. No number or result attached.
ideas.next: Keep using it.

ideas.name: My one-off watch of P1
ideas.how: I watch P1 through its first code commit and log departures without interrupting; a fresh agent then audits the transcript against a fixed list.
ideas.problem: Live watching might catch costly departures earlier than a transcript audit afterward.
ideas.stands: Trial on P1 only; kept only if it catches something the audit would find late. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Compare departures caught live with those the post-close transcript audit catches.

ideas.name: Rough HTML mockup before new-screen phases
ideas.how: Sonnet produces one rough HTML mockup of the screen's states and exact copy, written into the brief; I glance at it without blocking.
ideas.problem: A copy or state mistake on a new mobile screen costs a whole new fleet APK build and is found only after implementation.
ideas.stands: Trial on four new-screen phases (P2b-1, P5b-1, P9b, P10a); not a skill or rule, and not for P12a or P12. Not yet tested.
ideas.next: Produce the mockup for P2b-1; success would mean fewer APK rebuilds.

ideas.name: Context-system line moves to its own repository
ideas.how: I decided on 1 Nov 2026 that the line continues in its own repository at low priority; until moved it stays untracked.
ideas.problem: Experimental memory tooling should stay off the product's routes and out of its history; it now sits untracked in a repository with no remote.
ideas.stands: Decided, not yet done: the move needs my folder name. Measurement research does not start unless I ask.
ideas.next: I give the target folder name so the move can happen; keep experimental harness tooling separate.

ideas.name: Hold design docs to a stricter reading standard
ideas.how: Require that a design doc is actually read before it ships.
ideas.problem: Design docs can pile up faster than anyone reads them; reading capacity, not writing, becomes the limit.
ideas.stands: Parked: my critique rounds are already the read gate, so no change was proposed. Not tested.
ideas.next: None; it would return only if critique rounds stop covering design docs.

coverNote: This reference edition holds every idea, bottleneck, package card and term in full, each sorted by the seven metrics I judge the harness by: throughput, efficiency, token count, token cost, time taken, quality of output and hallucinations. The short edition beside it, `HARNESS-IDEAS-AND-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11-14.pdf`, tells the same story in under 25 pages. Every number carries a tag that says how sure we are of it.
howMade: **How this was compiled.** I followed our orchestration design.
